papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Releasing Graph Neural Networks with Differential Privacy Guarantees
papers_seen.abstract: With the increasing popularity of graph neural networks (GNNs) in several sensitive applications like healthcare and medicine, concerns have been raised over the privacy aspects of trained GNNs. More notably, GNNs are vulnerable to privacy attacks, such as membership inference attacks, even if only black-box access to the trained model is granted. We propose PrivGNN, a privacy-preserving framework for releasing GNN models in a centralized setting. Assuming an access to a public unlabeled graph, PrivGNN provides a framework to release GNN models trained explicitly on public data along with knowledge obtained from the private data in a privacy preserving manner. PrivGNN combines the knowledge-distillation framework with the two noise mechanisms, random subsampling, and noisy labeling, to ensure rigorous privacy guarantees. We theoretically analyze our approach in the Renyi differential privacy framework. Besides, we show the solid experimental performance of our method compared to several baselines adapted for graph-structured data. Our code is available at https://github.com/iyempissy/privGnn.

papers_seen.author: Holmes
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Over the past decade KD has expanded from soft-label (logit) matching to a toolkit that includes intermediate representation and attention matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and zero-shot protocols, and integrations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD reliably reduces inference cost and enables on-device or latency-constrained deployment when its signals, data strategy, and architecture alignment are chosen to match task and deployment constraints, but it has well-documented limitations related to teacher imperfections, capacity mismatch, data scarcity, and distributional shifts.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or multi-modal deep models into smaller, more deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or other structured knowledge. Work across vision, speech, and NLP shows a range of mechanisms (soft-label matching, internal-representation matching, layer mapping, and feature/attention guidance) and adaptations for limited or private data. Empirical results indicate distilled students can approach teacher accuracy while greatly reducing size and inference cost, but effectiveness depends on what knowledge is distilled, how it is represented, and the training regime.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-level toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. Effective KD requires selecting what to transfer (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational signals), matching teacher and student capacities, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques. When applied with task-aware objectives, projector or alignment modules, and careful treatment of data and teacher preparation, KD yields compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints, though capacity mismatch and data limitations remain important caveats.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Embracing the Dark Knowledge: Domain Generalization Using Regularized Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Though convolutional neural networks are widely used in different tasks, lack of generalization capability in the absence of sufficient and representative data is one of the challenges that hinder their practical application. In this paper, we propose a simple, effective, and plug-and-play training strategy named Knowledge Distillation for Domain Generalization (KDDG) which is built upon a knowledge distillation framework with the gradient filter as a novel regularization term. We find that both the ``richer dark knowledge" from the teacher network, as well as the gradient filter we proposed, can reduce the difficulty of learning the mapping which further improves the generalization ability of the model. We also conduct experiments extensively to show that our framework can significantly improve the generalization capability of deep neural networks in different tasks including image classification, segmentation, reinforcement learning by comparing our method with existing state-of-the-art domain generalization techniques. Last but not the least, we propose to adopt two metrics to analyze our proposed method in order to better understand how our proposed method benefits the generalization capability of deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Velasquez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multifaceted Tool Beyond Simple Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be understood and applied as a flexible toolbox rather than merely a compression trick. KD enables compression, regularization, privacy-preserving transfer, and adaptation across diverse constraints (data scarcity, heterogeneous devices, federated settings). Effective practice combines soft-target supervision with representation-level alignment, architecture-aware methods (pruning, quantization, search), and privacy-aware or teacher-free variants. However, careful design is required to avoid capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, and robustness or bias degradation.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and adaptable family of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster models suitable for deployment. Beyond the classic teacher-logit supervision, modern distillation covers feature-level matching, task-adaptive architecture search, multi-teacher transfer, and data-free scenarios. KD can be combined with pruning and structured sparsity, adapted for domain shifts, and used to transfer ensemble or task-specific knowledge into compact models. The choice of distillation target, the availability of data, and the deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy, domain) determine which distillation recipe will be most effective.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large, high-capacity models (teachers) into smaller, more efficient models (students). Across vision and language, practitioners combine KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, architectural design, and quantization) and with strategies for scarce or missing data to obtain deployable models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical success depends on choices about what to transfer (soft targets, features, attention), how to align heterogeneous architectures, the role of pre-training for compact models, and mechanisms to preserve robustness and rare-token behaviors. Data-free distillation, multi-task or multi-teacher schemes, and targeted representation matching extend KD’s applicability to many real-world settings.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transform large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable ones by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural properties from teacher to student. Approaches vary from logits-based transfer to feature- or module-level imitation, multi-teacher and meta-learned schemes, data-free (zero-shot) methods, and procedures designed for robustness or computational efficiency. Across vision, speech, graph, and NLP settings (including large pretrained Transformer models), distillation has enabled substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of the original performance. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer (probabilities, features, modules), how to generate or augment data for transfer, and how to preserve or transfer robustness and task-specific inductive biases. Remaining challenges include matching teacher performance across tasks with minimal data, ensuring robustness under adversarial or distributional shift, and balancing efficiency with fidelity in large-scale pretrained language models.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques that compress large, high-performing models into smaller, more efficient students for deployment in constrained settings. KD methods span soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-representation and attention transfer, relational objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and teacher-free or data-synthesizing approaches. When combined with complementary compression practices (pre-training compact architectures, pruning, quantization, and data augmentation), KD often preserves most of a teacher’s performance while reducing latency, memory, and energy requirements. However, success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, data availability and distributional shift, and mitigation of propagated biases or robustness gaps. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, common failure modes, and practical design patterns shown to improve distillation outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: The Practical Centrality of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable tool for reducing model size and inference cost while preserving (or even improving) performance. Beyond straightforward teacher→student logit matching, KD can be applied structurally (transforming architectures without redesign), combined with quantization, used for domain adaptation of large pretrained language models, leveraged in multi-teacher and few-shot settings, and operated without access to original data. KD’s benefits arise both from transferring predictive behavior and from inducing effective regularization; when paired with careful choices (e.g., feature projectors, divergence measures, or pseudo-replay for data-free settings), KD enables deployment of compact, reliable models across vision, speech, language, graph, and generative-model domains.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Salazar
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure from teacher models. A broad toolkit has emerged—matching softened outputs, aligning feature or attention maps, adversarial and online schemes, data-centric interventions (augmentation, synthetic or data-free sampling), and architecture-aware methods (pruning, quantization, or student-aware design). Practical deployment requires selecting the right signals to transfer, addressing data limitations and domain shift, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques. While distilled models often recover much of a teacher's accuracy with substantial efficiency gains, open problems remain in robustness, fairness, privacy, and principled teacher–student alignment.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Distilling Policy Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The transfer of knowledge from one policy to another is an important tool in Deep Reinforcement Learning. This process, referred to as distillation, has been used to great success, for example, by enhancing the optimisation of agents, leading to stronger performance faster, on harder domains [26, 32, 5, 8]. Despite the widespread use and conceptual simplicity of distillation, many different formulations are used in practice, and the subtle variations between them can often drastically change the performance and the resulting objective that is being optimised. In this work, we rigorously explore the entire landscape of policy distillation, comparing the motivations and strengths of each variant through theoretical and empirical analysis. Our results point to three distillation techniques, that are preferred depending on specifics of the task. Specifically a newly proposed expected entropy regularised distillation allows for quicker learning in a wide range of situations, while still guaranteeing convergence.

papers_seen.author: May
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Paradigm for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a compression trick: when treated as a broad training paradigm it enables compact, robust, and deployable models across modalities and tasks. By integrating logit-level guidance, intermediate feature transfer, architecture-aware projectors, adaptive teacher selection, data- and domain-aware strategies, and robustness-aware objectives, KD pipelines can produce students that approach teacher performance while satisfying latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical success requires designing what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous components, and how to shape inputs and curricula for the student—rather than relying on a single generic distillation recipe.

papers_seen.author: Galloway
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Tool for Compression, Adaptation, and Robust Deployment in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for transferring capabilities from large or multi-modal models into smaller, faster, or modality-limited models. When combined with complementary strategies—domain adaptation, feature-level matching, data augmentation, and meta-learning—distillation enables practical deployment across constrained devices, heterogeneous federated systems, and domain-shifted settings. However, KD is not a panacea: optimization subtleties and mismatches between teacher and student require methodological care and, in some cases, alternative regularization strategies.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Dependent Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while often preserving much of the teacher's effectiveness. KD methods range from matching soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations or using adversarial generators when training data are unavailable; they have been successfully applied across vision, generative modeling, recommender systems, and large pretrained language models. However, KD’s success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to address limited or private data, robustness, and bias—so practitioners must pair KD with task-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives to get reliable, deployable results.

papers_seen.author: Dean
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behaviors and internal signals. A broad family of KD methods—logit/soft-target matching, intermediate-representation alignment, multi-teacher aggregation, and data- or task-aware variants—has been applied across vision and language tasks. Practical deployment typically combines KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and requires attention to data availability, teacher–student alignment, and robustness or fairness concerns. Open challenges include principled handling of teacher errors, data-free distillation, and reliable transfer of robustness and fairness properties.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: TextKD-GAN: Text Generation using KnowledgeDistillation and Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Text generation is of particular interest in many NLP applications such as machine translation, language modeling, and text summarization. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) achieved a remarkable success in high quality image generation in computer vision,and recently, GANs have gained lots of interest from the NLP community as well. However, achieving similar success in NLP would be more challenging due to the discrete nature of text. In this work, we introduce a method using knowledge distillation to effectively exploit GAN setup for text generation. We demonstrate how autoencoders (AEs) can be used for providing a continuous representation of sentences, which is a smooth representation that assign non-zero probabilities to more than one word. We distill this representation to train the generator to synthesize similar smooth representations. We perform a number of experiments to validate our idea using different datasets and show that our proposed approach yields better performance in terms of the BLEU score and Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) measure compared to traditional GAN-based text generation approaches without pre-training.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Compression and Robustness in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, multifaceted technique for compressing large models while often preserving — and sometimes improving — task performance. KD can transfer ensemble behaviour, provide regularization benefits, enable deployment under privacy or communication constraints, and be adapted to domain-specific and generation tasks. Practical KD implementations leverage ensembles, feature-level projectors, data augmentation, self-distillation, or data-free/federated protocols depending on resource and data availability. This paper argues that KD should be treated not only as a compression trick but as a general-purpose training paradigm with distinct theoretical and practical consequences for representation quality, robustness, and deployability.

papers_seen.author: Horton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: A Central, Practical Tool with Clear Limits and Best-Practice Remedies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and NLP. When applied thoughtfully—choosing what knowledge to transfer, preparing or pretraining students, and combining KD with complementary compression primitives—distillation often yields compact models that recover much of teacher performance while meeting latency and memory constraints. However, KD is not a universal solution: optimization difficulties, teacher–student capacity mismatch, limited or mismatched data, privacy constraints, and the risk of transferring undesirable behaviors (biases, adversarial weaknesses) remain important concerns. A pragmatic approach treats KD as a flexible toolkit to be combined with targeted architectural, data, and objective choices that address these failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.author: Chapman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly used technique to transfer information from larger or more complex models to smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained models. It serves both model compression and training-stabilization roles across vision, speech, and language tasks. KD variants include offline teacher-student distillation, online/co-distillation among peers, feature- and representation-level matching, and hybrid schemes that combine distillation with quantization or specialized training objectives. Empirical evidence shows KD can improve accuracy, generalization, robustness, and inference efficiency, but its success depends on data complexity, teacher design, and the type of knowledge transferred.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation unifies multiple strategies for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable models while preserving performance. It supports a range of goals — parameter and latency reduction, robustness, interpretability, and privacy-aware deployment — by transferring information from a teacher to a student via soft outputs, intermediate representations, or structural/architectural guidance. Practical and research advances show that combining distillation modes (feature-level, output-level, progressive module replacement), data augmentation, and adaptive teacher training yields compact models that approach teacher performance even under limited data, heterogeneous devices, or privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical, Task-Aware, and Privacy-Conscious Agenda
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical suite of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster models suitable for deployment across modalities and tasks. Effective KD goes beyond naive logits matching: task-aware layer-wise alignment, progressive module replacement, multi-teacher schedules, and architecture-aware search can preserve accuracy while reducing compute and memory. Moreover, self-distillation and teacher-free variants reduce dependence on strong teachers, and specialized KD variants address scarce data, privacy, and federated constraints. These directions together form a roadmap for applying KD in real-world deep learning and NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Pham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical set of techniques to transfer predictive and representational knowledge from large, expensive teacher models to smaller, faster student models. Across computer vision, generative modeling, retrieval, and natural language processing, practitioners use KD to reduce inference cost, enable on-device deployment, and adapt models to new domains or privacy constraints. KD methods vary in what is transferred (soft targets, intermediate features, attention maps), how teacher and student are aligned (layer mapping, attention-weighted projection, task-aware filters), and whether original training data are available (data-free and zero-shot approaches). Success depends on careful choices of teacher preparation, student capacity and architecture, signal selection, and data or synthetic-sample strategies; when designed appropriately, KD combined with complementary compression (pruning, architecture transforms) yields compact models with strong empirical performance, while important limitations remain (representation mismatch, propagation of teacher biases, low-frequency token coverage).

papers_seen.author: Contreras
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of task performance. The field encompasses softened-logit transfer, intermediate feature and layer matching, online and multi-teacher schemes, data-free or data-limited techniques, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware surgery. Empirical work shows KD often improves deployment trade-offs in vision, speech, and language tasks, but its reliability depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, the availability and nature of distillation data, and interventions to mitigate optimization, robustness, and fairness issues. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a composable toolkit—selecting objectives, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives to match task and deployment constraints—and continue to explore theory and methods that address capacity mismatch, domain shift, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Moran
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a core technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient students suitable for deployment. Across modalities and tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in memory, compute, and latency while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Success depends on choosing appropriate distillation strategies that account for model structure, task specificity, data availability, and training dynamics. When tailored—via structural transformations, progressive module replacement, task-aware layer alignment, or data-centric augmentations—distillation consistently produces compact models that approach teacher accuracy and enable real-world use cases that would otherwise be impractical.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Toolchain for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and empirically effective paradigm for producing compact, resource-efficient models from larger teachers across computer vision, language, graph, and speech tasks. As a modular system, KD supports multiple information-transfer signals (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational structure), can operate with or without original training data, and composes naturally with complementary compression methods (quantization, pruning, and architecture search). Real-world deployment requires careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle limited or no access to teacher data, and how to address robustness and fairness concerns. When KD is applied as a deliberate toolchain—selecting task-aware objectives, incorporating multi-teacher or synthetic-data protocols, and combining with data- and model-level compression—practical students can approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Open problems remain around preserving rare-event behaviors, domain shift, and student-aware teacher shaping, which motivate focused research on curricula, data synthesis, and representation-aware objectives.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression strategies enable deployment of large pretrained models by transferring function or representation from larger (teacher) models to smaller (student) ones. Across supervised, self-supervised, and data-free settings, KD methods exploit soft targets, intermediate representation matching, architectural surgery, and data or training-time modifications to improve student accuracy, robustness, or efficiency. Empirical results show that appropriately designed distillation can retain most teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in model size, precision, or inference cost; but effectiveness depends on choices of targets, data, and teacher-student compatibility. Open challenges include preserving rare-token behavior in distilled NLP models, mitigating bias transfer, and jointly optimizing hardware constraints and task performance.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer via Adversarial Belief Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Performing knowledge transfer from a large teacher network to a smaller student is a popular task in modern deep learning applications. However, due to growing dataset sizes and stricter privacy regulations, it is increasingly common not to have access to the data that was used to train the teacher. We propose a novel method which trains a student to match the predictions of its teacher without using any data or metadata. We achieve this by training an adversarial generator to search for images on which the student poorly matches the teacher, and then using them to train the student. Our resulting student closely approximates its teacher for simple datasets like SVHN, and on CIFAR10 we improve on the state-of-the-art for few-shot distillation (with 100 images per class), despite using no data. Finally, we also propose a metric to quantify the degree of belief matching between teacher and student in the vicinity of decision boundaries, and observe a significantly higher match between our zero-shot student and the teacher, than between a student distilled with real data and the teacher. Code available at: https://github.com/polo5/ZeroShotKnowledgeTransfer

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Variants, and Practical Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring aspects of the teacher’s predictive behavior and internal representations. A diverse set of methods—matching output distributions, aligning intermediate features, progressive module replacement, multi-teacher and data-free schemes, and task- or domain-aware adaptations—has been developed to address deployment constraints such as latency, memory, data availability, privacy, and multimodal inputs. Empirical work shows that when the distillation recipe is matched to model architectures, data conditions, and deployment constraints, students can retain much of the teacher’s performance while offering practical efficiency gains; however, trade-offs and open challenges remain around robustness, domain shift, and faithful transfer of rare or fine-grained behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Dominguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical toolkit for compressing deep models for real-world deployment. KD unifies multiple signals (soft targets, intermediate representations, relational/attention matching) and interoperates naturally with complementary techniques (architecture search, pruning, quantization, and data synthesis). Properly designed KD pipelines—choosing what to transfer, mapping teacher and student representations, and addressing data or privacy constraints—yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance across classification, generation, detection, and language tasks. At the same time, KD has limits (capacity mismatch, optimization and data mismatch, and potential propagation of teacher biases), so production pipelines must combine KD with pretraining, data strategies, and robustness/fairness checks to be reliable.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile set of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students while preserving much of the teacher performance. KD spans simple logit-based supervision to richer representation-, relation-, and adversarial-level transfers and is used to enable on-device inference, multi-task models, domain specialization, privacy-aware releases, and data-limited deployments. Best outcomes arise when KD is combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), task-aware design, careful sample or synthetic-data strategies, and interventions for bias and privacy. KD has clear empirical benefits across modalities but also well-documented limits—sensitivity to data availability and heterogeneity, potential propagation of teacher errors or biases, and the need for architectural and optimization care—motivating principled adaptations and further study.

papers_seen.author: Snyder
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Insufficient Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely adopted framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. It can transfer final outputs, intermediate representations, structured relational signals, or ensemble knowledge, and supports data-side strategies including data-free and augmentation-aware schemes. In practice, KD reliably reduces inference cost and memory while preserving much of teacher performance when its formulation is matched to task constraints, data availability, and student capacity. However, distillation alone does not guarantee robust, fair, or privacy-preserving compression: practitioner success hinges on selecting appropriate distillation signals, addressing teacher–student and data mismatches, and combining KD with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet deployment goals.

papers_seen.author: Russell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Insights, and Practical Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior or internal structure. A broad family of distillation objectives—ranging from soft-label (logit) matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, layer-wise supervision, multi-teacher schedules, and integration with architecture search or data augmentation—enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Empirical successes span classification, object detection, machine translation, and language-model compression, but practical deployment requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to curate or synthesize distillation data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression techniques. The method’s effectiveness arises partly from the regularizing properties of soft targets and richer teacher signals, yet distillation can propagate teacher errors and struggle with capacity, data heterogeneity, and robustness unless augmented by task-aware design or additional engineering.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a core strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster ones while trying to retain their performance. Approaches vary from matching teacher output distributions to transferring internal representations or structured feature information, and from single-stage offline distillation to online and multi-teacher schemes. Empirical work across natural language, speech, vision and multimodal tasks shows that careful design—such as aligning intermediate features, adapting teachers to be student-friendly, using task- and domain-aware distillation, and leveraging online or instance-aware teacher weighting—can substantially reduce model size and latency with small performance loss. Still, distillation can introduce task-specific failure modes (e.g., degraded rare-word behavior or overfitting to teacher feature statistics), and practical deployment requires addressing teacher–student heterogeneity, data availability, and scalability.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Peters
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central tool for compressing large neural networks so they can run efficiently in production and on resource-constrained devices. Recent work shows KD can preserve much of the teacher performance while reducing inference cost, and that a range of complementary techniques—data augmentation, multi-teacher schedules, internal representation matching, layer alignment, meta-learning of teachers, and robustness-aware objectives—meaningfully improve student quality or transfer desirable properties. At the same time, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on optimization, the choice of teacher/student architectures, and the distributional complexity of the training data. I argue that best practice for KD in deep learning and NLP is to treat it as a family of methods to be combined—augmenting data, distilling intermediate representations, leveraging multiple or adaptive teachers, and explicitly distilling robustness—rather than as a single fixed recipe.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques reduce large, high-performing neural models to smaller, more efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or structural relationships. Methods vary from matching softened teacher outputs to aligning intermediate features, using multi-teacher ensembles, training students with surrogate or synthesized data when originals are unavailable, and combining distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to map or align heterogeneous architectures, whether and how the student is pre-trained, and which data or augmentation strategies are used. While KD can recover much of a teacher's performance and enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, open issues remain around robustness, distributional shifts, teacher imperfections, and principled optimization theory.

papers_seen.author: Henson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Multifaceted Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a single training trick but a central, practical framework for compressing large models into deployable students. When treated as a toolbox—combining soft-label transfer, representation-level alignment, data augmentation or synthesis, and integration with other compression methods—KD enables substantial reductions in memory and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. However, realizing those gains requires deliberate design: choosing which teacher signals to transfer, addressing optimization and capacity mismatches, and using data-aware or data-free strategies when original training data are unavailable. I argue that KD should be the core component of any production-focused compression pipeline, paired with representation-level objectives and careful data strategies to mitigate known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Compression and Robustness in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, multifaceted technique for compressing large models while often preserving — and sometimes improving — task performance. KD can transfer ensemble behaviour, provide regularization benefits, enable deployment under privacy or communication constraints, and be adapted to domain-specific and generation tasks. Practical KD implementations leverage ensembles, feature-level projectors, data augmentation, self-distillation, or data-free/federated protocols depending on resource and data availability. This paper argues that KD should be treated not only as a compression trick but as a general-purpose training paradigm with distinct theoretical and practical consequences for representation quality, robustness, and deployability.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing deep models and transferring capabilities across architectures and modalities. KD has enabled large speedups and model-size reductions while preserving or even improving downstream task performance when carefully applied. However, distillation is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on data availability, teacher–student alignment, and distributional heterogeneity, and it can transmit teacher biases or errors. Combining logit-based supervision with feature- and relation-focused objectives, aligning intermediate representations, and adapting distillation strategies to task and data constraints yields the best trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Component of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible approach for producing compact models from large teachers. When treated as a modular, task-aware system—combining soft-target supervision, intermediate representation matching, data and augmentation strategies, and complementary compression primitives—KD enables substantial reductions in latency and footprint while retaining most of the original performance. However, KD is not a panacea: its practical success requires careful attention to teacher–student alignment, data availability (including data-free or privacy-aware regimes), robustness to distribution shift and rare behaviors, and mitigation of transferred biases. I argue KD should be the default central tool in compression pipelines but used deliberately and in combination with other methods to meet deployment constraints and reliability requirements.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible, practical toolkit for producing compact, deployable deep models across vision and natural language tasks. KD encompasses matching teacher outputs, aligning internal representations, leveraging multi-teacher or online schedules, and using data-side strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free generation). When combined with architecture-aware design and complementary compression methods, KD often yields students that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Remaining challenges center on teacher–student mismatch, data availability, robustness, and the potential transfer of undesirable biases.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and a Prescription
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible tool for compressing large models into efficient students suitable for deployment. When combined with careful pre-training of compact architectures, representation-level supervision, and complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, distillation has important failure modes—capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity, and optimization difficulties—that require task-aware design choices around what to transfer, which teacher(s) to use, and how to prepare distillation data. A pragmatic pipeline that pre-trains compact models, distills both outputs and intermediate representations, and selectively combines KD with other compression steps yields the best trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy in practice.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Adaptation: Teaching to Adapt
papers_seen.abstract: Domain adaptation is crucial in many real-world applications where the distribution of the training data differs from the distribution of the test data. Previous Deep Learning-based approaches to domain adaptation need to be trained jointly on source and target domain data and are therefore unappealing in scenarios where models need to be adapted to a large number of domains or where a domain is evolving, e.g. spam detection where attackers continuously change their tactics.   To fill this gap, we propose Knowledge Adaptation, an extension of Knowledge Distillation (Bucilua et al., 2006; Hinton et al., 2015) to the domain adaptation scenario. We show how a student model achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised domain adaptation from multiple sources on a standard sentiment analysis benchmark by taking into account the domain-specific expertise of multiple teachers and the similarities between their domains.   When learning from a single teacher, using domain similarity to gauge trustworthiness is inadequate. To this end, we propose a simple metric that correlates well with the teacher's accuracy in the target domain. We demonstrate that incorporating high-confidence examples selected by this metric enables the student model to achieve state-of-the-art performance in the single-source scenario.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Knowledge Distillation in NLP: Pre-training, Task-Awareness, Privacy, and Robustness
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large language models into smaller, faster students for NLP applications. Its effectiveness depends not only on the student-teacher framework but on complementary practices: pre-training compact models, aligning distilled signals to task-relevant representations, handling limited or private data, leveraging multiple teachers when available, and explicitly distilling for robustness. When these elements are combined and tuned, distillation yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints.
