papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, pragmatic technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. KD operates at multiple levels—soft outputs, intermediate representations, and structured relational signals—and is effective across modalities when paired with complementary compression methods, careful data strategies, and student-aware architecture design. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its success depends on aligning teacher and student capacity, selecting appropriate distillation targets, preparing or synthesizing suitable training data, and validating robustness and fairness. A production-ready compression pipeline treats KD as a system of interacting components (signal selection, data, initialization, and optimization) and couples distillation with architecture-aware transforms, pruning, or quantization to meet real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression strategies enable deployment of large pretrained models by transferring function or representation from larger (teacher) models to smaller (student) ones. Across supervised, self-supervised, and data-free settings, KD methods exploit soft targets, intermediate representation matching, architectural surgery, and data or training-time modifications to improve student accuracy, robustness, or efficiency. Empirical results show that appropriately designed distillation can retain most teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in model size, precision, or inference cost; but effectiveness depends on choices of targets, data, and teacher-student compatibility. Open challenges include preserving rare-token behavior in distilled NLP models, mitigating bias transfer, and jointly optimizing hardware constraints and task performance.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. The literature has expanded beyond soft-label matching to include intermediate representation imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, multi- and adaptive-teacher schemes, data- and domain-aware protocols, and combinations with pruning or architecture search. Empirical work shows KD can preserve a large fraction of teacher performance across vision and language tasks, while theoretical and empirical analyses clarify when distillation helps, how teacher quality and data regimes affect outcomes, and what practical trade-offs remain. Open problems center on robustness to domain shift and adversaries, distillation without original data, and automated, architecture-agnostic pipelines for production systems.

papers_seen.author: Riley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques have become central for deploying high-performing deep models under resource constraints. Methods range from transferring soft-output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, many-to-many layer mappings, and task- or domain-adaptive compression of large pretrained language models. Advances address practical concerns such as absence of original data, low-precision inference, cross-modal transfer, and faster training-time distillation workflows. Empirical work demonstrates that representation-level supervision and flexible layer alignment often outperform pure logit-based approaches, while theoretical analyses connect KD to regularization schemes like label smoothing and quantify when teacher signals are most beneficial. Remaining challenges include preserving rare-token behaviors, handling domain shift, and balancing privacy, compute, and accuracy in on-device scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, Practical Benefits and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a simple teacher–student logit-matching trick into a broad, practical toolkit for compressing large models and adapting their knowledge to resource- and data-constrained settings. Effective distillation operates at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational signals), interacts strongly with data and augmentation choices, and is most useful when combined with complementary compression methods and careful teacher–student design. While KD often yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance, its success depends on dealing with data availability, domain shift, teacher quality, and optimization dynamics—areas that remain active research directions.

papers_seen.author: Gates
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practically effective approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across modalities. KD encompasses transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, and relational structure; it can be combined with architectural compression (pruning, quantization, parameter sharing) and with data strategies (augmentation, synthetic generation, data‑free rehearsal) to meet deployment constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey remedy: optimization challenges, teacher–student mismatches, data or domain shift, and risk of propagating teacher errors require task‑aware design, complementary compression methods, and careful validation. When applied as a principled toolkit — choosing what to transfer, how to align representations, how to prepare or synthesize data, and how to integrate pruning/quantization — KD yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance while satisfying latency, memory, and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core practical approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students while retaining much of the original performance. Multiple distillation mechanisms—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, adversarial/ensemble-based transfer, and data-free or selective-sample techniques—allow KD to address constraints such as limited data, heterogeneous deployment, low-precision hardware, and domain shift. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often acts both as a transfer of representational structure and as a regularizer; its success depends on choices about what is transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, how training data (real or synthetic) are used, and which complementary compression methods are applied. Remaining practical challenges include distributional mismatch, heterogeneity of architectures and devices, and principled teacher selection and optimization strategies.

papers_seen.author: Castaneda
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: An Integrated, Task-Aware Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical engine of model compression for deep learning and NLP when it is applied as an integrated, task-aware system. By combining soft-target transfer with representation-level alignment, targeted feature mimicking, data strategies (including synthesis when data are unavailable), and architecture-aware student design, practitioners can produce compact models that preserve much of the teacher’s utility while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD’s benefits are conditional: student capacity, data availability and complexity, architecture mismatch, and teacher artifacts limit outcomes unless addressed through deliberate pipeline choices and evaluation. This paper argues for a pragmatic KD-centered workflow and highlights key components and cautionary considerations for reliable compression in real-world settings.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Multi-Label Image Classification via Knowledge Distillation from Weakly-Supervised Detection
papers_seen.abstract: Multi-label image classification is a fundamental but challenging task towards general visual understanding. Existing methods found the region-level cues (e.g., features from RoIs) can facilitate multi-label classification. Nevertheless, such methods usually require laborious object-level annotations (i.e., object labels and bounding boxes) for effective learning of the object-level visual features. In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient deep framework to boost multi-label classification by distilling knowledge from weakly-supervised detection task without bounding box annotations. Specifically, given the image-level annotations, (1) we first develop a weakly-supervised detection (WSD) model, and then (2) construct an end-to-end multi-label image classification framework augmented by a knowledge distillation module that guides the classification model by the WSD model according to the class-level predictions for the whole image and the object-level visual features for object RoIs. The WSD model is the teacher model and the classification model is the student model. After this cross-task knowledge distillation, the performance of the classification model is significantly improved and the efficiency is maintained since the WSD model can be safely discarded in the test phase. Extensive experiments on two large-scale datasets (MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE) show that our framework achieves superior performances over the state-of-the-art methods on both performance and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and widely applicable paradigm for compressing large models and transferring knowledge across architectures, tasks, and deployment constraints. A range of KD variants—data-free, federated, multi-teacher, meta-learned teachers, intermediate-feature transfer, and architecture-aware compression—have been developed to address realistic constraints such as data privacy, limited communication, teacher imperfection, and task-specific efficiency. By matching the KD strategy to the deployment constraint (e.g., privacy, compute budget, domain shift, or paucity of data) practitioners can obtain compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency and resource requirements.

papers_seen.author: Benson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Multi-Ingredient Toolbox for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated as a configurable system rather than a single recipe. By choosing which teacher signals to transfer (logits, features, relations), aligning teacher and student architectures, and applying task- and data-aware strategies (including multi-teacher aggregation, adversarial or data-free synthesis, and architecture search), practitioners can produce compact models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. KD delivers practical gains across vision and NLP but requires careful design to avoid propagating teacher errors, mismatching capacities, or degrading robustness and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Flexible Toolkit for Reliable Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood as a composable toolkit rather than a single recipe: by transferring teacher signals at multiple levels, combining input-side strategies, and integrating complementary compression methods, KD enables compact models that meet practical deployment constraints. Effective distillation requires attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability and augmentation, and task-aware choices about what to transfer. When deployed with these design principles, KD substantially narrows the performance gap between large teachers and efficient students while remaining adaptable to privacy, federated, and heterogeneous-device settings.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Task-Aware Remedies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, flexible suite of techniques for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while often retaining most task performance. Empirical work demonstrates KD’s effectiveness across modalities and tasks, but also reveals systematic limitations arising from teacher-student capacity mismatch, optimization difficulties, data heterogeneity, and the sample-wise effects of soft targets. To make distillation reliably useful in production and research, practitioners should pair KD with task-aware layer selection, representation-level supervision, careful sample weighting, and complementary compression methods such as pruning or quantization. This balanced approach preserves KD’s deployment advantages while mitigating its failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Waller
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across computer vision, speech, multimodal, and NLP tasks, distillation protocols—ranging from soft-target (logit) matching to intermediate feature and attention-based transfers—enable practical trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and memory. Success depends on careful choices of distillation targets, teacher-student compatibility, data availability, and training dynamics; when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, low-precision, architecture search, or federated protocols) it yields deployable models for resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Powerful, Flexible — but Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods have matured into a practical toolkit for producing smaller, faster models while retaining much of the performance of larger teachers. These techniques have been applied across domains (vision, speech, NLP, healthcare), settings (offline compression, federated learning, continual adaptation), and architectures (ensembles, transformers, detectors, GANs). However, their success depends on factors such as the availability and nature of data used for distillation, domain mismatch between teacher and student, robustness and privacy requirements, and optimization dynamics. KD can unlock high-performing compact models when combined with task-aware design choices (e.g., feature imitation, augmentations, architecture search, or ensemble teachers), but practitioners must account for trade-offs and failure modes to use it effectively.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: MixKD: Towards Efficient Distillation of Large-scale Language Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale language models have recently demonstrated impressive empirical performance. Nevertheless, the improved results are attained at the price of bigger models, more power consumption, and slower inference, which hinder their applicability to low-resource (both memory and computation) platforms. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been demonstrated as an effective framework for compressing such big models. However, large-scale neural network systems are prone to memorize training instances, and thus tend to make inconsistent predictions when the data distribution is altered slightly. Moreover, the student model has few opportunities to request useful information from the teacher model when there is limited task-specific data available. To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.author: Stevens
papers_seen.title: The Central, Practical, and Conditional Role of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible set of techniques for transferring useful behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can meet deployment constraints while retaining much of the teacher’s utility. KD methods span soft-target matching, intermediate representation and layer-wise alignment, ensemble-to-single transfers, task-adaptive architecture search, and data-free or privacy-conscious pipelines. Empirical work shows KD can produce compact models that approach teacher performance across NLP, speech, and vision tasks, and that combining KD with architecture-aware compression or augmentation strategies often yields the best trade-offs. However, KD has limits: student capacity, the availability and quality of distilled data, and inherited teacher biases can all constrain outcomes. Responsible and effective compression therefore requires selecting the appropriate distillation signals, considering task and deployment constraints, and combining KD with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, or fairness-aware objectives).

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: TextKD-GAN: Text Generation using KnowledgeDistillation and Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Text generation is of particular interest in many NLP applications such as machine translation, language modeling, and text summarization. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) achieved a remarkable success in high quality image generation in computer vision,and recently, GANs have gained lots of interest from the NLP community as well. However, achieving similar success in NLP would be more challenging due to the discrete nature of text. In this work, we introduce a method using knowledge distillation to effectively exploit GAN setup for text generation. We demonstrate how autoencoders (AEs) can be used for providing a continuous representation of sentences, which is a smooth representation that assign non-zero probabilities to more than one word. We distill this representation to train the generator to synthesize similar smooth representations. We perform a number of experiments to validate our idea using different datasets and show that our proposed approach yields better performance in terms of the BLEU score and Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) measure compared to traditional GAN-based text generation approaches without pre-training.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Cornerstone of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic for transferring soft targets into a unifying toolkit that enables model compression, deployment on constrained devices, privacy-aware release, and modality transfer. By combining architectural mapping, contrastive and adversarial objectives, and data-free or federated setups, KD can preserve much of a teacher model's performance while drastically reducing footprint and computation. This makes KD essential for translating state-of-the-art large models into real-world, resource-limited, and privacy-sensitive applications.

papers_seen.author: Horton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: A Central, Practical Tool with Clear Limits and Best-Practice Remedies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and NLP. When applied thoughtfully—choosing what knowledge to transfer, preparing or pretraining students, and combining KD with complementary compression primitives—distillation often yields compact models that recover much of teacher performance while meeting latency and memory constraints. However, KD is not a universal solution: optimization difficulties, teacher–student capacity mismatch, limited or mismatched data, privacy constraints, and the risk of transferring undesirable behaviors (biases, adversarial weaknesses) remain important concerns. A pragmatic approach treats KD as a flexible toolkit to be combined with targeted architectural, data, and objective choices that address these failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a versatile suite of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Modern KD extends beyond soft-label matching to include representation- and relation-level objectives, multi- and self-distillation, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical deployment of distilled models depends on matching the distillation recipe to task constraints (data availability, teacher–student capacity, architecture heterogeneity, and privacy or communication limits) and frequently benefits from multi-stage or task-aware distillation schedules. While KD often yields compact models that approach teacher performance, open issues remain around capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher biases or errors, robustness under distribution shift, and reliable methods for distillation without original training data.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in NLP and Deep Learning: Necessity, Challenges, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models and transferring desirable properties (accuracy, robustness, or representations) into smaller, deployable students. In NLP and related deep-learning domains, distillation enables the efficient use of pretrained teachers, supports domain adaptation and continual learning, and can be adapted for supervised, self-supervised, and adversarial objectives. However, naive distillation can degrade specific behaviors (e.g., lexical choices or uncertainty calibration) unless the distillation pipeline addresses alignment of inputs and representations, intermediate-layer supervision, the sample-wise effects of soft labels, and robustness transfer. I argue that distillation should be treated as a design problem—choosing which knowledge to transfer, how to align teacher and student representations, and when to expose students to raw or adversarial signals—to yield compact models that preserve both accuracy and desirable inductive properties.

papers_seen.author: Mcdonald
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-ingredient approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, and other modalities. KD operates by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher to student, and is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods, data and augmentation strategies, and careful teacher–student design. While KD can preserve a large fraction of teacher performance and enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, its success depends on handling data availability, architecture and capacity mismatches, teacher artifacts, and distribution shifts. Treating KD as a configurable system—selecting what to transfer, how to align signals, and which auxiliary techniques to apply—yields the best practical trade-offs between compactness and task performance.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression strategies have become central for deploying high-performing deep models under resource, latency, and privacy constraints. Research has developed a spectrum of techniques — from soft-target supervision and intermediate-layer transfer to multi-teacher, data-free, and federated variants — and combined distillation with pruning and architecture search to compress large transformers and other architectures. Empirical and theoretical work highlights both practical gains (speed, memory, privacy) and fundamental tradeoffs (bias–variance, data heterogeneity, and information loss), pointing to hybrid protocols and adaptive selection of distillation signals as promising directions.

papers_seen.author: Stein
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students in vision, speech, and natural language processing. Work has expanded beyond the original teacher→student soft-label matching to include intermediate-representation imitation, multi-teacher and adaptive-teacher schedules, self- and teacher-free variants, and data-aware protocols (including data-free and privacy-preserving approaches). Empirical and theoretical analyses show KD can preserve much of teacher performance while substantially lowering latency, memory, and sometimes communication cost; success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, handling data heterogeneity, and combining KD with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Remaining challenges include robustness to domain shift and adversaries, preserving rare-token or long-tail behaviors, automating signal and teacher selection, and reliable operation without original training data.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable deploying large pretrained models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations from high-capacity teachers to smaller students. Methods include transferring softened output distributions, matching intermediate features or attention maps, layer- and task-aware alignment, online and mutual distillation, and data-free approaches that synthesize surrogate inputs. Empirical evidence across vision and language tasks shows that well-designed distillation can preserve most teacher performance while substantially reducing model size, latency, and energy use. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to map heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or private data. Remaining challenges center on preserving low-frequency or rare-token behavior in sequence models, avoiding transfer of biases or adversarial vulnerabilities, and jointly optimizing compression for hardware and task constraints.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Current Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely used set of techniques for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models to compact students. Across vision, language, speech, multimodal, and graph domains, KD has been adapted into many variants — matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, progressive module replacement, online/multi-teacher training, and data-free or privacy-aware pipelines — often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows distilled students can recover much of teacher performance when distillation targets, student preparation, and data strategies are chosen carefully. At the same time, KD’s effectiveness is limited by teacher quality, data availability or privacy, teacher–student architectural mismatch, and risks of transferring undesirable teacher behaviors. Practical deployment benefits from combining KD with complementary compression and data strategies, designing student-aware teacher signals, and accounting for robustness and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Flexible Toolkit for Reliable Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood as a composable toolkit rather than a single recipe: by transferring teacher signals at multiple levels, combining input-side strategies, and integrating complementary compression methods, KD enables compact models that meet practical deployment constraints. Effective distillation requires attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability and augmentation, and task-aware choices about what to transfer. When deployed with these design principles, KD substantially narrows the performance gap between large teachers and efficient students while remaining adaptable to privacy, federated, and heterogeneous-device settings.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, but Nuanced Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically proven approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones while preserving much of their performance. KD can operate at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate features, relational structure) and be combined with complementary compression techniques, data synthesis, or student-aware teacher training to meet deployment constraints in vision, language, and graph domains. However, its success depends on careful design choices — what to transfer, how to map teacher and student layers, how to handle limited or private data, and whether to adapt the teacher — and practitioners should treat KD as part of a broader compression toolkit rather than a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Peters
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central tool for compressing large neural networks so they can run efficiently in production and on resource-constrained devices. Recent work shows KD can preserve much of the teacher performance while reducing inference cost, and that a range of complementary techniques—data augmentation, multi-teacher schedules, internal representation matching, layer alignment, meta-learning of teachers, and robustness-aware objectives—meaningfully improve student quality or transfer desirable properties. At the same time, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on optimization, the choice of teacher/student architectures, and the distributional complexity of the training data. I argue that best practice for KD in deep learning and NLP is to treat it as a family of methods to be combined—augmenting data, distilling intermediate representations, leveraging multiple or adaptive teachers, and explicitly distilling robustness—rather than as a single fixed recipe.

papers_seen.author: Carrillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Design-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a flexible toolbox—combining softened-output supervision with representation-level alignment, teacher design, and complementary compression techniques—KD reliably reduces model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. At the same time, KD is not automatic: its success depends on what is distilled, student capacity, data availability, and targeted interventions to address robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation unifies multiple strategies for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable models while preserving performance. It supports a range of goals — parameter and latency reduction, robustness, interpretability, and privacy-aware deployment — by transferring information from a teacher to a student via soft outputs, intermediate representations, or structural/architectural guidance. Practical and research advances show that combining distillation modes (feature-level, output-level, progressive module replacement), data augmentation, and adaptive teacher training yields compact models that approach teacher performance even under limited data, heterogeneous devices, or privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Dodson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure. Research has developed a range of distillation objectives (soft logits, feature/attention imitation, relational losses), architectural and layer-mapping strategies, and complementary compression steps (quantization, pruning, architecture search). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can yield compact models that retain much of teacher accuracy across vision, language, and domain-specific tasks, but performance depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability, and distributional alignment. Practical deployments increasingly rely on multi-stage or task-aware pipelines, data- or privacy-aware variants, and teacher adaptations to improve transfer; open challenges include preserving rare-token/edge-case behavior, robustness under distributional shift, and scaling distillation in data-constrained or federated settings.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-level toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. Effective KD requires selecting what to transfer (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational signals), matching teacher and student capacities, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques. When applied with task-aware objectives, projector or alignment modules, and careful treatment of data and teacher preparation, KD yields compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints, though capacity mismatch and data limitations remain important caveats.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer via Adversarial Belief Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Performing knowledge transfer from a large teacher network to a smaller student is a popular task in modern deep learning applications. However, due to growing dataset sizes and stricter privacy regulations, it is increasingly common not to have access to the data that was used to train the teacher. We propose a novel method which trains a student to match the predictions of its teacher without using any data or metadata. We achieve this by training an adversarial generator to search for images on which the student poorly matches the teacher, and then using them to train the student. Our resulting student closely approximates its teacher for simple datasets like SVHN, and on CIFAR10 we improve on the state-of-the-art for few-shot distillation (with 100 images per class), despite using no data. Finally, we also propose a metric to quantify the degree of belief matching between teacher and student in the vicinity of decision boundaries, and observe a significantly higher match between our zero-shot student and the teacher, than between a student distilled with real data and the teacher. Code available at: https://github.com/polo5/ZeroShotKnowledgeTransfer

papers_seen.author: Carney
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses and transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models to improve efficiency while retaining performance. Methods span logits-based soft-label transfer, feature- or layer-wise matching, adversarial and data-free distillation, architecture-aware projection or search, and task-adaptive compression for NLP. Empirical work shows KD is effective across vision, speech, generative models, and language models; recent theory clarifies when and why soft labels help and when mixing hard labels matters. Practical designs—attention-guided layer alignment, projectors or ensembles of projectors, and careful data augmentation or synthetic-data generation—substantially affect student quality. Open challenges include data-privacy constraints, distillation across heterogeneous architectures, preserving teacher errors, and better theoretical/empirical guidance for designing KD pipelines for diverse tasks.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What is Known about Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Existing practice spans matching teacher output distributions, transferring intermediate representations or attention, online and ensemble distillation, and data-free or synthetic-data approaches when original training data are unavailable. KD is typically combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and shaped by practical concerns—teacher–student capacity alignment, what and how to transfer, data availability or privacy, and robustness—which determine real-world effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Waller
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across computer vision, speech, multimodal, and NLP tasks, distillation protocols—ranging from soft-target (logit) matching to intermediate feature and attention-based transfers—enable practical trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and memory. Success depends on careful choices of distillation targets, teacher-student compatibility, data availability, and training dynamics; when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, low-precision, architecture search, or federated protocols) it yields deployable models for resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure. Across vision, language, and multimodal settings, KD variants—logit/soft-target matching, feature- and layer-level imitation, multi-teacher and self-distillation, and data- or privacy-aware protocols—enable substantial reductions in size and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success requires matching the distillation objective to task constraints (data availability, architecture mismatch, privacy needs) and often combining KD with complementary techniques such as pruning or architecture search to meet hardware and latency targets.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Moonshine: Distilling with Cheap Convolutions
papers_seen.abstract: Many engineers wish to deploy modern neural networks in memory-limited settings; but the development of flexible methods for reducing memory use is in its infancy, and there is little knowledge of the resulting cost-benefit. We propose structural model distillation for memory reduction using a strategy that produces a student architecture that is a simple transformation of the teacher architecture: no redesign is needed, and the same hyperparameters can be used. Using attention transfer, we provide Pareto curves/tables for distillation of residual networks with four benchmark datasets, indicating the memory versus accuracy payoff. We show that substantial memory savings are possible with very little loss of accuracy, and confirm that distillation provides student network performance that is better than training that student architecture directly on data.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a versatile suite of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Modern KD extends beyond soft-label matching to include representation- and relation-level objectives, multi- and self-distillation, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical deployment of distilled models depends on matching the distillation recipe to task constraints (data availability, teacher–student capacity, architecture heterogeneity, and privacy or communication limits) and frequently benefits from multi-stage or task-aware distillation schedules. While KD often yields compact models that approach teacher performance, open issues remain around capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher biases or errors, robustness under distribution shift, and reliable methods for distillation without original training data.

papers_seen.author: Juarez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a multifaceted set of techniques for creating smaller, faster models from large neural teachers. Methods span soft-output transfer, intermediate-representation and attention matching, relational/contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-centric strategies including synthetic or data-free approaches. KD is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical work shows strong practical gains across NLP and other modalities, but success depends on careful alignment of teacher and student, data strategies, and attention to robustness and domain-shift limitations.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from large, often overparameterized teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while preserving performance. Across modalities and tasks, KD has evolved from simple soft-label matching to a diverse toolkit that includes intermediate representation matching, multi-teacher schedules, data-centric strategies (augmentation, data-free synthesis), online and distributed protocols, and task-aware adaptations. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how the student is initialized (including whether it is pre-trained), how the data distribution is shaped during distillation, and how robustness and rare-token behavior are addressed. Combining complementary techniques (pretraining, feature imitation, data mixing, and adaptive teacher strategies) produces compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints, but open issues remain around teacher selection, distributional mismatch, fairness, and adversarial robustness.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers_seen.author: Carr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, general-purpose approach for translating large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. Across architectures, modalities, and deployment constraints, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of the teacher's performance; however, realizing those gains in practice requires matching the distillation formulation to data availability, model mismatch, and robustness requirements.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Nuanced Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely adopted approach for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. KD operates through multiple mechanisms—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, and transferring relational or attention patterns—and often yields substantial improvements in latency, memory, and deployability relative to naive student training. However, distillation is not a turnkey solution: its effectiveness depends on what is transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, data availability and privacy constraints, and whether complementary compression methods are applied. Viewed as a toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables flexible, task-aware compression pipelines that can be adapted to real-world constraints while acknowledging remaining limits around robustness, data-free operation, and principled teacher selection.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing deep models and transferring capabilities across architectures and modalities. KD has enabled large speedups and model-size reductions while preserving or even improving downstream task performance when carefully applied. However, distillation is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on data availability, teacher–student alignment, and distributional heterogeneity, and it can transmit teacher biases or errors. Combining logit-based supervision with feature- and relation-focused objectives, aligning intermediate representations, and adapting distillation strategies to task and data constraints yields the best trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Dixon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods compress large deep models into smaller, faster, or more private models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. The literature shows a spectrum of KD signals (soft logits, intermediate features, layer mappings), enhancements via data interventions and architecture search, and combinations with pruning or low-precision inference. Practical success depends on task- and deployment-aware choices (which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, what augmentations or synthetic data to use) as well as attention to privacy and robustness. The field has produced effective recipes for compressing pretrained language models, vision transformers, and generative models, while ongoing work clarifies limits and complementary techniques for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Distilling Task-Specific Knowledge from BERT into Simple Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: In the natural language processing literature, neural networks are becoming increasingly deeper and complex. The recent poster child of this trend is the deep language representation model, which includes BERT, ELMo, and GPT. These developments have led to the conviction that previous-generation, shallower neural networks for language understanding are obsolete. In this paper, however, we demonstrate that rudimentary, lightweight neural networks can still be made competitive without architecture changes, external training data, or additional input features. We propose to distill knowledge from BERT, a state-of-the-art language representation model, into a single-layer BiLSTM, as well as its siamese counterpart for sentence-pair tasks. Across multiple datasets in paraphrasing, natural language inference, and sentiment classification, we achieve comparable results with ELMo, while using roughly 100 times fewer parameters and 15 times less inference time.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Trade-offs, and Empirical Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques seek to transfer predictive power and internal knowledge from large, expensive models (teachers) into smaller, faster models (students), enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Approaches vary from matching teacher output distributions to transferring intermediate representations, designing many-to-many layer mappings, performing data-free distillation when original training data are unavailable, and distilling ensembles or multiple teachers into a single model. In NLP, these methods are applied to compress pre-trained language models, speed up evaluation metrics, and produce task-adaptive compressed models while attempting to retain generalization and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a flexible, system-level toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD techniques transfer information ranging from softened outputs to intermediate representations and relational structure; they can be combined with complementary compression methods (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with data strategies that include augmentation, synthetic generation, or data-free approaches. Effective distillation depends on matching the distillation signals, student architecture, and data strategy to task and deployment constraints. While well-designed KD pipelines often recover most teacher performance, remaining challenges include optimization instability, transfer of teacher errors or biases, handling limited or private data, and preserving rare-token/long-tail behavior in sequence models.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Mahoney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Not Universal Solution for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective and versatile strategy for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When carefully designed—choosing what to transfer (logits, features, relations), preparing or synthesizing appropriate data, and combining KD with complementary methods such as quantization or architecture search—distillation can produce compact models that retain much of teacher performance across modalities. However, KD has limits: teacher–student capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity or absence, and optimization subtleties can reduce gains. Practical deployment therefore benefits from hybrid pipelines that adapt KD objectives to task constraints, incorporate robustness and privacy considerations, and use auxiliary compression techniques where appropriate.
