papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger, often ensemble or over-parameterized teacher models to smaller, faster student models. Across computer vision, graph, generative, and language tasks, distillation reduces storage and inference cost while often retaining most of the teacher's accuracy. Methods range from matching output distributions to aligning intermediate representations or using adversarial generators when training data are unavailable. Distillation has been applied successfully to compress transformers and other large pretrained language models, to speed up question answering and reading-comprehension systems, and to produce compact models suitable for deployment on edge devices. At the same time, distillation faces challenges including loss of certain types of teacher knowledge, sensitivity to which samples are distilled, potential transfer or amplification of undesirable biases, and concerns about robustness and privacy. Recent work addresses these issues by selective sample weighting, multi-teacher schemes, adversarial data-free approaches, and robustness-aware objectives, suggesting a rich design space for future improvement.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile mechanism to compress large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a central component of compression pipelines and matched to task constraints, KD enables large reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Success with KD depends on deliberate choices about what knowledge to transfer (logits, features, relations), how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle limited or missing teacher data, and how to protect robustness and fairness. I argue KD should be the default compression engine for modern deep learning and NLP systems, but its safe and effective use requires task-aware design and hybrid pipelines that combine KD with complementary methods such as student pretraining, progressive replacement, data synthesis, and fairness- or privacy-aware interventions.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from A Stronger Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Unlike existing knowledge distillation methods focus on the baseline settings, where the teacher models and training strategies are not that strong and competing as state-of-the-art approaches, this paper presents a method dubbed DIST to distill better from a stronger teacher. We empirically find that the discrepancy of predictions between the student and a stronger teacher may tend to be fairly severer. As a result, the exact match of predictions in KL divergence would disturb the training and make existing methods perform poorly. In this paper, we show that simply preserving the relations between the predictions of teacher and student would suffice, and propose a correlation-based loss to capture the intrinsic inter-class relations from the teacher explicitly. Besides, considering that different instances have different semantic similarities to each class, we also extend this relational match to the intra-class level. Our method is simple yet practical, and extensive experiments demonstrate that it adapts well to various architectures, model sizes and training strategies, and can achieve state-of-the-art performance consistently on image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation tasks. Code is available at: https://github.com/hunto/DIST_KD .

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Task-Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD is effective across modalities because it permits multiple kinds of transfer (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure) and can be combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies. However, its success is context-dependent: choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data determine final performance and robustness. Treating KD as a configurable, task-aware system—rather than a single recipe—yields the best trade-offs between compactness and retained capability.

papers_seen.author: Archer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers. KD can preserve predictive performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Its strengths derive from a variety of mechanisms — soft-label matching, internal-feature alignment, layer-mapping, and task-adaptive architecture design — and from being combinable with complementary compression techniques. However, realizing consistent gains requires careful choice of distilled targets, attention to representation alignment between teacher and student, and explicit handling of data-, fairness-, and robustness-related risks. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a toolbox of targeted interventions rather than a single recipe, and provides concise, evidence-based recommendations for practitioners compressing models in vision and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and a Prescription
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible tool for compressing large models into efficient students suitable for deployment. When combined with careful pre-training of compact architectures, representation-level supervision, and complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, distillation has important failure modes—capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity, and optimization difficulties—that require task-aware design choices around what to transfer, which teacher(s) to use, and how to prepare distillation data. A pragmatic pipeline that pre-trains compact models, distills both outputs and intermediate representations, and selectively combines KD with other compression steps yields the best trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy in practice.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques shrink large neural models into smaller, faster models for constrained deployment while attempting to preserve task performance. A diverse set of approaches—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, progressive module replacement, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free or generative sample synthesis—has emerged across vision, language, multimodal, and graph tasks. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention maps, or structural priors), how to align heterogeneous architectures, whether teacher or student are adapted during training, and how to handle limited or absent training data. Empirical work shows substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost are possible with modest performance loss, but open problems remain around principled teacher selection, robustness under domain shift, privacy, and closing optimization/capacity gaps between teachers and students.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) remains a practical and flexible approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across tasks and modalities. KD's benefits arise from multiple mechanisms: transferring soft output distributions, mimicking intermediate features, providing regularization that improves generalization, and enabling compression even when original training data are unavailable. Empirically and theoretically, KD should be treated as a toolbox: select loss forms (logit, feature, relational), augment or synthesize data when needed, and consider joint training of teacher and student or teacher design that is friendly to students. Combined with complementary compression techniques (quantization, pruning, architecture design), KD helps produce efficient models that retain much of the teacher's performance while meeting real deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Boyd
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a versatile, practically oriented set of techniques for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Across modalities and tasks, KD transfers information via softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational structure, and is most effective when combined with complementary practices such as pre-training compact students, careful selection or synthesis of distillation data, teacher scheduling, and architecture-aware alignment. Empirical work shows KD routinely enables meaningful latency and memory reductions with modest accuracy loss, but success depends on principled design choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or mismatched data; these considerations motivate task-aware pipelines and ongoing research into robustness, fairness, privacy, and theoretical underpinnings.

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques reduce the size and runtime of large neural models by transferring information from one or more high-capacity teacher models to a smaller student model. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, methods vary in what is transferred (logits, intermediate features, relations, or latent experts), how training data are used (original data, distilled predictions, or no data), and how multiple or imperfect teachers are combined. Practical adaptations include task-specific losses, sample selection or weighting, and architectural transformations; KD is also integrated with system-level strategies such as federated learning and pruning to meet device constraints. Empirical results show KD can preserve much of teacher performance while substantially reducing compute and memory, but success depends on choices of teacher strength, data availability, multi-teacher aggregation, and whether task structure (e.g., localization or ranking) is explicitly addressed.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and broadly applicable strategy for compressing large models and transferring their capabilities to smaller or specialized models. KD can operate at multiple levels (logits, intermediate layers, and features), can be combined with model pruning and precision reduction, and can support domain adaptation and on-device deployment. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its success depends on how teacher knowledge is represented and transferred, the choice of data and augmentations used during distillation, and the deployment context (e.g., heterogeneous federated environments). When methods for intermediate-layer alignment, feature mimicking, data-side regularization, and architecture-aware mapping are combined thoughtfully, KD yields compact, efficient models that retain much of the teacher’s performance while enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical family of methods for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller, faster, or constrained students. Techniques span matching teacher outputs (soft labels), aligning intermediate representations, layer-wise mappings, and data-centric strategies (augmentation, synthesized data, or data-free protocols). Effective deployments combine KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and training choices (pretraining, curriculum schedules, ensemble-to-single transfers). Despite broad empirical success across vision, language, retrieval, and generative tasks, KD requires attention to capacity mismatch, data availability, and optimization dynamics to realize robust, deployable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Stevens
papers_seen.title: The Central, Practical, and Conditional Role of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible set of techniques for transferring useful behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can meet deployment constraints while retaining much of the teacher’s utility. KD methods span soft-target matching, intermediate representation and layer-wise alignment, ensemble-to-single transfers, task-adaptive architecture search, and data-free or privacy-conscious pipelines. Empirical work shows KD can produce compact models that approach teacher performance across NLP, speech, and vision tasks, and that combining KD with architecture-aware compression or augmentation strategies often yields the best trade-offs. However, KD has limits: student capacity, the availability and quality of distilled data, and inherited teacher biases can all constrain outcomes. Responsible and effective compression therefore requires selecting the appropriate distillation signals, considering task and deployment constraints, and combining KD with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, or fairness-aware objectives).

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression approaches transform large, high-performance neural models into smaller, faster models suitable for constrained deployment while attempting to preserve task performance. Methods range from transferring softened output distributions to matching intermediate representations, designing task-aware layer mappings, synthesizing or augmenting data for training, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Applications include compressing pretrained transformers for NLP, improving robustness under domain shift, enabling on-device inference and federated learning with heterogeneous devices, and training non-autoregressive sequence models. Empirical and theoretical work highlights both practical gains and limitations: distillation can yield compact models with strong accuracy but its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, availability or synthesis of data, and handling low-frequency or domain-specific phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models by transferring information from one or more high-capacity teachers to a smaller student model. The field has evolved from simple soft-label matching to rich objectives that align intermediate representations, exploit multiple teachers, search for task-specific student architectures, and generate or synthesize data when original training sets are unavailable. Distillation is applied across modalities (language, speech, vision, graphs) and combined with other compression techniques to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical and theoretical work highlights both practical gains and recurring challenges — data availability, teacher–student heterogeneity, preserving rare or domain-specific behaviors, and principled objective design — and suggests strategies to mitigate them in deployed systems.

papers_seen.author: Santana
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students for deployment in resource-constrained settings. The literature shows a spectrum of distillation objectives—from matching soft output distributions to transferring intermediate representations, relational statistics, and task-specific features—and emphasizes combining KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free distillation). Successful distillation pipelines attend to teacher–student capacity alignment, layer- and signal-selection, and data provenance to preserve accuracy, robustness, and domain suitability. Remaining challenges include distillation without original data, robustness under distribution shift or adversarial attack, and automated, architecture-agnostic distillation for heterogeneous deployment environments.

papers_seen.author: Davenport
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models to enable faster, lower-memory, and more deployable systems. Across computer vision and natural language processing, KD spans logits-based soft-label transfer, feature- and layer-wise matching, online/co-distillation, self-distillation, and architecture-aware strategies (e.g., progressive module replacement and projector layers). Effective compression depends on choices about what knowledge to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, how to treat data during distillation (augmentation, synthetic or few-shot settings), and whether teachers are trained to be student-friendly. When designed to match deployment constraints and task characteristics, distillation pipelines can preserve most teacher performance while improving inference speed, robustness, and sometimes calibration; but they also face failure modes including optimization difficulties, capacity mismatch, and distributional shifts that require targeted remedies.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and intermediate representations. Across vision, speech, language, and graph modalities, KD methods exploit soft targets, feature- and attention-level alignment, contrastive and adversarial objectives, and architecture-aware design to trade accuracy for latency, memory, or privacy. Practical success depends on choices about teacher-student design, data availability and quality, and optimization strategies; contemporary work emphasizes combining representation-level objectives, teacher-friendly or teacher-free approaches, and data-aware training to produce robust, deployable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Cherry
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural relationships. Across vision and NLP, effective distillation combines choices about what to transfer (soft outputs, features, relational signals), how teachers are designed or ensembled, and what data or surrogates are used. Practical pipelines increasingly pair distillation with architecture search, curriculum strategies, and distributed training to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While distillation often recovers much of a teacher's performance, success depends on careful alignment of objectives, data complexity, and optimization procedures; open problems include principled handling of imperfect teachers, robustness and fairness under compression, and scalable privacy-preserving distillation.

papers_seen.author: Russell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Insights, and Practical Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior or internal structure. A broad family of distillation objectives—ranging from soft-label (logit) matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, layer-wise supervision, multi-teacher schedules, and integration with architecture search or data augmentation—enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Empirical successes span classification, object detection, machine translation, and language-model compression, but practical deployment requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to curate or synthesize distillation data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression techniques. The method’s effectiveness arises partly from the regularizing properties of soft targets and richer teacher signals, yet distillation can propagate teacher errors and struggle with capacity, data heterogeneity, and robustness unless augmented by task-aware design or additional engineering.

papers_seen.author: May
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Paradigm for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a compression trick: when treated as a broad training paradigm it enables compact, robust, and deployable models across modalities and tasks. By integrating logit-level guidance, intermediate feature transfer, architecture-aware projectors, adaptive teacher selection, data- and domain-aware strategies, and robustness-aware objectives, KD pipelines can produce students that approach teacher performance while satisfying latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical success requires designing what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous components, and how to shape inputs and curricula for the student—rather than relying on a single generic distillation recipe.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or multi-modal deep models into smaller, more deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or other structured knowledge. Work across vision, speech, and NLP shows a range of mechanisms (soft-label matching, internal-representation matching, layer mapping, and feature/attention guidance) and adaptations for limited or private data. Empirical results indicate distilled students can approach teacher accuracy while greatly reducing size and inference cost, but effectiveness depends on what knowledge is distilled, how it is represented, and the training regime.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable method for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably reduces parameter counts and inference cost while preserving much teacher performance when paired with task-aware design choices and complementary compression techniques. Its success, however, depends on decisions about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, access to data or synthetic surrogates, and mitigation of robustness and distribution-shift failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, modality-agnostic approach that enables conversion of large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When treated as a composable toolkit—combining soft-target transfer, intermediate representation alignment, relational or structural signals, data augmentation/synthesis, and multi-stage teacher–student schedules—KD yields compact models that retain much of the teacher's effectiveness. Real-world success requires attention to teacher quality, data provenance, architecture alignment, and safeguards for robustness and fairness; with these design choices, KD is a practical backbone for deploying efficient deep learning and NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transform large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable ones by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural properties from teacher to student. Approaches vary from logits-based transfer to feature- or module-level imitation, multi-teacher and meta-learned schemes, data-free (zero-shot) methods, and procedures designed for robustness or computational efficiency. Across vision, speech, graph, and NLP settings (including large pretrained Transformer models), distillation has enabled substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of the original performance. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer (probabilities, features, modules), how to generate or augment data for transfer, and how to preserve or transfer robustness and task-specific inductive biases. Remaining challenges include matching teacher performance across tasks with minimal data, ensuring robustness under adversarial or distributional shift, and balancing efficiency with fidelity in large-scale pretrained language models.

papers_seen.author: Joyce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Settings, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable deployment of high-performing deep models in latency- or resource-constrained settings by transferring knowledge from larger “teacher” models or ensembles to smaller “student” models. Work in this area spans methods that match final outputs, intermediate representations, or relational structure; approaches that adapt teacher signals through meta-learning or task-aware filters; and specializations for settings such as vision–language, graph learning, federated or distributed training, and data-free scenarios. Empirical results show KD can yield large efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance, but practical success depends on handling domain shift, architectural mismatch, heterogeneous data and devices, and the quality or calibration of teacher outputs. Important theoretical and statistical analyses have begun to clarify when and why distillation helps, but open problems remain around robust, privacy-preserving, and architecture-agnostic distillation for production systems.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods have become central tools for deploying large deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. Work in this area spans techniques that transfer predictive behavior or internal representations from large teacher models to smaller students, approaches that operate without access to original training data, methods that preserve privacy or reduce communication in distributed settings, and specialized strategies for large pre-trained language and vision transformer models. Key themes include layer- and module-level mappings between teacher and student, task-aware selection of distilled signals, adversarial and generative approaches to synthesize training inputs, and the combination of pruning or architecture search with distillation. Practical trade-offs arise between fidelity to teacher behavior, student capacity, data availability, and robustness to distribution shifts or adversarial attacks. Ongoing challenges include aligning heterogeneous modalities and architectures, selecting what information to transfer for a given downstream task, and ensuring privacy and robustness while maintaining high compression ratios.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.

papers_seen.author: Beck
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful set of techniques for transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller student models so that compact models can retain much of the performance of their teachers. Across modalities and tasks, KD has evolved from simple soft-target (logit) matching to include feature- and layer-level supervision, online and multi-teacher schemes, meta-learned teachers, data-free and privacy-aware variants, and combinations with quantization and low-precision inference. Empirical work shows KD can substantially reduce model size and inference cost with modest performance loss, but success depends on careful choice of what to transfer, how to align teacher and student representations, and how to handle limited or mismatched data. Remaining practical issues include teacher–student heterogeneity, propagation of teacher errors, robustness to domain shifts, and limits to compression for some generative and structured prediction tasks.

papers_seen.author: Wells
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practice, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or costly models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. A rich toolkit has emerged—matching soft teacher outputs, imitating intermediate representations or attention, aligning layers, and combining distillation with architecture-aware search or other compression primitives. When matched to task constraints (data availability, teacher–student capacity, domain shift), distillation can yield compact models that approach teacher performance and enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, success requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to curate or synthesize data for distillation, and how to mitigate capacity and robustness issues.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: The Central Role and Practical Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a core set of techniques for converting large, expensive neural models into smaller, faster students suitable for real-world deployment. KD variants transfer soft outputs, intermediate representations, or structural behaviors; they can be combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture modification) and adapted for constrained data, privacy, and deployment regimes. However, distillation’s success depends on principled choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, how to obtain or synthesize training data, and how to mitigate teacher-induced errors or biases. Practical deployments therefore require task-aware distillation design, careful teacher selection or adaptation, and evaluation of failure modes such as degraded rare-token behavior or domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Cruz
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable paradigm for transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller, more efficient students. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, KD methods—ranging from matching teacher output distributions to aligning intermediate representations and relational structure—enable substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to obtain or synthesize training data, and whether to complement distillation with adversarial or ensemble signals. When these elements are chosen and tuned for task and deployment constraints, KD produces compact models that are effective in resource-limited and application-specific settings.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Cross-modal Knowledge Distillation for Vision-to-Sensor Action Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) based on multi-modal approach has been recently shown to improve the accuracy performance of HAR. However, restricted computational resources associated with wearable devices, i.e., smartwatch, failed to directly support such advanced methods. To tackle this issue, this study introduces an end-to-end Vision-to-Sensor Knowledge Distillation (VSKD) framework. In this VSKD framework, only time-series data, i.e., accelerometer data, is needed from wearable devices during the testing phase. Therefore, this framework will not only reduce the computational demands on edge devices, but also produce a learning model that closely matches the performance of the computational expensive multi-modal approach. In order to retain the local temporal relationship and facilitate visual deep learning models, we first convert time-series data to two-dimensional images by applying the Gramian Angular Field ( GAF) based encoding method. We adopted ResNet18 and multi-scale TRN with BN-Inception as teacher and student network in this study, respectively. A novel loss function, named Distance and Angle-wised Semantic Knowledge loss (DASK), is proposed to mitigate the modality variations between the vision and the sensor domain. Extensive experimental results on UTD-MHAD, MMAct, and Berkeley-MHAD datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and competitiveness of the proposed VSKD model which can deployed on wearable sensors.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Distilling Task-Specific Knowledge from BERT into Simple Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: In the natural language processing literature, neural networks are becoming increasingly deeper and complex. The recent poster child of this trend is the deep language representation model, which includes BERT, ELMo, and GPT. These developments have led to the conviction that previous-generation, shallower neural networks for language understanding are obsolete. In this paper, however, we demonstrate that rudimentary, lightweight neural networks can still be made competitive without architecture changes, external training data, or additional input features. We propose to distill knowledge from BERT, a state-of-the-art language representation model, into a single-layer BiLSTM, as well as its siamese counterpart for sentence-pair tasks. Across multiple datasets in paraphrasing, natural language inference, and sentiment classification, we achieve comparable results with ELMo, while using roughly 100 times fewer parameters and 15 times less inference time.

papers_seen.author: Aguilar
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a multifaceted toolkit for shrinking large neural models while retaining much of their accuracy. Approaches include matching teacher outputs (soft logits), aligning intermediate representations or attention patterns, transforming architectures to be resource-efficient, and designing teacher–student curricula or multi-teacher aggregations. KD is applied across supervised, self-supervised, few-shot, federated, and privacy-constrained scenarios and is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align layers and capacity, and how to handle limited or sensitive data; when designed carefully, KD enables deployment of compact models for diverse NLP and vision tasks while exposing open questions about robustness, fairness, and distributional generalization.

papers_seen.author: House
papers_seen.title: Practical Knowledge Distillation for Deploying Large NLP and Deep Models: A Unified Argument for Multi-Teacher, Data-Agnostic, and Federated Techniques
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and essential set of techniques for compressing large deep and language models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, privacy, and device-heterogeneity constraints. A mature KD strategy must simultaneously preserve teacher knowledge, generalize across domains and distributions, and respect deployment constraints (e.g., lack of original data or heterogeneous client devices). Empirical and methodological advances show that combining multi-teacher strategies, data-agnostic/distillation-from-generator approaches, feature-level projectors or ensembles, targeted augmentation, and adaptations for federated settings yields robust, efficient student models that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Travis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression: Evidence, Mechanisms, Limits, and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a central and practical toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across vision, generative modeling, and natural language processing. KD succeeds because it can transfer diverse signals—soft logits, intermediate representations, relational structure—and because those signals can be adapted to constraints such as data scarcity, architecture mismatch, or privacy. However, distillation is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align layers, how to prepare or synthesize data, and how to address teacher errors and optimization instabilities. The best outcomes arise from integrated distillation pipelines that combine representation-level objectives, careful data strategies (including augmentation or synthetic samples), architecture-aware mapping, and multi-stage or multi-teacher schedules tailored to the deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques that compress large, high-performing models into smaller, more efficient students for deployment in constrained settings. KD methods span soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-representation and attention transfer, relational objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and teacher-free or data-synthesizing approaches. When combined with complementary compression practices (pre-training compact architectures, pruning, quantization, and data augmentation), KD often preserves most of a teacher’s performance while reducing latency, memory, and energy requirements. However, success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, data availability and distributional shift, and mitigation of propagated biases or robustness gaps. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, common failure modes, and practical design patterns shown to improve distillation outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring information from a teacher model. Across computer vision, language, graph, and healthcare applications, KD variants augment or replace naive logit matching with feature/hint matching, data augmentation, layer mapping strategies, and data-free or privacy-aware mechanisms. Practical work emphasizes task-adaptive compression, many-to-many layer alignment for pre-trained transformers, and the use of synthetic or mixed inputs to improve student generalization. At the same time, theoretical and empirical studies highlight limitations under data heterogeneity and imperfect teachers, motivating hybrid losses that mix soft and hard labels and methods that control privacy leakage during distillation.

papers_seen.author: Ware
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical System for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential and practical approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a system—covering teacher design, the training signal, data and augmentation, and efficiency constraints—KD can retain much of a teacher's performance while meeting latency, memory, and domain requirements. However, its success depends on careful choices about teacher quality, distillation objectives, available data, and complementary compression techniques; awareness of these factors yields the most reliable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Practical Prescriptions for Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, efficient students suitable for deployment. While KD reliably reduces model size and inference cost, its effectiveness depends critically on choices around teacher design, the training signal (soft labels vs. representations), the data used for distillation, and additional constraints such as fairness and privacy. To realize reliable, high-quality compressed models in NLP and related domains, practitioners should treat KD as a system composed of complementary ingredients—data augmentation, multi-teacher or meta-learned teachers, representation-level objectives, and interventions for bias and privacy—rather than a single off-the-shelf loss.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have become central tools for shrinking large deep models into smaller, faster, or more interpretable models while retaining much of their performance. Research has expanded beyond the original logit-based teacher-student paradigm to include feature mimicking, self-distillation, data-free and privacy-preserving variants, multi-teacher and adaptive-teacher strategies, and task- or hardware-aware compression. These methods have been applied across modalities — including vision, graphs, generative models, and a broad set of NLP tasks — and are increasingly combined with architecture search and pruning to meet deployment constraints. Despite empirical successes, important questions remain about what knowledge is most useful to transfer, how to select or adapt teachers, and how to operate under data, compute, or privacy limitations.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across vision and language, KD variants — from simple soft-target matching to feature-level, layer-aware, and many-to-many mapping approaches — enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to map layers, how to use or synthesize data, and whether to adapt teachers or students; remaining challenges include handling heterogeneous data and devices, preserving robustness and fairness, and enabling data-free or privacy-conscious distillation.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring useful predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models. The literature offers a range of objectives (soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, relational losses), architectural strategies (layer mapping, progressive replacement, many-to-many alignment), and data approaches (using original data, augmented or synthesized surrogates, or data-free/zero-shot methods). Practical success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to manage data scarcity, privacy, and domain shift. Applications include compressing pre-trained language models for NLP, adapting multi-modal models to single modalities, compressing ranking and detection systems, and enabling deployment under compute, latency, or privacy constraints. Open challenges remain in preserving rare-token behaviors, coping with imperfect or heterogeneous teachers, and designing robust, privacy-aware distillation protocols.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques form a diverse toolkit for transferring information from larger, more expensive models to smaller, faster, or more constrained models. Methods range from matching output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, altering training curricula, and designing compression-aware teachers or architectures. These approaches have been applied across domains including vision, speech, translation, retrieval, and on-device deployment, and have been adapted to privacy- and communication-constrained settings. Empirical and analytical work has clarified different mechanisms by which distillation aids learning, and recent work explores automation, adversarial feature transfer, sample selection, and architecture-aware strategies to improve efficiency without sacrificing much performance.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core practical approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students while retaining much of the original performance. Multiple distillation mechanisms—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, adversarial/ensemble-based transfer, and data-free or selective-sample techniques—allow KD to address constraints such as limited data, heterogeneous deployment, low-precision hardware, and domain shift. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often acts both as a transfer of representational structure and as a regularizer; its success depends on choices about what is transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, how training data (real or synthetic) are used, and which complementary compression methods are applied. Remaining practical challenges include distributional mismatch, heterogeneity of architectures and devices, and principled teacher selection and optimization strategies.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Revisiting Knowledge Distillation via Label Smoothing Regularization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to distill the knowledge of a cumbersome teacher model into a lightweight student model. Its success is generally attributed to the privileged information on similarities among categories provided by the teacher model, and in this sense, only strong teacher models are deployed to teach weaker students in practice. In this work, we challenge this common belief by following experimental observations: 1) beyond the acknowledgment that the teacher can improve the student, the student can also enhance the teacher significantly by reversing the KD procedure; 2) a poorly-trained teacher with much lower accuracy than the student can still improve the latter significantly. To explain these observations, we provide a theoretical analysis of the relationships between KD and label smoothing regularization. We prove that 1) KD is a type of learned label smoothing regularization and 2) label smoothing regularization provides a virtual teacher model for KD. From these results, we argue that the success of KD is not fully due to the similarity information between categories from teachers, but also to the regularization of soft targets, which is equally or even more important.   Based on these analyses, we further propose a novel Teacher-free Knowledge Distillation (Tf-KD) framework, where a student model learns from itself or manuallydesigned regularization distribution. The Tf-KD achieves comparable performance with normal KD from a superior teacher, which is well applied when a stronger teacher model is unavailable. Meanwhile, Tf-KD is generic and can be directly deployed for training deep neural networks. Without any extra computation cost, Tf-KD achieves up to 0.65\% improvement on ImageNet over well-established baseline models, which is superior to label smoothing regularization.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from matching teacher logits to a flexible toolkit for producing compact, efficient models suitable for deployment and adaptation in deep learning and NLP. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can transfer predictive behavior, intermediate representations, and task-specific properties (e.g., robustness or privacy signals), and it is most effective when combined with complementary strategies such as pre-training of compact architectures, data-side interventions, and low-precision or structured pruning. Success depends on careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous teacher and student architectures, how to construct or augment distillation data, and how to adapt teacher behavior; practical pipelines treat KD as one component of a broader compression workflow rather than a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Robbins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Central Tool for Compressing Deep and NLP Models: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical method to transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models into smaller, faster students, enabling deployment under latency, memory, and data constraints. KD is most effective when integrated with sensible pre-training, representation-level supervision, adaptive teacher strategies, and complementary compression techniques; but it is not a universal solution and can fail when data are limited, teacher and student representations mismatch, or optimization is poorly designed. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a flexible toolbox—applied carefully, combined with other compression methods, and adapted to domain or system constraints—to deliver reliable, high-quality compressed models for deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and/or internal representations. A rich set of mechanisms—soft-target (logit) matching, feature or representation imitation, layer-wise mapping, multi-teacher and ensemble-to-student transfers, and data-free or privacy-aware strategies—has been developed and combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Empirical evidence shows distilled students can recover much of teacher accuracy while substantially reducing latency and footprint, but success depends on choices about what to transfer, data and augmentation strategies, teacher quality, and training schedules. Ongoing work focuses on robustness to domain shift, heterogeneous devices, limited or unavailable data, and principled ways to align heterogeneous teacher and student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Yu
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: Toward Integrated Feature-, Data- and Robustness-aware Knowledge Distillation for Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has matured from simple logit matching into a toolbox of complementary techniques. Empirical and theoretical work shows that (1) matching internal features often transfers richer representations than logits alone, (2) the choice of input-side interventions (e.g., data augmentation) substantially changes distillation dynamics, and (3) robustness, teacher quality, and sample selection must be addressed explicitly. I argue that effective model compression in deep learning and NLP requires integrating feature-level mimicry with careful input-space design, selective or confidence-weighted teacher signals, and robustness-aware objectives. This combined approach maximizes student performance while keeping models compact and deployment-ready.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Task-Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD is effective across modalities because it permits multiple kinds of transfer (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure) and can be combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies. However, its success is context-dependent: choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data determine final performance and robustness. Treating KD as a configurable, task-aware system—rather than a single recipe—yields the best trade-offs between compactness and retained capability.
