papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: The Practical Centrality of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable tool for reducing model size and inference cost while preserving (or even improving) performance. Beyond straightforward teacher→student logit matching, KD can be applied structurally (transforming architectures without redesign), combined with quantization, used for domain adaptation of large pretrained language models, leveraged in multi-teacher and few-shot settings, and operated without access to original data. KD’s benefits arise both from transferring predictive behavior and from inducing effective regularization; when paired with careful choices (e.g., feature projectors, divergence measures, or pseudo-replay for data-free settings), KD enables deployment of compact, reliable models across vision, speech, language, graph, and generative-model domains.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a flexible, system-level toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD techniques transfer information ranging from softened outputs to intermediate representations and relational structure; they can be combined with complementary compression methods (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with data strategies that include augmentation, synthetic generation, or data-free approaches. Effective distillation depends on matching the distillation signals, student architecture, and data strategy to task and deployment constraints. While well-designed KD pipelines often recover most teacher performance, remaining challenges include optimization instability, transfer of teacher errors or biases, handling limited or private data, and preserving rare-token/long-tail behavior in sequence models.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Methods, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring behavioral and representational signals from teachers. KD includes diverse techniques — soft-target supervision, intermediate feature and attention matching, layer-mapping strategies, online and ensemble-to-single transfers, and selective sample or data-aware procedures — that are adapted to task, architecture, and deployment constraints. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and appropriate data strategies, KD can yield compact models that retain most teacher performance; however, success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, and data availability.

papers_seen.author: Ware
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical System for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential and practical approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a system—covering teacher design, the training signal, data and augmentation, and efficiency constraints—KD can retain much of a teacher's performance while meeting latency, memory, and domain requirements. However, its success depends on careful choices about teacher quality, distillation objectives, available data, and complementary compression techniques; awareness of these factors yields the most reliable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Toolchain for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and empirically effective paradigm for producing compact, resource-efficient models from larger teachers across computer vision, language, graph, and speech tasks. As a modular system, KD supports multiple information-transfer signals (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational structure), can operate with or without original training data, and composes naturally with complementary compression methods (quantization, pruning, and architecture search). Real-world deployment requires careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle limited or no access to teacher data, and how to address robustness and fairness concerns. When KD is applied as a deliberate toolchain—selecting task-aware objectives, incorporating multi-teacher or synthetic-data protocols, and combining with data- and model-level compression—practical students can approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Open problems remain around preserving rare-event behaviors, domain shift, and student-aware teacher shaping, which motivate focused research on curricula, data synthesis, and representation-aware objectives.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure from teachers to students. A rich family of KD methods—soft-target/logit matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, multi-teacher and ensemble supervision, data-free and data-augmented distillation, and teacher-student co-design—has been developed to meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy) across vision and language tasks. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance when distillation objectives, data strategies, and architecture choices are well matched. Remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher biases or errors, scarcity or absence of real data, and preserving low-frequency behaviors in sequence models. Practical pipelines combine pretraining of compact architectures, multi-objective distillation (outputs + internals), data augmentation or synthesis, and teacher adaptation to produce robust, efficient student models.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure. Across vision and natural language tasks, KD methods—ranging from soft-target/logit matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, selective sample transfer, multi-teacher and data-free strategies—enable substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute while often preserving most of the teacher’s performance. Practical success depends on matching what is distilled to student capacity, managing data availability (including data-free or synthetic approaches), and addressing harms such as transferred biases or degraded rare-token behavior. A pragmatic pipeline mixes pretraining, representation-aware losses, targeted data manipulations, and teacher-aware design to achieve favorable trade-offs among efficiency, accuracy, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Cherry
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural relationships. Across vision and NLP, effective distillation combines choices about what to transfer (soft outputs, features, relational signals), how teachers are designed or ensembled, and what data or surrogates are used. Practical pipelines increasingly pair distillation with architecture search, curriculum strategies, and distributed training to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While distillation often recovers much of a teacher's performance, success depends on careful alignment of objectives, data complexity, and optimization procedures; open problems include principled handling of imperfect teachers, robustness and fairness under compression, and scalable privacy-preserving distillation.

papers_seen.author: Carrillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Design-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a flexible toolbox—combining softened-output supervision with representation-level alignment, teacher design, and complementary compression techniques—KD reliably reduces model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. At the same time, KD is not automatic: its success depends on what is distilled, student capacity, data availability, and targeted interventions to address robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and broadly applicable strategy for compressing large models and transferring their capabilities to smaller or specialized models. KD can operate at multiple levels (logits, intermediate layers, and features), can be combined with model pruning and precision reduction, and can support domain adaptation and on-device deployment. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its success depends on how teacher knowledge is represented and transferred, the choice of data and augmentations used during distillation, and the deployment context (e.g., heterogeneous federated environments). When methods for intermediate-layer alignment, feature mimicking, data-side regularization, and architecture-aware mapping are combined thoughtfully, KD yields compact, efficient models that retain much of the teacher’s performance while enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Pre-training Plus Strategic Distillation: Practical Principles for Compressing Deep NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are most effective when combined with deliberate choices about pre-training, the form of knowledge transferred, data manipulation during distillation, and adaptive teacher-student dynamics. Compact models that are pre-trained, trained to mimic both outputs and internal representations, and exposed to carefully designed augmented or mixed inputs can match much of the performance of larger models while meeting deployment constraints. However, compression success depends critically on optimization, data distribution, and task-specific phenomena such as rare-word behavior in sequence generation. I argue that a pragmatic pipeline—pre-train compact architectures, distill soft targets and internal representations, use augmentation/mixing to shape training data complexity, and apply adaptive or meta-learned teacher strategies—offers the best trade-off between efficiency and accuracy for deep learning and NLP applications.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: R2L: Distilling Neural Radiance Field to Neural Light Field for Efficient Novel View Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Recent research explosion on Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) shows the encouraging potential to represent complex scenes with neural networks. One major drawback of NeRF is its prohibitive inference time: Rendering a single pixel requires querying the NeRF network hundreds of times. To resolve it, existing efforts mainly attempt to reduce the number of required sampled points. However, the problem of iterative sampling still exists. On the other hand, Neural Light Field (NeLF) presents a more straightforward representation over NeRF in novel view synthesis -- the rendering of a pixel amounts to one single forward pass without ray-marching. In this work, we present a deep residual MLP network (88 layers) to effectively learn the light field. We show the key to successfully learning such a deep NeLF network is to have sufficient data, for which we transfer the knowledge from a pre-trained NeRF model via data distillation. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world scenes show the merits of our method over other counterpart algorithms. On the synthetic scenes, we achieve 26-35x FLOPs reduction (per camera ray) and 28-31x runtime speedup, meanwhile delivering significantly better (1.4-2.8 dB average PSNR improvement) rendering quality than NeRF without any customized parallelism requirement.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible, practical toolkit for producing compact, deployable deep models across vision and natural language tasks. KD encompasses matching teacher outputs, aligning internal representations, leveraging multi-teacher or online schedules, and using data-side strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free generation). When combined with architecture-aware design and complementary compression methods, KD often yields students that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Remaining challenges center on teacher–student mismatch, data availability, robustness, and the potential transfer of undesirable biases.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Compressing Visual-linguistic Model via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite exciting progress in pre-training for visual-linguistic (VL) representations, very few aspire to a small VL model. In this paper, we study knowledge distillation (KD) to effectively compress a transformer-based large VL model into a small VL model. The major challenge arises from the inconsistent regional visual tokens extracted from different detectors of Teacher and Student, resulting in the misalignment of hidden representations and attention distributions. To address the problem, we retrain and adapt the Teacher by using the same region proposals from Student's detector while the features are from Teacher's own object detector. With aligned network inputs, the adapted Teacher is capable of transferring the knowledge through the intermediate representations. Specifically, we use the mean square error loss to mimic the attention distribution inside the transformer block and present a token-wise noise contrastive loss to align the hidden state by contrasting with negative representations stored in a sample queue. To this end, we show that our proposed distillation significantly improves the performance of small VL models on image captioning and visual question answering tasks. It reaches 120.8 in CIDEr score on COCO captioning, an improvement of 5.1 over its non-distilled counterpart; and an accuracy of 69.8 on VQA 2.0, a 0.8 gain from the baseline. Our extensive experiments and ablations confirm the effectiveness of VL distillation in both pre-training and fine-tuning stages.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Robust Cross-Modal Representation Learning with Progressive Self-Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The learning objective of vision-language approach of CLIP does not effectively account for the noisy many-to-many correspondences found in web-harvested image captioning datasets, which contributes to its compute and data inefficiency. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel training framework based on cross-modal contrastive learning that uses progressive self-distillation and soft image-text alignments to more efficiently learn robust representations from noisy data. Our model distills its own knowledge to dynamically generate soft-alignment targets for a subset of images and captions in every minibatch, which are then used to update its parameters. Extensive evaluation across 14 benchmark datasets shows that our method consistently outperforms its CLIP counterpart in multiple settings, including: (a) zero-shot classification, (b) linear probe transfer, and (c) image-text retrieval, without incurring added computational cost. Analysis using an ImageNet-based robustness test-bed reveals that our method offers better effective robustness to natural distribution shifts compared to both ImageNet-trained models and CLIP itself. Lastly, pretraining with datasets spanning two orders of magnitude in size shows that our improvements over CLIP tend to scale with number of training examples.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Compression and Robustness in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, multifaceted technique for compressing large models while often preserving — and sometimes improving — task performance. KD can transfer ensemble behaviour, provide regularization benefits, enable deployment under privacy or communication constraints, and be adapted to domain-specific and generation tasks. Practical KD implementations leverage ensembles, feature-level projectors, data augmentation, self-distillation, or data-free/federated protocols depending on resource and data availability. This paper argues that KD should be treated not only as a compression trick but as a general-purpose training paradigm with distinct theoretical and practical consequences for representation quality, robustness, and deployability.

papers_seen.author: Ortiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, Applications, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a broad, mature toolkit for turning large, high-performing neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable models. Approaches vary from transferring softened outputs to aligning intermediate representations or relational structure, from online and multi-teacher schemes to data-free and privacy-aware pipelines. Empirical work across vision, language, speech, and other modalities shows that well-designed distillation can preserve most of a teacher's performance while delivering substantial reductions in inference cost, parameter count, and memory footprint. Practical success depends on matching distillation targets and schedules to student capacity and deployment constraints, handling limited or private data appropriately, and addressing robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift concerns.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Distilled Semantics for Comprehensive Scene Understanding from Videos
papers_seen.abstract: Whole understanding of the surroundings is paramount to autonomous systems. Recent works have shown that deep neural networks can learn geometry (depth) and motion (optical flow) from a monocular video without any explicit supervision from ground truth annotations, particularly hard to source for these two tasks. In this paper, we take an additional step toward holistic scene understanding with monocular cameras by learning depth and motion alongside with semantics, with supervision for the latter provided by a pre-trained network distilling proxy ground truth images. We address the three tasks jointly by a) a novel training protocol based on knowledge distillation and self-supervision and b) a compact network architecture which enables efficient scene understanding on both power hungry GPUs and low-power embedded platforms. We thoroughly assess the performance of our framework and show that it yields state-of-the-art results for monocular depth estimation, optical flow and motion segmentation.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring information from a teacher model. Across computer vision, language, graph, and healthcare applications, KD variants augment or replace naive logit matching with feature/hint matching, data augmentation, layer mapping strategies, and data-free or privacy-aware mechanisms. Practical work emphasizes task-adaptive compression, many-to-many layer alignment for pre-trained transformers, and the use of synthetic or mixed inputs to improve student generalization. At the same time, theoretical and empirical studies highlight limitations under data heterogeneity and imperfect teachers, motivating hybrid losses that mix soft and hard labels and methods that control privacy leakage during distillation.

papers_seen.author: Chandler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Multi-Tool Approach to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single recipe but as a flexible family of methods that, when combined with task-aware design and complementary compression techniques, enables deployment of compact models with strong utility. KD can transfer final-output behavior, intermediate representations, and structured relationships; it can operate with or without original training data, be adapted for privacy-sensitive or federated settings, and be combined with quantization or pruning to meet hardware constraints. Effective practice requires attention to what is distilled, how teachers and students are prepared, and how KD is integrated into the broader compression pipeline to avoid propagation of teacher biases or degradation on rare or shifted data.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Model Compression and Practical NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher's effectiveness. A growing body of work shows KD's versatility across modalities (vision, speech, text), deployment regimes (edge devices, distributed training), and model families (transformers, convolutional nets, generative models). Combining richer teacher signals (intermediate representations, attention maps, or learned teacher updates), stronger input-side practices (data augmentation), and complementary compression methods (architecture search, pruning) yields robust, efficient students suitable for real-world constraints. This paper argues that distillation should be treated not as a single recipe but as a flexible toolkit whose components are chosen to match task constraints, and it highlights promising techniques to improve transfer fidelity, training efficiency, and downstream performance.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques shrink large neural models into smaller, faster models for constrained deployment while attempting to preserve task performance. A diverse set of approaches—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, progressive module replacement, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free or generative sample synthesis—has emerged across vision, language, multimodal, and graph tasks. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention maps, or structural priors), how to align heterogeneous architectures, whether teacher or student are adapted during training, and how to handle limited or absent training data. Empirical work shows substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost are possible with modest performance loss, but open problems remain around principled teacher selection, robustness under domain shift, privacy, and closing optimization/capacity gaps between teachers and students.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central, Practical, and Best Used as an Integrated, Multi‑Level Strategy
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable toolkit for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD works best when it goes beyond naive logits-only matching and integrates representation-level transfer, input-side interventions, robustness-aware objectives, and complementary compression methods. However, effective deployment requires careful teacher–student co-design, attention to data provenance and augmentation, explicit handling of teacher uncertainty and bias, and privacy-aware training choices. Treated as a flexible, multi-stage pipeline rather than a single recipe, KD enables substantial efficiency gains while managing the key failure modes that emerge in real-world settings.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural knowledge. Methods span matching softened output distributions, feature- and attention-level imitation, layer mapping and progressive module replacement, channel- and module-aware transfers, and data-free or generative approaches for when original training data are unavailable. Practical pipelines combine KD with quantization, low-precision training, pruning, or architecture transformations and often rely on staged or adaptive teacher-student schedules. Empirical evidence shows KD can yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance across vision and NLP tasks, but success depends on teacher quality, what and which samples are distilled, data availability, and careful engineering of interfaces between heterogeneous teacher and student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Owens
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, multi-faceted approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, faster models while preserving much of their performance. Beyond simple teacher-student logits matching, distillation can be adapted to transfer inductive biases, deploy in federated or privacy-constrained settings, operate without access to original training data, and improve robustness and domain specialization. When combined with techniques such as feature mimicking, careful soft-label regularization, and online or ensemble-based training regimes, distillation provides a flexible toolkit to meet the efficiency, privacy, and deployment constraints of modern deep learning and NLP applications.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers_seen.author: Hickman
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation for Compressing Deep Models in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central tool to make large deep models practical: it reduces model size and latency, enables domain adaptation, preserves privacy and scalability, and can even improve robustness when applied carefully. Successful deployments balance which teacher signals are transferred (logits, features, attention or answers), how they are aligned (layer-wise, projector-mediated, task-aware filters), and the training setup (multi-teacher, online, or adversarial). I argue that a principled combination of feature-level guidance, task-aware selection, and appropriate distillation architecture gives the best tradeoffs for NLP deployment: it preserves downstream performance while enabling orders-of-magnitude gains in speed, capacity, and deployability.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Mahoney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Not Universal Solution for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective and versatile strategy for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When carefully designed—choosing what to transfer (logits, features, relations), preparing or synthesizing appropriate data, and combining KD with complementary methods such as quantization or architecture search—distillation can produce compact models that retain much of teacher performance across modalities. However, KD has limits: teacher–student capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity or absence, and optimization subtleties can reduce gains. Practical deployment therefore benefits from hybrid pipelines that adapt KD objectives to task constraints, incorporate robustness and privacy considerations, and use auxiliary compression techniques where appropriate.

papers_seen.author: Kelley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and complementary model-compression methods form a versatile toolkit for transferring knowledge from large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. Work in the past decade has expanded simple teacher→student logit matching into a broad set of techniques that match intermediate representations, exploit attention or structural signals, operate with or without access to original training data, and combine with architecture-aware compression (pruning, quantization, or search). Empirical evidence shows distilled students can recover much of teacher quality across language, vision, and retrieval tasks when distillation objectives, student capacity, and data strategies are chosen deliberately. Important practical concerns remain: optimization and capacity mismatches that limit perfect teacher replication, distributional or privacy constraints on distillation data, and trade-offs between fidelity, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Flores
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad ecosystem of KD variants has emerged—matching teacher output distributions, aligning intermediate features or attention, transferring relational structure, online and multi-teacher schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware techniques. In practice KD is often combined with pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data-management strategies to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While KD routinely enables large reductions in parameters and inference cost with modest drops in accuracy, challenges remain in handling domain shift, limited or private data, preserving rare-token or fine-grained behaviors, and avoiding propagation of teacher errors and biases.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Flexible Core Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not a single recipe but a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large models into compact students suitable for deployment. When combined with task-aware architecture choices, ensemble or self-generated signals, and orthogonal compression methods, KD reliably reduces inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Careful attention to what is distilled, data strategy, and training dynamics mitigates common failure modes and enables robust, real-world compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Ware
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical System for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential and practical approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a system—covering teacher design, the training signal, data and augmentation, and efficiency constraints—KD can retain much of a teacher's performance while meeting latency, memory, and domain requirements. However, its success depends on careful choices about teacher quality, distillation objectives, available data, and complementary compression techniques; awareness of these factors yields the most reliable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Capabilities, Mechanisms, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically indispensable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—choosing appropriate distillation targets, preparing the student (often via pre-training), and addressing data, privacy, and robustness constraints—KD yields compact models that retain a substantial fraction of teacher performance across vision, speech, and language tasks. However, its success depends on design choices (what to distill and when), data availability, and mitigation of teacher errors; thus KD is best treated as a system of complementary techniques rather than a single recipe.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers with Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of unifying knowledge from a set of classifiers with different architectures and target classes into a single classifier, given only a generic set of unlabelled data. We call this problem Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers (UHC). This problem is motivated by scenarios where data is collected from multiple sources, but the sources cannot share their data, e.g., due to privacy concerns, and only privately trained models can be shared. In addition, each source may not be able to gather data to train all classes due to data availability at each source, and may not be able to train the same classification model due to different computational resources. To tackle this problem, we propose a generalisation of knowledge distillation to merge HCs. We derive a probabilistic relation between the outputs of HCs and the probability over all classes. Based on this relation, we propose two classes of methods based on cross-entropy minimisation and matrix factorisation, which allow us to estimate soft labels over all classes from unlabelled samples and use them in lieu of ground truth labels to train a unified classifier. Our extensive experiments on ImageNet, LSUN, and Places365 datasets show that our approaches significantly outperform a naive extension of distillation and can achieve almost the same accuracy as classifiers that are trained in a centralised, supervised manner.

papers_seen.author: Ortiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, Applications, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a broad, mature toolkit for turning large, high-performing neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable models. Approaches vary from transferring softened outputs to aligning intermediate representations or relational structure, from online and multi-teacher schemes to data-free and privacy-aware pipelines. Empirical work across vision, language, speech, and other modalities shows that well-designed distillation can preserve most of a teacher's performance while delivering substantial reductions in inference cost, parameter count, and memory footprint. Practical success depends on matching distillation targets and schedules to student capacity and deployment constraints, handling limited or private data appropriately, and addressing robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift concerns.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Unifying Tool: Beyond Compression to Privacy, Robustness, Fairness, and Theory
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation began as a technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, faster models, but its utility now spans privacy-preserving training, robustness transfer, fairness mitigation, domain generalization, and theoretical insights about learning. Distillation can (1) produce compact models that retain most of a teacher's performance, (2) transfer nontrivial inductive biases and robustness properties, and (3) be adapted to settings with privacy constraints or imperfect teachers. However, distillation is not a panacea: teacher errors, choice of distilled data, and sample-level effects can harm the student unless carefully managed. This perspective synthesizes empirical and theoretical evidence to argue that knowledge distillation is a central, flexible methodology for modern deep learning, while highlighting practical constraints and directions for responsible application.

papers_seen.author: Bass
papers_seen.title: Position: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Paradigm for Model Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated not as a narrow compression trick but as a unifying, practical paradigm for producing compact, deployable models while preserving accuracy, robustness, and task-specific behavior. KD’s range—spanning soft-target supervision, intermediate representation matching, multi-teacher schedules, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and adversarial or curriculum-enhanced transfers—makes it uniquely suited to combine with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet real-world constraints. At the same time, KD requires careful design to handle teacher-student mismatch, low-frequency phenomena, domain shift, and data-availability or privacy limits; following representation-aware objectives, adaptive teacher strategies, and hybrid compression pipelines yields the most reliable results.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: TextKD-GAN: Text Generation using KnowledgeDistillation and Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Text generation is of particular interest in many NLP applications such as machine translation, language modeling, and text summarization. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) achieved a remarkable success in high quality image generation in computer vision,and recently, GANs have gained lots of interest from the NLP community as well. However, achieving similar success in NLP would be more challenging due to the discrete nature of text. In this work, we introduce a method using knowledge distillation to effectively exploit GAN setup for text generation. We demonstrate how autoencoders (AEs) can be used for providing a continuous representation of sentences, which is a smooth representation that assign non-zero probabilities to more than one word. We distill this representation to train the generator to synthesize similar smooth representations. We perform a number of experiments to validate our idea using different datasets and show that our proposed approach yields better performance in terms of the BLEU score and Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) measure compared to traditional GAN-based text generation approaches without pre-training.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for NLP: Efficacy, Best Practices, and Practical Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students in NLP. When applied with attention to what to transfer (logits, features, or layers), how to align teacher and student representations, and how to prepare data and student initialization, KD yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. However, distillation can propagate teacher errors, suffer from representation mismatch, and interact with privacy and robustness requirements—so practitioners must combine KD with complementary techniques and careful validation to meet real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques reduce large, high-performing neural models to smaller, more efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or structural relationships. Methods vary from matching softened teacher outputs to aligning intermediate features, using multi-teacher ensembles, training students with surrogate or synthesized data when originals are unavailable, and combining distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to map or align heterogeneous architectures, whether and how the student is pre-trained, and which data or augmentation strategies are used. While KD can recover much of a teacher's performance and enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, open issues remain around robustness, distributional shifts, teacher imperfections, and principled optimization theory.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structured signals. A wide variety of KD strategies—matching softened logits, aligning features or attention maps, multi-teacher schedules, and data- or task-aware augmentation—enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical success depends on what is distilled, student capacity and architecture alignment, availability and provenance of data, and task-specific constraints (e.g., robustness or federated heterogeneity). Carefully designed pipelines can preserve most teacher performance while substantially reducing resource cost, but KD also has important failure modes that motivate complementary techniques and careful engineering.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: The Practical Centrality and Limitations of Knowledge Distillation for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a primary tool for compressing large deep models into compact, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. KD has been applied across modalities and use-cases—distilling large language models into lightweight encoders, compressing ensembles into single predictors, enabling privacy- and device-aware deployments, and even operating without access to original training data. At the same time, theoretical gaps, data- and heterogeneity-driven failure modes, and teacher biases motivate hybrid strategies (multi-teacher, meta-learned teachers, data-free generators, and combined compression techniques) to realize KD’s full potential in practical systems.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Not Sufficient Tool for Compression and Deployment in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile technique for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller students, enabling substantial runtime, memory, and latency gains while preserving much of predictive performance. KD is effective across modalities and deployment regimes, but its success depends on careful method choice, teacher quality, data availability, and combination with complementary compression strategies. Future progress requires deeper theoretical understanding, better automation for heterogeneous and privacy-sensitive settings, and principled integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Adaptation: Teaching to Adapt
papers_seen.abstract: Domain adaptation is crucial in many real-world applications where the distribution of the training data differs from the distribution of the test data. Previous Deep Learning-based approaches to domain adaptation need to be trained jointly on source and target domain data and are therefore unappealing in scenarios where models need to be adapted to a large number of domains or where a domain is evolving, e.g. spam detection where attackers continuously change their tactics.   To fill this gap, we propose Knowledge Adaptation, an extension of Knowledge Distillation (Bucilua et al., 2006; Hinton et al., 2015) to the domain adaptation scenario. We show how a student model achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised domain adaptation from multiple sources on a standard sentiment analysis benchmark by taking into account the domain-specific expertise of multiple teachers and the similarities between their domains.   When learning from a single teacher, using domain similarity to gauge trustworthiness is inadequate. To this end, we propose a simple metric that correlates well with the teacher's accuracy in the target domain. We demonstrate that incorporating high-confidence examples selected by this metric enables the student model to achieve state-of-the-art performance in the single-source scenario.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and adaptable family of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster models suitable for deployment. Beyond the classic teacher-logit supervision, modern distillation covers feature-level matching, task-adaptive architecture search, multi-teacher transfer, and data-free scenarios. KD can be combined with pruning and structured sparsity, adapted for domain shifts, and used to transfer ensemble or task-specific knowledge into compact models. The choice of distillation target, the availability of data, and the deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy, domain) determine which distillation recipe will be most effective.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and broadly applicable strategy for compressing large models and transferring their capabilities to smaller or specialized models. KD can operate at multiple levels (logits, intermediate layers, and features), can be combined with model pruning and precision reduction, and can support domain adaptation and on-device deployment. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its success depends on how teacher knowledge is represented and transferred, the choice of data and augmentations used during distillation, and the deployment context (e.g., heterogeneous federated environments). When methods for intermediate-layer alignment, feature mimicking, data-side regularization, and architecture-aware mapping are combined thoughtfully, KD yields compact, efficient models that retain much of the teacher’s performance while enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Humphrey
papers_seen.title: Best Practices and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones across modalities (classification, sequence modeling, generation, graph-structured data, and federated systems). KD’s strengths arise not only from transferring teacher logits but also from transferring richer representation-level, adversarial, and self-derived signals. However, distillation has well-documented failure modes—optimization difficulties, propagation of teacher errors, and domain or device heterogeneity—that require specific remedies. Combining representation-level objectives, teacher-friendly training, self-distillation or teacher-free approaches, and careful data strategies yields more robust and efficient compressed models while avoiding common pitfalls.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Bowers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Variants
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger or multi-modal models into smaller, faster, or more private models. Across vision, speech, and NLP tasks, a consistent set of practices has emerged—logit/soft-label transfer, intermediate-layer matching, and task- or domain-specific adaptation—augmented by variants that address missing data, distributed training, privacy, and teacher-student mismatch. Empirical results show that distilled students can approach teacher accuracy while enjoying large gains in inference speed and memory, and recent work clarifies when and why distillation acts as an effective regularizer.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, faster models while retaining much of their performance. Across modalities and tasks—language understanding, machine translation, reading comprehension, and large-scale distributed training—recent work shows KD can improve inference speed, aid domain adaptation, enable training without original data, and increase robustness. Combining innovations in layer mapping, feature-level transfer, online and data-free techniques, and teacher optimization yields the best trade-offs for real deployments.
