papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Adaptation: Teaching to Adapt
papers_seen.abstract: Domain adaptation is crucial in many real-world applications where the distribution of the training data differs from the distribution of the test data. Previous Deep Learning-based approaches to domain adaptation need to be trained jointly on source and target domain data and are therefore unappealing in scenarios where models need to be adapted to a large number of domains or where a domain is evolving, e.g. spam detection where attackers continuously change their tactics.   To fill this gap, we propose Knowledge Adaptation, an extension of Knowledge Distillation (Bucilua et al., 2006; Hinton et al., 2015) to the domain adaptation scenario. We show how a student model achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised domain adaptation from multiple sources on a standard sentiment analysis benchmark by taking into account the domain-specific expertise of multiple teachers and the similarities between their domains.   When learning from a single teacher, using domain similarity to gauge trustworthiness is inadequate. To this end, we propose a simple metric that correlates well with the teacher's accuracy in the target domain. We demonstrate that incorporating high-confidence examples selected by this metric enables the student model to achieve state-of-the-art performance in the single-source scenario.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques enable deploying high-performing deep models under resource constraints by transferring information from large teacher models into smaller students. Approaches range from task-agnostic distillation and architecture search to layer-matching, internal representation imitation, data-free distillation, and techniques that adapt either the teacher or the student to improve transfer. Empirical work across vision and language shows these methods can substantially reduce model size and latency while retaining much of the original performance, and task- or domain-aware strategies often yield the best practical trade-offs. Remaining challenges include robustness without access to original data, aligning heterogeneous inputs or modalities, and automating compression for downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Ware
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical System for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential and practical approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a system—covering teacher design, the training signal, data and augmentation, and efficiency constraints—KD can retain much of a teacher's performance while meeting latency, memory, and domain requirements. However, its success depends on careful choices about teacher quality, distillation objectives, available data, and complementary compression techniques; awareness of these factors yields the most reliable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Travis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression: Evidence, Mechanisms, Limits, and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a central and practical toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across vision, generative modeling, and natural language processing. KD succeeds because it can transfer diverse signals—soft logits, intermediate representations, relational structure—and because those signals can be adapted to constraints such as data scarcity, architecture mismatch, or privacy. However, distillation is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align layers, how to prepare or synthesize data, and how to address teacher errors and optimization instabilities. The best outcomes arise from integrated distillation pipelines that combine representation-level objectives, careful data strategies (including augmentation or synthetic samples), architecture-aware mapping, and multi-stage or multi-teacher schedules tailored to the deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core and Its Limits for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD can transfer information at multiple levels (output logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or relational structure), be applied with or without original training data, and be combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet deployment constraints. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, the availability and nature of data, and how to handle heterogeneity or robustness concerns. A pragmatic KD protocol blends pre-training of compact architectures, appropriate choice of distillation signals, data strategies (including data-free methods when needed), and complementary compression techniques, while actively addressing teacher weighting and domain-shift risks.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Mathis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multifaceted Toolbox for Compression, Regularization, and Privacy in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a flexible, multi-purpose methodology rather than only a compression trick. KD enables smaller, efficient models for deployment, but it also serves as a mechanism for learned regularization, domain adaptation, and privacy-aware model release. Practical success relies on matching the distillation signals (soft targets, intermediate features, relations), the teacher selection and scheduling, and the data or data-generation strategy to the deployment constraints. Combining logits-based supervision with representation-level objectives, multi-stage or multi-teacher schedules, and privacy-aware query mechanisms produces more reliable and robust student models for real-world NLP and deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Toolchain for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and empirically effective paradigm for producing compact, resource-efficient models from larger teachers across computer vision, language, graph, and speech tasks. As a modular system, KD supports multiple information-transfer signals (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational structure), can operate with or without original training data, and composes naturally with complementary compression methods (quantization, pruning, and architecture search). Real-world deployment requires careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle limited or no access to teacher data, and how to address robustness and fairness concerns. When KD is applied as a deliberate toolchain—selecting task-aware objectives, incorporating multi-teacher or synthetic-data protocols, and combining with data- and model-level compression—practical students can approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Open problems remain around preserving rare-event behaviors, domain shift, and student-aware teacher shaping, which motivate focused research on curricula, data synthesis, and representation-aware objectives.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Moonshine: Distilling with Cheap Convolutions
papers_seen.abstract: Many engineers wish to deploy modern neural networks in memory-limited settings; but the development of flexible methods for reducing memory use is in its infancy, and there is little knowledge of the resulting cost-benefit. We propose structural model distillation for memory reduction using a strategy that produces a student architecture that is a simple transformation of the teacher architecture: no redesign is needed, and the same hyperparameters can be used. Using attention transfer, we provide Pareto curves/tables for distillation of residual networks with four benchmark datasets, indicating the memory versus accuracy payoff. We show that substantial memory savings are possible with very little loss of accuracy, and confirm that distillation provides student network performance that is better than training that student architecture directly on data.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Cross-modal Knowledge Distillation for Vision-to-Sensor Action Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) based on multi-modal approach has been recently shown to improve the accuracy performance of HAR. However, restricted computational resources associated with wearable devices, i.e., smartwatch, failed to directly support such advanced methods. To tackle this issue, this study introduces an end-to-end Vision-to-Sensor Knowledge Distillation (VSKD) framework. In this VSKD framework, only time-series data, i.e., accelerometer data, is needed from wearable devices during the testing phase. Therefore, this framework will not only reduce the computational demands on edge devices, but also produce a learning model that closely matches the performance of the computational expensive multi-modal approach. In order to retain the local temporal relationship and facilitate visual deep learning models, we first convert time-series data to two-dimensional images by applying the Gramian Angular Field ( GAF) based encoding method. We adopted ResNet18 and multi-scale TRN with BN-Inception as teacher and student network in this study, respectively. A novel loss function, named Distance and Angle-wised Semantic Knowledge loss (DASK), is proposed to mitigate the modality variations between the vision and the sensor domain. Extensive experimental results on UTD-MHAD, MMAct, and Berkeley-MHAD datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and competitiveness of the proposed VSKD model which can deployed on wearable sensors.

papers_seen.author: Zavala
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Limited Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach that enables deploying large models under resource, latency, and privacy constraints by transferring knowledge from teacher to student models. KD extends beyond simple logit matching to include representation-level transfer, attention- and feature-guided objectives, multi-teacher schedules, and integration with architecture search and pretraining. While KD reliably improves efficiency and can preserve many teacher behaviors, its success depends on choices of distillation targets, teacher preparation, student architecture, and data strategies; it can also amplify teacher errors or struggle under data heterogeneity, requiring complementary techniques and careful engineering for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Beyond in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a compression trick but a flexible paradigm that improves efficiency, robustness, privacy, and generalization across modalities and tasks. KD can compress large pretrained models into lightweight deployable models, transfer internal representations to preserve teacher behaviors, operate without original training data, and be adapted to distributed and privacy-sensitive settings. Recent methodological advances—layer- and attention-aware projection, multi-teacher schedules, meta-learned teachers, and techniques connecting KD to regularization—make distillation a practical and theoretically grounded tool for both research and production NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, language, graph learning, and distributed settings, KD variants—soft-target matching, representation- and relational-level supervision, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free or federated protocols—have enabled substantial reductions in model size and latency while often preserving much of teacher performance. Practical gains depend on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle limited, private, or heterogeneous data; consequently KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods and task-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Methods, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or costly models into smaller, faster models by transferring information from a teacher to a student. Research over the past decade shows multiple complementary mechanisms for effective distillation—soft-target supervision, feature and representation mimicking, layer-wise alignment, and task-aware selection of teacher knowledge. Practical advances adapt distillation to domain constraints (few-shot data, modality mismatch, federated or latency-constrained deployment) and model families (transformers, convolutional nets, graph neural networks, generative models). Empirical work demonstrates that thoughtful choices about what to transfer (logits vs. features vs. relations), how to align layers, and how to prepare data and pretraining substantially affect student performance, sometimes enabling students to match or even surpass teachers under resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Knowledge Distillation in NLP: Pre-training, Task-Awareness, Privacy, and Robustness
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large language models into smaller, faster students for NLP applications. Its effectiveness depends not only on the student-teacher framework but on complementary practices: pre-training compact models, aligning distilled signals to task-relevant representations, handling limited or private data, leveraging multiple teachers when available, and explicitly distilling for robustness. When these elements are combined and tuned, distillation yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile model-compression paradigm that transfers predictive behavior from larger (teacher) models to smaller (student) models. Work across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks has expanded KD beyond soft-label matching to include internal representation matching, layer mapping, feature attention, curriculum strategies, data-side techniques (including data-free methods and augmentation-aware KD), multi-teacher weighting, and task-specific adaptations. Empirical and theoretical analyses show that KD can act both as a conduit of teacher “dark knowledge” (similarity structure among classes) and as a regularizer related to label smoothing; practical improvements require matching the right kinds of knowledge (outputs, intermediate features, relational signals) and addressing mismatches in inputs, data distributions, and training curricula. Applications in NLP (e.g., retrieval, translation, spoken QA) illustrate how KD strategies must be adapted to task structure and data idiosyncrasies to preserve quality on low-frequency phenomena while achieving significant runtime and memory savings.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural relationships. A spectrum of techniques — matching softened outputs, aligning features or attention, layer-mapping (including many-to-many mappings), multi-teacher or ensemble transfers, and data-free or generator-based synthesis — enables large reductions in size and latency while largely preserving task performance. KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and careful data and training choices; but it faces practical challenges including capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and the potential transfer of teacher biases or adversarial vulnerabilities.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable method for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably reduces parameter counts and inference cost while preserving much teacher performance when paired with task-aware design choices and complementary compression techniques. Its success, however, depends on decisions about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, access to data or synthetic surrogates, and mitigation of robustness and distribution-shift failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Koch
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques seek to transfer predictive power from larger, high-capacity models (teachers or ensembles) into smaller, efficient models (students) while preserving accuracy and generalization. Approaches vary from matching teacher outputs (logits) to imitating intermediate representations, designing student-friendly teachers, handling limited or no access to original training data, and tailoring distillation to task-specific architectures (e.g., detection, reinforcement learning, recommender systems). Practical concerns include privacy, computational cost at training or inference, multi-teacher integration, and the role of pre-training for compact models. Empirical results across vision, language evaluation, medical imaging, recommender systems, and reinforcement learning show that appropriately chosen distillation objectives and training regimes can yield compact models that approach teacher performance while delivering large savings in storage and latency.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable method for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their accuracy. KD operates through multiple signals (soft logits, intermediate representations, relational structure) and is most effective when combined with task-aware data strategies and complementary compression methods. When designed with attention to what to transfer, how to align architectures, and how to handle limited or sensitive data, KD enables deployment of compact models across modalities and constraints while exposing important open questions about robustness, bias propagation, and distributional generalization.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Embracing the Dark Knowledge: Domain Generalization Using Regularized Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Though convolutional neural networks are widely used in different tasks, lack of generalization capability in the absence of sufficient and representative data is one of the challenges that hinder their practical application. In this paper, we propose a simple, effective, and plug-and-play training strategy named Knowledge Distillation for Domain Generalization (KDDG) which is built upon a knowledge distillation framework with the gradient filter as a novel regularization term. We find that both the ``richer dark knowledge" from the teacher network, as well as the gradient filter we proposed, can reduce the difficulty of learning the mapping which further improves the generalization ability of the model. We also conduct experiments extensively to show that our framework can significantly improve the generalization capability of deep neural networks in different tasks including image classification, segmentation, reinforcement learning by comparing our method with existing state-of-the-art domain generalization techniques. Last but not the least, we propose to adopt two metrics to analyze our proposed method in order to better understand how our proposed method benefits the generalization capability of deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Molina
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Practices, Limits, and Practical Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure so students can meet latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Practical KD combines choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention, relations), how to align teachers and students (layer mapping, pre-training, progressive replacement), and how to handle data (real, synthesized, or privacy-preserving) to retain much of teacher utility. While KD often yields substantial compression with modest performance loss, it faces predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, domain or data-shift, and propagation of teacher errors—so it is typically used together with complementary compression tools and careful data and training protocols.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression methods form a diverse toolkit for producing smaller, faster, or more deployable models while retaining much of the performance of larger teachers. Research spans soft-label and self-distillation strategies, layer- and representation-level transfers, architecture-aware and task-adaptive compression, and deployment-aware approaches that combine pruning, quantization, and distillation. Empirical work shows that careful choice of distillation signal (logits, intermediate representations, or feature maps), alignment strategy between teacher and student layers, data augmentation, and optimization scheduling materially affects student performance. Practical systems exploit these design choices to compress large pre-trained language models, accelerate inference, enable heterogeneous-device training, or improve low-precision networks. Despite progress, open questions remain about principled objective design, sample efficiency under limited data, and theory connecting transferred representations to generalization.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile tool for transferring functionality from large, expensive models to smaller, more efficient ones across modalities. When properly applied, KD can enable deployment of compact models with competitive accuracy, but its effectiveness depends on dataset complexity, selection of distilled signals, and complementary compression strategies. This paper synthesizes empirical findings and method-level advances to argue for principled, task-aware KD workflows that mitigate common pitfalls while maximizing compression gains.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable method for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. When applied thoughtfully—selecting what to transfer (logits, features, attention), aligning inputs and architectures, and combining KD with complementary compression (pruning, structured sparsity, quantization) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic samples, curriculum)—KD enables resource-efficient deployment across vision, language, multimodal, and federated settings. However, its success depends on teacher quality, data availability, and alignment between teacher and student; addressing these constraints through multi-teacher designs, black-box adaptation, and feature-level alignment remains essential for robust, private, and high-performance compression.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring useful predictive behavior and representations from a teacher to a student. Methods span matching teacher output distributions (soft labels), aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, adversarial or data-free approaches, and online or federated variants that trade communication and privacy constraints against fidelity. Practical success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to manage imperfect or heterogeneous data and devices, and whether to combine distillation with complementary compression strategies (e.g., pruning or architecture search). While distilled students often retain much of a teacher's performance and enable deployment under latency or resource constraints, open challenges include preserving rare-token behaviors, handling domain shift and robustness, and designing privacy- and communication-efficient protocols for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Tool for Model Compression and Deployment in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a compression trick but a core engineering technique that enables deployment, adaptation, privacy, and robustness for large neural models in real-world systems. By treating distillation as a family of methods—ranging from output soft-target transfer to feature- and layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, and privacy-aware protocols—practitioners can compress models while preserving task performance and satisfying latency, memory, and data-privacy constraints. Thoughtful application of KD, combined with complementary methods (pretraining, projector design, multi-stage schedules, and careful handling of teacher imperfections), yields compact models that are practical for production while exposing clear avenues for further research.

papers_seen.author: Gilbert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from matching softened logits to a flexible, task-aware toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. Modern distillation transfers output behavior, intermediate representations, relational structure, or ensemble knowledge; can operate with limited or no access to original training data; and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when adapted to deployment constraints such as latency, memory, privacy, and domain shift. Practical application requires matching the distillation recipe to task requirements, student capacity, and data availability while managing teacher imperfections and robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Component of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible approach for producing compact models from large teachers. When treated as a modular, task-aware system—combining soft-target supervision, intermediate representation matching, data and augmentation strategies, and complementary compression primitives—KD enables substantial reductions in latency and footprint while retaining most of the original performance. However, KD is not a panacea: its practical success requires careful attention to teacher–student alignment, data availability (including data-free or privacy-aware regimes), robustness to distribution shift and rare behaviors, and mitigation of transferred biases. I argue KD should be the default central tool in compression pipelines but used deliberately and in combination with other methods to meet deployment constraints and reliability requirements.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses larger, higher-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other learned structure. Across NLP and broader deep-learning tasks, a family of techniques—logit/soft-target matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, layer-wise mapping, multi-teacher and ensemble transfer, and data-free or generator-based synthesis—enable substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. Distillation is both a practical engineering toolkit for deployment constraints (latency, memory, heterogeneity, privacy) and an active research area that raises challenges around preserving robustness, handling domain and data shifts, and designing principled curricula and teacher signals for maximal downstream utility.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: The Central Role and Evolving Practices of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental and versatile approach for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP. It enables compact, efficient student models that retain much of a teacher's performance, supports deployment on resource-constrained devices, and can be adapted to privacy-sensitive or distributed settings. Recent advances extend distillation beyond simple logits matching to many-to-many layer mapping, task-adaptive compression, teacher-aware training, adversarial and data-free scenarios, and robustness-aware objectives. Together these developments show that distillation is both a practical engineering tool and a rich research paradigm for addressing capacity, data availability, privacy, and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central, Practical, and Best Used as an Integrated, Multi‑Level Strategy
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable toolkit for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD works best when it goes beyond naive logits-only matching and integrates representation-level transfer, input-side interventions, robustness-aware objectives, and complementary compression methods. However, effective deployment requires careful teacher–student co-design, attention to data provenance and augmentation, explicit handling of teacher uncertainty and bias, and privacy-aware training choices. Treated as a flexible, multi-stage pipeline rather than a single recipe, KD enables substantial efficiency gains while managing the key failure modes that emerge in real-world settings.

papers_seen.author: Hickman
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation for Compressing Deep Models in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central tool to make large deep models practical: it reduces model size and latency, enables domain adaptation, preserves privacy and scalability, and can even improve robustness when applied carefully. Successful deployments balance which teacher signals are transferred (logits, features, attention or answers), how they are aligned (layer-wise, projector-mediated, task-aware filters), and the training setup (multi-teacher, online, or adversarial). I argue that a principled combination of feature-level guidance, task-aware selection, and appropriate distillation architecture gives the best tradeoffs for NLP deployment: it preserves downstream performance while enabling orders-of-magnitude gains in speed, capacity, and deployability.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Nuanced Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely adopted approach for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. KD operates through multiple mechanisms—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, and transferring relational or attention patterns—and often yields substantial improvements in latency, memory, and deployability relative to naive student training. However, distillation is not a turnkey solution: its effectiveness depends on what is transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, data availability and privacy constraints, and whether complementary compression methods are applied. Viewed as a toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables flexible, task-aware compression pipelines that can be adapted to real-world constraints while acknowledging remaining limits around robustness, data-free operation, and principled teacher selection.

papers_seen.author: Ortiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, Applications, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a broad, mature toolkit for turning large, high-performing neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable models. Approaches vary from transferring softened outputs to aligning intermediate representations or relational structure, from online and multi-teacher schemes to data-free and privacy-aware pipelines. Empirical work across vision, language, speech, and other modalities shows that well-designed distillation can preserve most of a teacher's performance while delivering substantial reductions in inference cost, parameter count, and memory footprint. Practical success depends on matching distillation targets and schedules to student capacity and deployment constraints, handling limited or private data appropriately, and addressing robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift concerns.

papers_seen.author: Merritt
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Deployment-First System: Strengths, Limits, and Practical Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, modality-agnostic technique for turning large, high-performing models into compact, deployable students. When treated as a system—covering teacher design, selection of distilled signals, data strategies, and complementary compression methods—KD enables substantial reductions in size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. However, its success is conditional on choices of what to transfer (logits, features, attention, or structural behavior), student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthesis, and task-aware training procedures. Effective compression therefore requires distillation objectives and pipelines matched to the deployment constraints and to the nature of the teacher and task.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other learned structure. A broad family of techniques—soft-target (logit) matching, representation- and layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher and ensemble transfer, architecture-aware transformations, and data-free or generator-based synthesis—has been developed to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical and theoretical work shows distillation often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices, but effectiveness depends on choices about what is transferred, teacher and student architecture, data availability, and optimization. Practical pipelines combine distillation with complementary methods (pretraining of compact models, data augmentation, pruning/quantization, and task-aware objectives) and must address challenges such as capacity mismatch, domain shift, robustness preservation, and faithful transfer of rare behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Flexible Core Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not a single recipe but a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large models into compact students suitable for deployment. When combined with task-aware architecture choices, ensemble or self-generated signals, and orthogonal compression methods, KD reliably reduces inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Careful attention to what is distilled, data strategy, and training dynamics mitigates common failure modes and enables robust, real-world compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central practical mechanism to compress large neural models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment in resource-, latency-, or privacy-constrained settings. Research has developed a family of distillation objectives (soft logits, feature/representation matching, relational/correlation losses), training schedules (multi-stage, multi-teacher, self-distillation), and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or distilled corpora, data-free queries) that, when combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), enable compact models to recover much of the original performance. Success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to map teacher and student representations, and how to adapt pretraining and task data to the student’s capacity; remaining challenges include domain shift, teacher–student mismatch, low-frequency behavior in NLP, and privacy-aware distillation.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are mature, diverse strategies to reduce the computational and memory costs of large deep models while retaining much of their task performance. Approaches span architecture-level methods that search or prune for compact student networks, training-time methods that transfer dark knowledge via logits or intermediate representations, and data-centric methods that operate when original training data are unavailable. Empirical work shows success compressing large language models into lightweight networks for NLP tasks, highlights task- and data-specific pitfalls (notably for low-frequency tokens in sequence tasks), and motivates specialized extensions in federated and domain-adaptive settings. Theory and interpretive analyses have begun to clarify why distillation helps generalization and optimization, and recent work advocates shaping teachers to be more student-friendly or designing student-aware compression procedures. Overall, the literature shows a practical toolkit of complementary techniques—task-adaptive architecture search, feature- and attention-based matching, adversarial or synthetic-data distillation, and teacher-student co-training—each with trade-offs between efficiency, robustness, and fidelity to teacher behavior.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable method for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. When applied thoughtfully—selecting what to transfer (logits, features, attention), aligning inputs and architectures, and combining KD with complementary compression (pruning, structured sparsity, quantization) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic samples, curriculum)—KD enables resource-efficient deployment across vision, language, multimodal, and federated settings. However, its success depends on teacher quality, data availability, and alignment between teacher and student; addressing these constraints through multi-teacher designs, black-box adaptation, and feature-level alignment remains essential for robust, private, and high-performance compression.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural knowledge. Methods span matching softened output distributions, feature- and attention-level imitation, layer mapping and progressive module replacement, channel- and module-aware transfers, and data-free or generative approaches for when original training data are unavailable. Practical pipelines combine KD with quantization, low-precision training, pruning, or architecture transformations and often rely on staged or adaptive teacher-student schedules. Empirical evidence shows KD can yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance across vision and NLP tasks, but success depends on teacher quality, what and which samples are distilled, data availability, and careful engineering of interfaces between heterogeneous teacher and student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Horton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: A Central, Practical Tool with Clear Limits and Best-Practice Remedies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and NLP. When applied thoughtfully—choosing what knowledge to transfer, preparing or pretraining students, and combining KD with complementary compression primitives—distillation often yields compact models that recover much of teacher performance while meeting latency and memory constraints. However, KD is not a universal solution: optimization difficulties, teacher–student capacity mismatch, limited or mismatched data, privacy constraints, and the risk of transferring undesirable behaviors (biases, adversarial weaknesses) remain important concerns. A pragmatic approach treats KD as a flexible toolkit to be combined with targeted architectural, data, and objective choices that address these failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Castaneda
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: An Integrated, Task-Aware Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical engine of model compression for deep learning and NLP when it is applied as an integrated, task-aware system. By combining soft-target transfer with representation-level alignment, targeted feature mimicking, data strategies (including synthesis when data are unavailable), and architecture-aware student design, practitioners can produce compact models that preserve much of the teacher’s utility while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD’s benefits are conditional: student capacity, data availability and complexity, architecture mismatch, and teacher artifacts limit outcomes unless addressed through deliberate pipeline choices and evaluation. This paper argues for a pragmatic KD-centered workflow and highlights key components and cautionary considerations for reliable compression in real-world settings.

papers_seen.author: Ibarra
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from matching soft teacher outputs into a flexible toolkit for producing compact, efficient models across vision and language. Empirical and methodological work shows KD can transfer final predictions, intermediate representations, relational structure, and inductive biases from large teachers to smaller students, and it is often most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when adapted to data constraints (real-data, augmented, or data-free regimes). Practical success depends on choices about distillation targets, teacher-student alignment, and data; remaining challenges include teacher imperfections, distributional mismatch, and preserving robustness and fairness under compression.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: The Case for Practical, Adaptive Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible tool for compressing large deep learning models into deployable students. Recent work shows KD can both directly reduce model size and serve as a mechanism to transfer inductive biases, intermediate representations, and task-specific attention. However, real-world constraints — limited or private training data, domain and client heterogeneity, and redundant teacher representations — require KD methods that are data-free, adversarially robust, task-aware, and selective about what teacher knowledge to transfer.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods transfer knowledge from larger or ensembles of models to smaller, more efficient models. Across computer vision, natural language processing, and generative modeling, research has developed many variants: prediction-level soft-target transfer, layer- and representation-level supervision, multi-teacher and ensemble distillation, online and data-free distillation, and privacy-preserving compression. Empirical work shows that these approaches can substantially reduce model size and inference cost with modest loss in task performance, but practical success depends on alignment between teacher and student capacity, careful choice of what and how to transfer, and the availability (or absence) of original training data. Theoretical and empirical analyses highlight optimization and capacity gaps that limit perfect imitation, motivate task-aware and attention-guided transfers, and point to trade-offs when teachers are imperfect. Remaining challenges include principled teacher selection and weighting, robust data-free distillation, and reconciling compression with privacy and fairness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Koch
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques seek to transfer predictive power from larger, high-capacity models (teachers or ensembles) into smaller, efficient models (students) while preserving accuracy and generalization. Approaches vary from matching teacher outputs (logits) to imitating intermediate representations, designing student-friendly teachers, handling limited or no access to original training data, and tailoring distillation to task-specific architectures (e.g., detection, reinforcement learning, recommender systems). Practical concerns include privacy, computational cost at training or inference, multi-teacher integration, and the role of pre-training for compact models. Empirical results across vision, language evaluation, medical imaging, recommender systems, and reinforcement learning show that appropriately chosen distillation objectives and training regimes can yield compact models that approach teacher performance while delivering large savings in storage and latency.

papers_seen.author: Soto
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for compressing large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students for deployment in resource-, latency-, or privacy-constrained environments. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while providing additional benefits such as implicit regularization, improved robustness in some settings, domain adaptation, and enabling training when original data are unavailable. A practical KD pipeline selects what to transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, relational structure), how to supply data (real, augmented, synthesized, or data-free), and how to align teacher and student architectures; combining KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) typically yields the best trade-offs. Remaining challenges include handling teacher–student capacity mismatch, domain and distributional shift, optimization stability, preservation of low-frequency behaviors in NLP, and privacy constraints, which motivate hybrid, task-aware distillation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Methods, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring behavioral and representational signals from teachers. KD includes diverse techniques — soft-target supervision, intermediate feature and attention matching, layer-mapping strategies, online and ensemble-to-single transfers, and selective sample or data-aware procedures — that are adapted to task, architecture, and deployment constraints. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and appropriate data strategies, KD can yield compact models that retain most teacher performance; however, success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, and data availability.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, faster models while retaining much of their performance. Across modalities and tasks—language understanding, machine translation, reading comprehension, and large-scale distributed training—recent work shows KD can improve inference speed, aid domain adaptation, enable training without original data, and increase robustness. Combining innovations in layer mapping, feature-level transfer, online and data-free techniques, and teacher optimization yields the best trade-offs for real deployments.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Current Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely used set of techniques for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models to compact students. Across vision, language, speech, multimodal, and graph domains, KD has been adapted into many variants — matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, progressive module replacement, online/multi-teacher training, and data-free or privacy-aware pipelines — often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows distilled students can recover much of teacher performance when distillation targets, student preparation, and data strategies are chosen carefully. At the same time, KD’s effectiveness is limited by teacher quality, data availability or privacy, teacher–student architectural mismatch, and risks of transferring undesirable teacher behaviors. Practical deployment benefits from combining KD with complementary compression and data strategies, designing student-aware teacher signals, and accounting for robustness and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Backbone of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical, flexible, and empirically effective family of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. Across modalities and deployment constraints, KD enables moving from research-stage, high-capacity architectures to resource-efficient models suitable for latency- and privacy-constrained production. Realizing KD's full potential requires attention to teacher quality, data and domain mismatches, and scalability; appropriate choices—representation-level objectives, multi-teacher signals, online protocols, and privacy-aware distillation—address these challenges and make KD a core tool for applied deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Turner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. A family of methods—matching teacher soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational structure, and synthesizing or selecting data—enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. Success in real systems depends on task-aware design, careful teacher–student pairing, handling limited or private data, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search.
