papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Advances
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic for shrinking large models into a principled and versatile toolkit for compressing, adapting, and scaling deep models in NLP. By transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure from a teacher to a student, KD enables high-quality, resource-efficient models that meet latency and capacity constraints while preserving task performance. Recent work demonstrates KD variants that are task-adaptive, layer-aware, many-to-many, online, and even teacher-free, making KD applicable across domain adaptation, multi-tasking, multimodality, and large-scale distributed training. This paper argues that KD should be viewed not merely as a compression trick but as a unifying framework that links theoretical insights, practical training strategies, and system-level considerations for deploying compact NLP models.

papers_seen.author: Travis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression: Evidence, Mechanisms, Limits, and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a central and practical toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across vision, generative modeling, and natural language processing. KD succeeds because it can transfer diverse signals—soft logits, intermediate representations, relational structure—and because those signals can be adapted to constraints such as data scarcity, architecture mismatch, or privacy. However, distillation is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align layers, how to prepare or synthesize data, and how to address teacher errors and optimization instabilities. The best outcomes arise from integrated distillation pipelines that combine representation-level objectives, careful data strategies (including augmentation or synthetic samples), architecture-aware mapping, and multi-stage or multi-teacher schedules tailored to the deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: Joyce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Settings, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable deployment of high-performing deep models in latency- or resource-constrained settings by transferring knowledge from larger “teacher” models or ensembles to smaller “student” models. Work in this area spans methods that match final outputs, intermediate representations, or relational structure; approaches that adapt teacher signals through meta-learning or task-aware filters; and specializations for settings such as vision–language, graph learning, federated or distributed training, and data-free scenarios. Empirical results show KD can yield large efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance, but practical success depends on handling domain shift, architectural mismatch, heterogeneous data and devices, and the quality or calibration of teacher outputs. Important theoretical and statistical analyses have begun to clarify when and why distillation helps, but open problems remain around robust, privacy-preserving, and architecture-agnostic distillation for production systems.

papers_seen.author: Holmes
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Over the past decade KD has expanded from soft-label (logit) matching to a toolkit that includes intermediate representation and attention matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and zero-shot protocols, and integrations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD reliably reduces inference cost and enables on-device or latency-constrained deployment when its signals, data strategy, and architecture alignment are chosen to match task and deployment constraints, but it has well-documented limitations related to teacher imperfections, capacity mismatch, data scarcity, and distributional shifts.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Multifaceted Paradigm for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central, flexible paradigm for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD is most effective when combined with complementary practices—pretraining compact architectures, aligning intermediate representations, selecting or synthesizing appropriate distillation data, and using multi-teacher or staged schedules. While KD can yield compact models that approach teacher performance and enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, its success requires deliberate design to mitigate capacity mismatch, data provenance issues, and the risk of propagating teacher errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Engine for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has matured from a heuristic into a set of principled, modality-agnostic techniques that enable deployment of high-capacity models in resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings. By transferring predictive behaviour and internal representations from large teachers to compact students, distillation preserves much of the teacher's utility while enabling large speed, memory, and communication gains. Recent advances show that combining representation-level matching, teacher–student co-design, data-free synthesis, and task-adaptive compression yields robust, practical pipelines for compressing models across vision, language, graph, and federated settings.

papers_seen.author: Carr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, general-purpose approach for translating large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. Across architectures, modalities, and deployment constraints, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of the teacher's performance; however, realizing those gains in practice requires matching the distillation formulation to data availability, model mismatch, and robustness requirements.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or multi-modal deep models into smaller, more deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or other structured knowledge. Work across vision, speech, and NLP shows a range of mechanisms (soft-label matching, internal-representation matching, layer mapping, and feature/attention guidance) and adaptations for limited or private data. Empirical results indicate distilled students can approach teacher accuracy while greatly reducing size and inference cost, but effectiveness depends on what knowledge is distilled, how it is represented, and the training regime.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression strategies enable deployment of large pretrained models by transferring function or representation from larger (teacher) models to smaller (student) ones. Across supervised, self-supervised, and data-free settings, KD methods exploit soft targets, intermediate representation matching, architectural surgery, and data or training-time modifications to improve student accuracy, robustness, or efficiency. Empirical results show that appropriately designed distillation can retain most teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in model size, precision, or inference cost; but effectiveness depends on choices of targets, data, and teacher-student compatibility. Open challenges include preserving rare-token behavior in distilled NLP models, mitigating bias transfer, and jointly optimizing hardware constraints and task performance.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, but Nuanced Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically proven approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones while preserving much of their performance. KD can operate at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate features, relational structure) and be combined with complementary compression techniques, data synthesis, or student-aware teacher training to meet deployment constraints in vision, language, and graph domains. However, its success depends on careful design choices — what to transfer, how to map teacher and student layers, how to handle limited or private data, and whether to adapt the teacher — and practitioners should treat KD as part of a broader compression toolkit rather than a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Estes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Toolbox: Principles, Limits, and Practical Prescriptions for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation should be understood and applied as a flexible set of techniques that go well beyond simple parameter compression. When treated as a toolbox—combining soft-target supervision, internal representation matching, layer-aware alignment, attention-guided mapping, and complementary compression methods—distillation can produce compact models that preserve accuracy, improve interpretability, and transfer robustness or privacy properties. Success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to prepare the student, and how to mitigate propagation of teacher defects; practitioners benefit from system-level designs that pair distillation objectives with pre-training, data augmentation, and architecture-aware compression.

papers_seen.author: Valdez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile technique for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones while preserving much of their predictive performance. KD has matured beyond simple output-matching into a family of methods that transfer intermediate representations, attention or channel-wise signals, and task-specific inductive biases; it can operate under data scarcity or privacy constraints and can be combined with architecture search or other compression primitives to produce deployment-ready models. Successful application requires matching the distillation recipe to the task, student capacity, and deployment constraints and managing teacher imperfections and data mismatches.

papers_seen.author: Velasquez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multifaceted Tool Beyond Simple Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be understood and applied as a flexible toolbox rather than merely a compression trick. KD enables compression, regularization, privacy-preserving transfer, and adaptation across diverse constraints (data scarcity, heterogeneous devices, federated settings). Effective practice combines soft-target supervision with representation-level alignment, architecture-aware methods (pruning, quantization, search), and privacy-aware or teacher-free variants. However, careful design is required to avoid capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, and robustness or bias degradation.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for transferring information from larger, often over-parameterized teacher models into smaller, faster student models to enable deployment under constraints of latency, memory, data access, or privacy. KD techniques span output-level supervision (soft logits), intermediate representation matching, multi-teacher and ensemble strategies, self- and progressive distillation, and data-free or zero-shot variants. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance across modalities (vision, speech, translation, detection, and generation) while enabling on-device and real-time use; success depends on the choice of distillation targets, the match between teacher and student capacity, the availability and quality of data, and appropriate regularization or augmentation during training. Practical deployment typically combines KD with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and privacy-aware mechanisms to produce robust compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for NLP: Efficacy, Best Practices, and Practical Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students in NLP. When applied with attention to what to transfer (logits, features, or layers), how to align teacher and student representations, and how to prepare data and student initialization, KD yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. However, distillation can propagate teacher errors, suffer from representation mismatch, and interact with privacy and robustness requirements—so practitioners must combine KD with complementary techniques and careful validation to meet real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Nunez
papers_seen.title: Beyond Compression: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Practical, Private, and Robust Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is often framed narrowly as a model-compression trick to shrink large neural networks. This paper argues KD should instead be viewed as a core engineering and scientific tool for practical deployment: it enables training with limited or private data, yields task- and domain-adaptive compact models, improves robustness and fairness, and transfers intermediate representations and attention patterns that standard supervised training cannot. We synthesize evidence from recent work to show how variants of KD—self-distillation, layer-wise projection, multi-teacher schemes, teacher annealing, and data-free distillation—address concrete deployment challenges in vision and NLP, and we derive practical recommendations for combining these techniques in real systems.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring information from a teacher model. Across computer vision, language, graph, and healthcare applications, KD variants augment or replace naive logit matching with feature/hint matching, data augmentation, layer mapping strategies, and data-free or privacy-aware mechanisms. Practical work emphasizes task-adaptive compression, many-to-many layer alignment for pre-trained transformers, and the use of synthetic or mixed inputs to improve student generalization. At the same time, theoretical and empirical studies highlight limitations under data heterogeneity and imperfect teachers, motivating hybrid losses that mix soft and hard labels and methods that control privacy leakage during distillation.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Evidence
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring behavior, internal representations, or relational structure. It is a flexible, modality-agnostic toolkit that can be adapted to constraints such as limited data, privacy, latency, and heterogeneous architectures. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance when combined with representation matching, multi-teacher strategies, data synthesis, or architecture-aware design, but success depends on careful alignment of teacher signals, student capacity, and data strategies. Remaining challenges include optimization stability, capacity mismatch, and avoiding transfer of teacher errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible, practical toolkit for producing compact, deployable deep models across vision and natural language tasks. KD encompasses matching teacher outputs, aligning internal representations, leveraging multi-teacher or online schedules, and using data-side strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free generation). When combined with architecture-aware design and complementary compression methods, KD often yields students that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Remaining challenges center on teacher–student mismatch, data availability, robustness, and the potential transfer of undesirable biases.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques have been widely adopted to reduce model size and runtime while retaining performance. Work across vision, language, and multimodal tasks shows multiple complementary strategies—logit matching, feature mimicking, layer-wise alignment, progressive module replacement, and self-distillation—can be effective alone or in combination. Practical success depends on choices about teacher strength, student architecture, pre-training, and optimization, and recent systems integrate distillation with pruning, low-precision, and architecture search to meet deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Oliver
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core of Model Compression: Effectiveness, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and NLP. When combined with complementary practices—task-aware signal selection, intermediate representation alignment, pretraining for compact architectures, multi-teacher or self-distillation, and data augmentation or synthesis—KD can yield compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency and resource constraints. However, KD is not a universal solution: data availability, teacher–student heterogeneity, fairness concerns, and theoretical gaps constrain its effectiveness in some settings. Careful design choices and hybrid pipelines are therefore required to realize reliable compression in production systems.

papers_seen.author: Carrillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Design-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a flexible toolbox—combining softened-output supervision with representation-level alignment, teacher design, and complementary compression techniques—KD reliably reduces model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. At the same time, KD is not automatic: its success depends on what is distilled, student capacity, data availability, and targeted interventions to address robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Toolkit for Reliable Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a composable toolkit—combining soft-target transfer, representation-level matching, data augmentation, selective sample strategies, and multi-teacher or federated adaptations—KD can produce efficient models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. However, KD has known failure modes (teacher error propagation, data- and device-heterogeneity, and sample-wise regularization effects) that require explicit remedies and system-level design choices to ensure robust transfer.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Variants, and Practical Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring aspects of the teacher’s predictive behavior and internal representations. A diverse set of methods—matching output distributions, aligning intermediate features, progressive module replacement, multi-teacher and data-free schemes, and task- or domain-aware adaptations—has been developed to address deployment constraints such as latency, memory, data availability, privacy, and multimodal inputs. Empirical work shows that when the distillation recipe is matched to model architectures, data conditions, and deployment constraints, students can retain much of the teacher’s performance while offering practical efficiency gains; however, trade-offs and open challenges remain around robustness, domain shift, and faithful transfer of rare or fine-grained behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Payne
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, central tool for model compression in modern deep learning and NLP pipelines because it reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teachers to smaller, deployable students. When KD is designed as a system—combined with representation-level objectives, data strategies, multi-teacher signals, and complementary compression methods—it delivers large practical wins in latency, memory, and deployability while preserving most task performance. Responsible use requires attention to teacher–student alignment, data availability and privacy, and mitigation of transferred errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large, high-capacity models (teachers) into smaller, more efficient models (students). Across vision and language, practitioners combine KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, architectural design, and quantization) and with strategies for scarce or missing data to obtain deployable models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical success depends on choices about what to transfer (soft targets, features, attention), how to align heterogeneous architectures, the role of pre-training for compact models, and mechanisms to preserve robustness and rare-token behaviors. Data-free distillation, multi-task or multi-teacher schemes, and targeted representation matching extend KD’s applicability to many real-world settings.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, but Nuanced Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically proven approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones while preserving much of their performance. KD can operate at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate features, relational structure) and be combined with complementary compression techniques, data synthesis, or student-aware teacher training to meet deployment constraints in vision, language, and graph domains. However, its success depends on careful design choices — what to transfer, how to map teacher and student layers, how to handle limited or private data, and whether to adapt the teacher — and practitioners should treat KD as part of a broader compression toolkit rather than a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Rubio
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical, and Context-Aware Toolkit for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and practically proven approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. As a toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD encompasses soft-targets, intermediate representation matching, attention- and layer-aware mappings, multi- and online-teacher schemes, and data-aware protocols (including data-free and few-shot variants). KD delivers strong efficiency–performance tradeoffs when paired with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search, but its benefits depend on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or private data. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the central, adaptable component of compression pipelines while recognizing its limits and prescribing evidence-based design practices for robust, task-aware deployment.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques have been widely adopted to reduce model size and runtime while retaining performance. Work across vision, language, and multimodal tasks shows multiple complementary strategies—logit matching, feature mimicking, layer-wise alignment, progressive module replacement, and self-distillation—can be effective alone or in combination. Practical success depends on choices about teacher strength, student architecture, pre-training, and optimization, and recent systems integrate distillation with pruning, low-precision, and architecture search to meet deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile technique that enables compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teachers' performance. When combined with complementary practices — pre-training compact architectures, aligning intermediate representations, data-centric augmentation, privacy-aware protocols, and task-aware loss design — distillation yields efficient models suitable for real-world NLP and multimodal deployments. However, KD is not a silver bullet: optimization difficulties, capacity mismatch, and data limitations require careful method choices and evaluation. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a central, pragmatic engine of model compression, but one that must be applied with principled, task-aware adjustments to achieve reliable gains in practice.

papers_seen.author: Crosby
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, faster ones by transferring information from one or more teacher models to a student model. Methods range from matching output distributions (soft logits) to aligning internal representations, using ensembles or multiple teachers, conducting distillation without access to original data, and employing self-distillation or teacher-adaptation strategies. Empirical work across vision and language shows that careful choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to manage data constraints determine the trade-offs between efficiency, accuracy, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Manning
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Nuanced Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for creating compact, deployable models from large teachers. When treated as a configurable toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables significant reductions in memory, compute, and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. Its success depends on careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to manage data (real, augmented, or synthesized), and how KD is integrated with complementary compression methods. KD is powerful for production constraints but must be applied with task-aware design to avoid propagating teacher weaknesses or failing under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: TextKD-GAN: Text Generation using KnowledgeDistillation and Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Text generation is of particular interest in many NLP applications such as machine translation, language modeling, and text summarization. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) achieved a remarkable success in high quality image generation in computer vision,and recently, GANs have gained lots of interest from the NLP community as well. However, achieving similar success in NLP would be more challenging due to the discrete nature of text. In this work, we introduce a method using knowledge distillation to effectively exploit GAN setup for text generation. We demonstrate how autoencoders (AEs) can be used for providing a continuous representation of sentences, which is a smooth representation that assign non-zero probabilities to more than one word. We distill this representation to train the generator to synthesize similar smooth representations. We perform a number of experiments to validate our idea using different datasets and show that our proposed approach yields better performance in terms of the BLEU score and Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) measure compared to traditional GAN-based text generation approaches without pre-training.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.author: Deleon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transform large, high-performing models into smaller, faster, or more private students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structured signals. Over the past decade these methods have evolved from logits-based soft-label transfer to a wide range of strategies including feature- and attention-matching, layer-wise alignment, progressive module replacement, data-free and privacy-preserving protocols, and adaptations for few-shot or federated settings. Empirical work shows that properly designed distillation pipelines can retain much of teacher performance while substantially reducing model size and inference cost; however, effectiveness depends on what is distilled, student capacity, data availability, and practical constraints such as privacy, communication, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: Practical Principles for Effective Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. While classic distillation focuses on matching teacher output probabilities, practical compression across modalities and tasks benefits from richer transfer mechanisms: aligning internal representations, selecting task-relevant signals, leveraging data augmentation or synthetic data when real data are scarce, and using adversarial or ensemble strategies to expose diverse and robust teacher knowledge. When combined thoughtfully these methods enable students that are much smaller and faster while retaining or even improving accuracy and robustness on downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Flexible Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated not as a single recipe but as a flexible toolkit: it can transfer logits, internal representations, or structured relational knowledge; it can be combined with architecture search, multi-teacher schemes, or data synthesis; and it can be adapted with task-aware filtering or teacher-aware training to address capacity mismatch and deployment constraints. Carefully chosen distillation targets, appropriate data strategies, and complementary compression components produce small, deployable models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, or privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Not Sufficient Tool for Compression and Deployment in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile technique for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller students, enabling substantial runtime, memory, and latency gains while preserving much of predictive performance. KD is effective across modalities and deployment regimes, but its success depends on careful method choice, teacher quality, data availability, and combination with complementary compression strategies. Future progress requires deeper theoretical understanding, better automation for heterogeneous and privacy-sensitive settings, and principled integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central Tool That Must Be Used as a Toolkit for Reliable Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a vital method for turning large, high-performing deep models into smaller, deployable students. Empirical work across vision, speech, and NLP shows that matching teacher outputs and internal signals can yield students that recover much of teacher accuracy while delivering large gains in latency, memory, and energy. However, KD is not a single recipe: practical success depends on which teacher signals are transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, what data are used (real, augmented, or synthetic), and whether distillation is combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Careful, task-aware design and hybrid pipelines are therefore required to realize robust, production-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible, empirically effective toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring teacher behavior through output probabilities, intermediate representations, or structured signals and by combining distillation with data strategies and complementary compression primitives, practitioners can achieve large reductions in memory, latency, and compute while retaining most of the original performance. However, realizing these gains in real systems requires attention to data availability, teacher–student alignment, fairness and bias risks, and task- or hardware-aware design choices.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Lin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques are central tools for converting large, high-performing deep models into smaller, faster models that are practical for deployment. A broad repertoire of methods exists—matching soft logits, aligning intermediate representations, adversarial and online co-training, and data- or task-aware augmentation—often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical evidence shows distilled students can recover much of teacher performance across vision, speech, and language tasks, but success depends on how teacher signals are represented, what data are used, and how architecture or domain mismatches are addressed. Practical deployment requires attention to data availability, privacy or federated constraints, teacher errors, and optimization stability; promising directions include pre-training compact students, online and federated distillation protocols, and specialized layer- or modality-aware objectives.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Distilling Object Detectors with Fine-grained Feature Imitation
papers_seen.abstract: State-of-the-art CNN based recognition models are often computationally prohibitive to deploy on low-end devices. A promising high level approach tackling this limitation is knowledge distillation, which let small student model mimic cumbersome teacher model's output to get improved generalization. However, related methods mainly focus on simple task of classification while do not consider complex tasks like object detection. We show applying the vanilla knowledge distillation to detection model gets minor gain. To address the challenge of distilling knowledge in detection model, we propose a fine-grained feature imitation method exploiting the cross-location discrepancy of feature response. Our intuition is that detectors care more about local near object regions. Thus the discrepancy of feature response on the near object anchor locations reveals important information of how teacher model tends to generalize. We design a novel mechanism to estimate those locations and let student model imitate the teacher on them to get enhanced performance. We first validate the idea on a developed lightweight toy detector which carries simplest notion of current state-of-the-art anchor based detection models on challenging KITTI dataset, our method generates up to 15% boost of mAP for the student model compared to the non-imitated counterpart. We then extensively evaluate the method with Faster R-CNN model under various scenarios with common object detection benchmark of Pascal VOC and COCO, imitation alleviates up to 74% performance drop of student model compared to teacher. Codes released at https://github.com/twangnh/Distilling-Object-Detectors

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: SEED: Self-supervised Distillation For Visual Representation
papers_seen.abstract: This paper is concerned with self-supervised learning for small models. The problem is motivated by our empirical studies that while the widely used contrastive self-supervised learning method has shown great progress on large model training, it does not work well for small models. To address this problem, we propose a new learning paradigm, named SElf-SupErvised Distillation (SEED), where we leverage a larger network (as Teacher) to transfer its representational knowledge into a smaller architecture (as Student) in a self-supervised fashion. Instead of directly learning from unlabeled data, we train a student encoder to mimic the similarity score distribution inferred by a teacher over a set of instances. We show that SEED dramatically boosts the performance of small networks on downstream tasks. Compared with self-supervised baselines, SEED improves the top-1 accuracy from 42.2% to 67.6% on EfficientNet-B0 and from 36.3% to 68.2% on MobileNet-v3-Large on the ImageNet-1k dataset.

papers_seen.author: Holmes
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Over the past decade KD has expanded from soft-label (logit) matching to a toolkit that includes intermediate representation and attention matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and zero-shot protocols, and integrations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD reliably reduces inference cost and enables on-device or latency-constrained deployment when its signals, data strategy, and architecture alignment are chosen to match task and deployment constraints, but it has well-documented limitations related to teacher imperfections, capacity mismatch, data scarcity, and distributional shifts.

papers_seen.author: Hodges
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Capabilities, Limitations, and Practical Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. Across vision, language, multimodal, and graph domains, KD variants enable deployment on resource-constrained devices, speed up training at scale, and allow transfer of robustness or domain expertise when carefully designed. However, successful distillation depends on alignment of teacher and student inputs/representations, the choice of distilled signals (logits, features, attention, or contrastive embeddings), and careful handling of privacy, robustness, and domain shift. Best practice combines representation-level matching, adaptive teacher strategies, confidence-aware multi-teacher fusion, and privacy- or robustness-aware objectives to meet practical constraints while maximizing student performance.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from large, often overparameterized teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while preserving performance. Across modalities and tasks, KD has evolved from simple soft-label matching to a diverse toolkit that includes intermediate representation matching, multi-teacher schedules, data-centric strategies (augmentation, data-free synthesis), online and distributed protocols, and task-aware adaptations. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how the student is initialized (including whether it is pre-trained), how the data distribution is shaped during distillation, and how robustness and rare-token behavior are addressed. Combining complementary techniques (pretraining, feature imitation, data mixing, and adaptive teacher strategies) produces compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints, but open issues remain around teacher selection, distributional mismatch, fairness, and adversarial robustness.

papers_seen.author: Callahan
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable strategy for compressing large neural networks into smaller, faster models while retaining much of their performance. Across modalities and tasks, distillation enables deployment of powerful pretrained models in resource-constrained settings, supports specialization (e.g., task or domain adaptation), and can be combined with complementary compression techniques (quantization, pruning, architecture search) to produce practical, production-ready models. Advances in distillation methodology — including multi-teacher schemes, self-distillation, teacher meta-learning, and task-aware layer-wise alignment — address fundamental challenges of capacity mismatch, information selection, and optimization stability, leading to more robust and efficient student models. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a core component of any production-focused compression pipeline for deep learning and NLP systems, and that research emphasis on better teacher–student dynamics and task-aware transfer will yield the largest practical gains.

papers_seen.author: Lambert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring aspects of teacher behavior. The field has expanded from soft-label (logit) supervision to diverse strategies including feature- and representation-level imitation, flexible layer mapping, online/co-distillation, data- and domain-aware augmentation, and multimodal-to-mono-modal transfer. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost, but success depends on what is transferred (soft targets, features, relations), how teacher and student architectures are aligned, the availability and quality of distillation data, and deployment constraints such as privacy, domain shift, and compute budget. Open challenges include selecting the right distillation targets for task and capacity gap, ensuring robustness and fairness post-compression, and automating adaptive distillation pipelines for heterogeneous production settings.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression approaches transform large, high-performance neural models into smaller, faster models suitable for constrained deployment while attempting to preserve task performance. Methods range from transferring softened output distributions to matching intermediate representations, designing task-aware layer mappings, synthesizing or augmenting data for training, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Applications include compressing pretrained transformers for NLP, improving robustness under domain shift, enabling on-device inference and federated learning with heterogeneous devices, and training non-autoregressive sequence models. Empirical and theoretical work highlights both practical gains and limitations: distillation can yield compact models with strong accuracy but its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, availability or synthesis of data, and handling low-frequency or domain-specific phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Stevens
papers_seen.title: The Central, Practical, and Conditional Role of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible set of techniques for transferring useful behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can meet deployment constraints while retaining much of the teacher’s utility. KD methods span soft-target matching, intermediate representation and layer-wise alignment, ensemble-to-single transfers, task-adaptive architecture search, and data-free or privacy-conscious pipelines. Empirical work shows KD can produce compact models that approach teacher performance across NLP, speech, and vision tasks, and that combining KD with architecture-aware compression or augmentation strategies often yields the best trade-offs. However, KD has limits: student capacity, the availability and quality of distilled data, and inherited teacher biases can all constrain outcomes. Responsible and effective compression therefore requires selecting the appropriate distillation signals, considering task and deployment constraints, and combining KD with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, or fairness-aware objectives).

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a flexible and central mechanism for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and language tasks. The literature frames KD as a family of objectives — soft-target (logit) supervision, intermediate representation matching, relational or attention-based losses, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware procedures — which are often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while drastically reducing inference cost, but its success depends on careful design choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or absent training data, and how to mitigate capacity mismatch and robustness issues. Task-aware and architecture-aware adaptations (including layer-wise filtering, task-adaptive architecture search, and transformer-specific compression) have proven effective in producing compact models for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and a Prescription
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible tool for compressing large models into efficient students suitable for deployment. When combined with careful pre-training of compact architectures, representation-level supervision, and complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, distillation has important failure modes—capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity, and optimization difficulties—that require task-aware design choices around what to transfer, which teacher(s) to use, and how to prepare distillation data. A pragmatic pipeline that pre-trains compact models, distills both outputs and intermediate representations, and selectively combines KD with other compression steps yields the best trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy in practice.
