papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Adaptation: Teaching to Adapt
papers_seen.abstract: Domain adaptation is crucial in many real-world applications where the distribution of the training data differs from the distribution of the test data. Previous Deep Learning-based approaches to domain adaptation need to be trained jointly on source and target domain data and are therefore unappealing in scenarios where models need to be adapted to a large number of domains or where a domain is evolving, e.g. spam detection where attackers continuously change their tactics.   To fill this gap, we propose Knowledge Adaptation, an extension of Knowledge Distillation (Bucilua et al., 2006; Hinton et al., 2015) to the domain adaptation scenario. We show how a student model achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised domain adaptation from multiple sources on a standard sentiment analysis benchmark by taking into account the domain-specific expertise of multiple teachers and the similarities between their domains.   When learning from a single teacher, using domain similarity to gauge trustworthiness is inadequate. To this end, we propose a simple metric that correlates well with the teacher's accuracy in the target domain. We demonstrate that incorporating high-confidence examples selected by this metric enables the student model to achieve state-of-the-art performance in the single-source scenario.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a single training trick into a flexible, task-aware toolkit for compressing large models into efficient students suitable for real-world deployment. KD can transfer output behavior, internal representations, and relational or structural knowledge; it can be adapted to constraints such as missing training data, privacy, distributed training, and domain shifts; and when combined with complementary techniques (architecture adaptation, pruning, task-aware layer selection) it produces compact models that retain much of the teacher's accuracy while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements. Practical use of KD requires matching the distillation strategy to the application constraints (what to transfer, which data to use, and how to align heterogeneous architectures).

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-level toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. Effective KD requires selecting what to transfer (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational signals), matching teacher and student capacities, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques. When applied with task-aware objectives, projector or alignment modules, and careful treatment of data and teacher preparation, KD yields compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints, though capacity mismatch and data limitations remain important caveats.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What is Known about Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Existing practice spans matching teacher output distributions, transferring intermediate representations or attention, online and ensemble distillation, and data-free or synthetic-data approaches when original training data are unavailable. KD is typically combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and shaped by practical concerns—teacher–student capacity alignment, what and how to transfer, data availability or privacy, and robustness—which determine real-world effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing deep models and transferring capabilities across architectures and modalities. KD has enabled large speedups and model-size reductions while preserving or even improving downstream task performance when carefully applied. However, distillation is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on data availability, teacher–student alignment, and distributional heterogeneity, and it can transmit teacher biases or errors. Combining logit-based supervision with feature- and relation-focused objectives, aligning intermediate representations, and adapting distillation strategies to task and data constraints yields the best trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment. Research over the past decade has produced a wide array of distillation variants (logit-based supervision, feature and attention matching, multi- and self-distillation, data-free methods) and shown how KD can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet practical constraints. Empirical and theoretical work identifies both the strengths of KD (regularization, practical deployment gains, domain adaptation) and its limits (optimization difficulty, capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors), motivating a pragmatic set of design choices for robust compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Engine for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has matured from a heuristic into a set of principled, modality-agnostic techniques that enable deployment of high-capacity models in resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings. By transferring predictive behaviour and internal representations from large teachers to compact students, distillation preserves much of the teacher's utility while enabling large speed, memory, and communication gains. Recent advances show that combining representation-level matching, teacher–student co-design, data-free synthesis, and task-adaptive compression yields robust, practical pipelines for compressing models across vision, language, graph, and federated settings.

papers_seen.author: Mahoney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Not Universal Solution for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective and versatile strategy for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When carefully designed—choosing what to transfer (logits, features, relations), preparing or synthesizing appropriate data, and combining KD with complementary methods such as quantization or architecture search—distillation can produce compact models that retain much of teacher performance across modalities. However, KD has limits: teacher–student capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity or absence, and optimization subtleties can reduce gains. Practical deployment therefore benefits from hybrid pipelines that adapt KD objectives to task constraints, incorporate robustness and privacy considerations, and use auxiliary compression techniques where appropriate.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques compress large neural models into smaller, faster, or more private students by transferring information from a teacher. Research over the past decade has explored a spectrum of KD variants — from soft-label logits transfer to feature-map matching, adversarial and online schemes, few-shot and privacy-preserving compression, and theoretical analyses of when and why distillation helps. Empirical work shows KD improves deployment practicality across vision, speech, NLP, graph, and generative models, while recent studies examine robustness, data-efficiency, the role of pre-training, and the impact of teacher quality. Important open directions include principled methods for sample selection, cross-domain transfer, formal guarantees under limited data or adversaries, and integrating KD with compression primitives such as pruning and structured sparsity.

papers_seen.author: Mathis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multifaceted Toolbox for Compression, Regularization, and Privacy in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a flexible, multi-purpose methodology rather than only a compression trick. KD enables smaller, efficient models for deployment, but it also serves as a mechanism for learned regularization, domain adaptation, and privacy-aware model release. Practical success relies on matching the distillation signals (soft targets, intermediate features, relations), the teacher selection and scheduling, and the data or data-generation strategy to the deployment constraints. Combining logits-based supervision with representation-level objectives, multi-stage or multi-teacher schedules, and privacy-aware query mechanisms produces more reliable and robust student models for real-world NLP and deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring useful predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models. The literature offers a range of objectives (soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, relational losses), architectural strategies (layer mapping, progressive replacement, many-to-many alignment), and data approaches (using original data, augmented or synthesized surrogates, or data-free/zero-shot methods). Practical success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to manage data scarcity, privacy, and domain shift. Applications include compressing pre-trained language models for NLP, adapting multi-modal models to single modalities, compressing ranking and detection systems, and enabling deployment under compute, latency, or privacy constraints. Open challenges remain in preserving rare-token behaviors, coping with imperfect or heterogeneous teachers, and designing robust, privacy-aware distillation protocols.

papers_seen.author: Chandler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Multi-Tool Approach to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single recipe but as a flexible family of methods that, when combined with task-aware design and complementary compression techniques, enables deployment of compact models with strong utility. KD can transfer final-output behavior, intermediate representations, and structured relationships; it can operate with or without original training data, be adapted for privacy-sensitive or federated settings, and be combined with quantization or pruning to meet hardware constraints. Effective practice requires attention to what is distilled, how teachers and students are prepared, and how KD is integrated into the broader compression pipeline to avoid propagation of teacher biases or degradation on rare or shifted data.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: The Central Role and Evolving Practices of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental and versatile approach for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP. It enables compact, efficient student models that retain much of a teacher's performance, supports deployment on resource-constrained devices, and can be adapted to privacy-sensitive or distributed settings. Recent advances extend distillation beyond simple logits matching to many-to-many layer mapping, task-adaptive compression, teacher-aware training, adversarial and data-free scenarios, and robustness-aware objectives. Together these developments show that distillation is both a practical engineering tool and a rich research paradigm for addressing capacity, data availability, privacy, and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Morrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core of Model Compression — Strengths, Limits, and Recommended Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with attention to which teacher signals are transferred, how the student is initialized, and how complementary compression methods are integrated, KD reliably reduces inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a magic bullet: theoretical and empirical work highlights optimization gaps, failures under heterogeneous data or federated settings, and robustness and rare-token fidelity issues. Realistic deployment therefore requires task-aware distillation recipes, student pre-training, data strategies (including data-free synthesis when necessary), and explicit evaluation of failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Orr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation condenses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment under memory, latency, or privacy constraints. Techniques span soft-target learning, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational objectives, layer-mapping strategies, and data-centric adaptations (including data-free and few-shot regimes). When combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search, distillation produces compact models that often retain most of the teacher's accuracy; success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, handling mismatched inputs or modalities, and designing appropriate data or augmentation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across vision and language, KD variants — from simple soft-target matching to feature-level, layer-aware, and many-to-many mapping approaches — enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to map layers, how to use or synthesize data, and whether to adapt teachers or students; remaining challenges include handling heterogeneous data and devices, preserving robustness and fairness, and enabling data-free or privacy-conscious distillation.

papers_seen.author: Ibarra
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from matching soft teacher outputs into a flexible toolkit for producing compact, efficient models across vision and language. Empirical and methodological work shows KD can transfer final predictions, intermediate representations, relational structure, and inductive biases from large teachers to smaller students, and it is often most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when adapted to data constraints (real-data, augmented, or data-free regimes). Practical success depends on choices about distillation targets, teacher-student alignment, and data; remaining challenges include teacher imperfections, distributional mismatch, and preserving robustness and fairness under compression.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques provide a broad, practically oriented toolkit for shrinking large neural models while retaining most of their performance. Methods include transferring soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, adapting teacher or student architectures, using adversarial or data-free sample generation, and combining distillation with quantization or pruning. Empirical results across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks show substantial latency and memory gains; success depends on what signals are transferred, how layers are matched, data availability and augmentation, and the deployment constraints that shape algorithmic choices.

papers_seen.author: Archer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers. KD can preserve predictive performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Its strengths derive from a variety of mechanisms — soft-label matching, internal-feature alignment, layer-mapping, and task-adaptive architecture design — and from being combinable with complementary compression techniques. However, realizing consistent gains requires careful choice of distilled targets, attention to representation alignment between teacher and student, and explicit handling of data-, fairness-, and robustness-related risks. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a toolbox of targeted interventions rather than a single recipe, and provides concise, evidence-based recommendations for practitioners compressing models in vision and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structured signals. A wide variety of KD strategies—matching softened logits, aligning features or attention maps, multi-teacher schedules, and data- or task-aware augmentation—enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical success depends on what is distilled, student capacity and architecture alignment, availability and provenance of data, and task-specific constraints (e.g., robustness or federated heterogeneity). Carefully designed pipelines can preserve most teacher performance while substantially reducing resource cost, but KD also has important failure modes that motivate complementary techniques and careful engineering.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Cornerstone of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. KD operates at multiple levels (soft targets, intermediate representations, relational structure) and can be combined with complementary compression techniques and data strategies to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When tailored to model architecture, task demands, and available data, KD yields compact models that enable real-world deployment across modalities and domains.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and adaptable family of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster models suitable for deployment. Beyond the classic teacher-logit supervision, modern distillation covers feature-level matching, task-adaptive architecture search, multi-teacher transfer, and data-free scenarios. KD can be combined with pruning and structured sparsity, adapted for domain shifts, and used to transfer ensemble or task-specific knowledge into compact models. The choice of distillation target, the availability of data, and the deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy, domain) determine which distillation recipe will be most effective.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Compression and Transfer in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured beyond a single recipe for copying soft labels: it is a flexible set of techniques that address model compression, domain and task transfer, privacy-constrained scenarios, distributed training, and continual learning. Practical KD variants operate at different levels (logits, features, layers), use data augmentation or synthetic data when real data are unavailable, and adapt training schedules to the target application. When chosen to match the constraints of the deployment setting—data availability, compute budget, task type, and model architecture—KD consistently enables smaller or more specialized students to approach or sometimes exceed teacher performance while offering operational benefits such as faster inference, lower memory, and more reproducible training.

papers_seen.author: Zavala
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Limited Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach that enables deploying large models under resource, latency, and privacy constraints by transferring knowledge from teacher to student models. KD extends beyond simple logit matching to include representation-level transfer, attention- and feature-guided objectives, multi-teacher schedules, and integration with architecture search and pretraining. While KD reliably improves efficiency and can preserve many teacher behaviors, its success depends on choices of distillation targets, teacher preparation, student architecture, and data strategies; it can also amplify teacher errors or struggle under data heterogeneity, requiring complementary techniques and careful engineering for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: Practical Principles for Effective Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. While classic distillation focuses on matching teacher output probabilities, practical compression across modalities and tasks benefits from richer transfer mechanisms: aligning internal representations, selecting task-relevant signals, leveraging data augmentation or synthetic data when real data are scarce, and using adversarial or ensemble strategies to expose diverse and robust teacher knowledge. When combined thoughtfully these methods enable students that are much smaller and faster while retaining or even improving accuracy and robustness on downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Multi-Purpose Tool for Compression, Adaptation, and Responsible Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a broad, practical toolbox rather than a narrow compression trick. Beyond shrinking parameter counts, KD can regularize learning, transfer intermediate and structural knowledge, enable model adaptation when data are limited or private, preserve robustness and fairness properties, and support cross-modal or modality-restricted deployment. Realizing these benefits in deep learning and NLP requires combining complementary signals (soft targets, feature/attention matching, and relational losses), adapting teacher schedules and layer mappings to student capacity, and integrating KD with data synthesis or multi-teacher strategies when original data are unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates through multiple mechanisms—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational structure, and providing regularization—that together enable substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. KD integrates naturally with other compression methods (architecture search, pruning, quantization), supports data-free and privacy-sensitive settings, and scales across modalities and deployment constraints. At the same time, effective distillation requires careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to map teacher and student layers, how to handle imperfect teachers and data mismatch, and when to combine KD with complementary techniques. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a toolbox rather than a single recipe and offers practical, evidence-based recommendations for deploying KD in real systems.

papers_seen.author: Soto
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for compressing large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students for deployment in resource-, latency-, or privacy-constrained environments. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while providing additional benefits such as implicit regularization, improved robustness in some settings, domain adaptation, and enabling training when original data are unavailable. A practical KD pipeline selects what to transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, relational structure), how to supply data (real, augmented, synthesized, or data-free), and how to align teacher and student architectures; combining KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) typically yields the best trade-offs. Remaining challenges include handling teacher–student capacity mismatch, domain and distributional shift, optimization stability, preservation of low-frequency behaviors in NLP, and privacy constraints, which motivate hybrid, task-aware distillation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Distilled Semantics for Comprehensive Scene Understanding from Videos
papers_seen.abstract: Whole understanding of the surroundings is paramount to autonomous systems. Recent works have shown that deep neural networks can learn geometry (depth) and motion (optical flow) from a monocular video without any explicit supervision from ground truth annotations, particularly hard to source for these two tasks. In this paper, we take an additional step toward holistic scene understanding with monocular cameras by learning depth and motion alongside with semantics, with supervision for the latter provided by a pre-trained network distilling proxy ground truth images. We address the three tasks jointly by a) a novel training protocol based on knowledge distillation and self-supervision and b) a compact network architecture which enables efficient scene understanding on both power hungry GPUs and low-power embedded platforms. We thoroughly assess the performance of our framework and show that it yields state-of-the-art results for monocular depth estimation, optical flow and motion segmentation.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Cornerstone of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. KD operates at multiple levels (soft targets, intermediate representations, relational structure) and can be combined with complementary compression techniques and data strategies to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When tailored to model architecture, task demands, and available data, KD yields compact models that enable real-world deployment across modalities and domains.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Powerful, Flexible — but Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods have matured into a practical toolkit for producing smaller, faster models while retaining much of the performance of larger teachers. These techniques have been applied across domains (vision, speech, NLP, healthcare), settings (offline compression, federated learning, continual adaptation), and architectures (ensembles, transformers, detectors, GANs). However, their success depends on factors such as the availability and nature of data used for distillation, domain mismatch between teacher and student, robustness and privacy requirements, and optimization dynamics. KD can unlock high-performing compact models when combined with task-aware design choices (e.g., feature imitation, augmentations, architecture search, or ensemble teachers), but practitioners must account for trade-offs and failure modes to use it effectively.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Learning Compact Metrics for MT
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in machine translation and multilingual text generation have led researchers to adopt trained metrics such as COMET or BLEURT, which treat evaluation as a regression problem and use representations from multilingual pre-trained models such as XLM-RoBERTa or mBERT. Yet studies on related tasks suggest that these models are most efficient when they are large, which is costly and impractical for evaluation. We investigate the trade-off between multilinguality and model capacity with RemBERT, a state-of-the-art multilingual language model, using data from the WMT Metrics Shared Task. We present a series of experiments which show that model size is indeed a bottleneck for cross-lingual transfer, then demonstrate how distillation can help addressing this bottleneck, by leveraging synthetic data generation and transferring knowledge from one teacher to multiple students trained on related languages. Our method yields up to 10.5% improvement over vanilla fine-tuning and reaches 92.6% of RemBERT's performance using only a third of its parameters.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: The Practical Centrality and Limitations of Knowledge Distillation for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a primary tool for compressing large deep models into compact, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. KD has been applied across modalities and use-cases—distilling large language models into lightweight encoders, compressing ensembles into single predictors, enabling privacy- and device-aware deployments, and even operating without access to original training data. At the same time, theoretical gaps, data- and heterogeneity-driven failure modes, and teacher biases motivate hybrid strategies (multi-teacher, meta-learned teachers, data-free generators, and combined compression techniques) to realize KD’s full potential in practical systems.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other learned structure. A broad family of techniques—soft-target (logit) matching, representation- and layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher and ensemble transfer, architecture-aware transformations, and data-free or generator-based synthesis—has been developed to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical and theoretical work shows distillation often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices, but effectiveness depends on choices about what is transferred, teacher and student architecture, data availability, and optimization. Practical pipelines combine distillation with complementary methods (pretraining of compact models, data augmentation, pruning/quantization, and task-aware objectives) and must address challenges such as capacity mismatch, domain shift, robustness preservation, and faithful transfer of rare behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Welch
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: Practical Directions for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to compress large models into lightweight students for deployment. Recent work shows that KD can preserve most of a teacher's performance while dramatically reducing model size or computational cost, but gains depend on what knowledge is transferred, how teachers and students are prepared, and the distillation protocol. I argue that (1) transferring richer information than final logits, (2) preparing students with pre-training, (3) augmenting or synthesizing data during distillation, and (4) co-optimizing architecture-aware compression with distillation together form a robust recipe for reliable compression in NLP and other domains. These directions address generalization, data scarcity, and architectural differences, and they are supported by recent empirical and methodological studies across speech, vision, retrieval, and language modeling.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/VainF/Data-Free-Adversarial-Distillation.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Releasing Graph Neural Networks with Differential Privacy Guarantees
papers_seen.abstract: With the increasing popularity of graph neural networks (GNNs) in several sensitive applications like healthcare and medicine, concerns have been raised over the privacy aspects of trained GNNs. More notably, GNNs are vulnerable to privacy attacks, such as membership inference attacks, even if only black-box access to the trained model is granted. We propose PrivGNN, a privacy-preserving framework for releasing GNN models in a centralized setting. Assuming an access to a public unlabeled graph, PrivGNN provides a framework to release GNN models trained explicitly on public data along with knowledge obtained from the private data in a privacy preserving manner. PrivGNN combines the knowledge-distillation framework with the two noise mechanisms, random subsampling, and noisy labeling, to ensure rigorous privacy guarantees. We theoretically analyze our approach in the Renyi differential privacy framework. Besides, we show the solid experimental performance of our method compared to several baselines adapted for graph-structured data. Our code is available at https://github.com/iyempissy/privGnn.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques compress large, high-performing models into smaller, faster, or lower-precision models while retaining much of their performance. Approaches range from matching teacher soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations and using contrastive or projection-based objectives. Practical training choices—such as which layers or features to mimic, how to filter or weight training samples, the role of data augmentation, and whether compact models are pre-trained—strongly affect outcomes. KD has been applied across domains (vision, language, graphs), combined with quantization and low-precision deployment, and adapted for resource-heterogeneous and latency-sensitive settings. Empirical and theoretical work highlights that KD works both by transferring relational/representational knowledge and by providing regularizing soft targets; effective distillation designs balance these mechanisms and tailor the transfer to task and capacity constraints.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, pragmatic technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. KD operates at multiple levels—soft outputs, intermediate representations, and structured relational signals—and is effective across modalities when paired with complementary compression methods, careful data strategies, and student-aware architecture design. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its success depends on aligning teacher and student capacity, selecting appropriate distillation targets, preparing or synthesizing suitable training data, and validating robustness and fairness. A production-ready compression pipeline treats KD as a system of interacting components (signal selection, data, initialization, and optimization) and couples distillation with architecture-aware transforms, pruning, or quantization to meet real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable method for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. When applied thoughtfully—selecting what to transfer (logits, features, attention), aligning inputs and architectures, and combining KD with complementary compression (pruning, structured sparsity, quantization) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic samples, curriculum)—KD enables resource-efficient deployment across vision, language, multimodal, and federated settings. However, its success depends on teacher quality, data availability, and alignment between teacher and student; addressing these constraints through multi-teacher designs, black-box adaptation, and feature-level alignment remains essential for robust, private, and high-performance compression.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural relationships. A spectrum of techniques — matching softened outputs, aligning features or attention, layer-mapping (including many-to-many mappings), multi-teacher or ensemble transfers, and data-free or generator-based synthesis — enables large reductions in size and latency while largely preserving task performance. KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and careful data and training choices; but it faces practical challenges including capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and the potential transfer of teacher biases or adversarial vulnerabilities.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Dependent Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while often preserving much of the teacher's effectiveness. KD methods range from matching soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations or using adversarial generators when training data are unavailable; they have been successfully applied across vision, generative modeling, recommender systems, and large pretrained language models. However, KD’s success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to address limited or private data, robustness, and bias—so practitioners must pair KD with task-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives to get reliable, deployable results.

papers_seen.author: Benson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Multi-Ingredient Toolbox for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated as a configurable system rather than a single recipe. By choosing which teacher signals to transfer (logits, features, relations), aligning teacher and student architectures, and applying task- and data-aware strategies (including multi-teacher aggregation, adversarial or data-free synthesis, and architecture search), practitioners can produce compact models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. KD delivers practical gains across vision and NLP but requires careful design to avoid propagating teacher errors, mismatching capacities, or degrading robustness and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Bell
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of techniques for transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. The field includes matching softened output distributions, imitating intermediate representations or attention maps, transferring relational or structural knowledge, and combining distillation with data-side techniques (augmentation, synthetic data) and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing parameters and latency, but effectiveness depends on choices of knowledge to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and task-specific constraints. Remaining challenges include robustness under domain shift, fairness and bias transfer, privacy in distributed settings, and limits to compression for some generative tasks.

papers_seen.author: Nunez
papers_seen.title: Beyond Compression: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Practical, Private, and Robust Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is often framed narrowly as a model-compression trick to shrink large neural networks. This paper argues KD should instead be viewed as a core engineering and scientific tool for practical deployment: it enables training with limited or private data, yields task- and domain-adaptive compact models, improves robustness and fairness, and transfers intermediate representations and attention patterns that standard supervised training cannot. We synthesize evidence from recent work to show how variants of KD—self-distillation, layer-wise projection, multi-teacher schemes, teacher annealing, and data-free distillation—address concrete deployment challenges in vision and NLP, and we derive practical recommendations for combining these techniques in real systems.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural relations. A variety of KD objectives—matching teacher logits (soft targets), aligning features or attention maps, transferring relational or contrastive structure, and self- or multi-teacher schemes—have been adapted across vision, language, multimodal, and structured prediction tasks. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and which data to use or synthesize for distillation. Although KD often preserves much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, open challenges remain including optimization hardness, propagation of teacher errors, domain and device heterogeneity, data- or privacy-constrained settings, and preserving robustness under distributional shift. Effective deployment commonly combines KD with complementary techniques (pre-training students, pruning, quantization, or data augmentation) and task-aware design choices.

papers_seen.author: Atkinson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) condenses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural knowledge. A rich set of techniques—soft-target (logit) transfer, feature- and attention-level imitation, layer mapping and progressive replacement, data-free or zero-shot distillation, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search—has emerged. Practical success depends on choices about teacher signals, student architecture and capacity, data availability and augmentation, and integration with complementary compression methods. Remaining challenges include teacher–student mismatch, preserving robustness and rare behaviors, and operating under limited or private data.

papers_seen.author: Vance
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural teachers into smaller students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across vision and language, KD methods include matching softened teacher outputs, aligning intermediate features or attention maps, ensembling or multi-teacher schemes, self- and online-distillation, and data-free or synthetic-data approaches. Empirical work shows that properly designed KD pipelines can produce compact models that retain most teacher performance and enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. At the same time, distillation success depends on teacher–student compatibility, choice of distillation targets, data availability, and training dynamics; open challenges include preserving robustness and fairness, understanding which teacher signals matter for which tasks and architectures, and distilling under strict data or privacy limitations.
