papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable ones by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural relations. Across vision and natural language tasks, KD variants—logits/soft-label matching, feature- and relation-level imitation, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols—enable substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while often retaining most of the teacher’s performance. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to generate or curate data for transfer, and how to align teacher and student capacity; common extensions address fairness, federated or distributed settings, and privacy constraints. Remaining challenges include optimization difficulties, propagation of teacher errors (especially on low-frequency phenomena), domain and device heterogeneity, and preserving robustness under distributional shift.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Robust and Resource-Efficient Data-Free Knowledge Distillation by Generative Pseudo Replay
papers_seen.abstract: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation (KD) allows knowledge transfer from a trained neural network (teacher) to a more compact one (student) in the absence of original training data. Existing works use a validation set to monitor the accuracy of the student over real data and report the highest performance throughout the entire process. However, validation data may not be available at distillation time either, making it infeasible to record the student snapshot that achieved the peak accuracy. Therefore, a practical data-free KD method should be robust and ideally provide monotonically increasing student accuracy during distillation. This is challenging because the student experiences knowledge degradation due to the distribution shift of the synthetic data. A straightforward approach to overcome this issue is to store and rehearse the generated samples periodically, which increases the memory footprint and creates privacy concerns. We propose to model the distribution of the previously observed synthetic samples with a generative network. In particular, we design a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with a training objective that is customized to learn the synthetic data representations optimally. The student is rehearsed by the generative pseudo replay technique, with samples produced by the VAE. Hence knowledge degradation can be prevented without storing any samples. Experiments on image classification benchmarks show that our method optimizes the expected value of the distilled model accuracy while eliminating the large memory overhead incurred by the sample-storing methods.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Valdez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile technique for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones while preserving much of their predictive performance. KD has matured beyond simple output-matching into a family of methods that transfer intermediate representations, attention or channel-wise signals, and task-specific inductive biases; it can operate under data scarcity or privacy constraints and can be combined with architecture search or other compression primitives to produce deployment-ready models. Successful application requires matching the distillation recipe to the task, student capacity, and deployment constraints and managing teacher imperfections and data mismatches.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and allied compression techniques have become central tools for reducing the computational and storage cost of large deep models while retaining much of their performance. Research has expanded beyond the original soft-label paradigm to include distillation of internal representations, layer- and channel-wise alignment, progressive module replacement, and teacher-student co-design. Applications span vision, NLP, graph models, generative networks, and large-scale distributed training. Recent work also explores distillation for robustness, low-precision deployment, few-shot compression, and federated or multi-device settings. Despite strong empirical gains, open challenges remain in transferring inductive biases, choosing what and when to distill, and preserving attributes such as fairness and adversarial robustness in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from matching teacher logits to a flexible toolkit for producing compact, efficient models suitable for deployment and adaptation in deep learning and NLP. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can transfer predictive behavior, intermediate representations, and task-specific properties (e.g., robustness or privacy signals), and it is most effective when combined with complementary strategies such as pre-training of compact architectures, data-side interventions, and low-precision or structured pruning. Success depends on careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous teacher and student architectures, how to construct or augment distillation data, and how to adapt teacher behavior; practical pipelines treat KD as one component of a broader compression workflow rather than a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have become central tools for shrinking large deep models into smaller, faster, or more interpretable models while retaining much of their performance. Research has expanded beyond the original logit-based teacher-student paradigm to include feature mimicking, self-distillation, data-free and privacy-preserving variants, multi-teacher and adaptive-teacher strategies, and task- or hardware-aware compression. These methods have been applied across modalities — including vision, graphs, generative models, and a broad set of NLP tasks — and are increasingly combined with architecture search and pruning to meet deployment constraints. Despite empirical successes, important questions remain about what knowledge is most useful to transfer, how to select or adapt teachers, and how to operate under data, compute, or privacy limitations.

papers_seen.author: Dominguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical toolkit for compressing deep models for real-world deployment. KD unifies multiple signals (soft targets, intermediate representations, relational/attention matching) and interoperates naturally with complementary techniques (architecture search, pruning, quantization, and data synthesis). Properly designed KD pipelines—choosing what to transfer, mapping teacher and student representations, and addressing data or privacy constraints—yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance across classification, generation, detection, and language tasks. At the same time, KD has limits (capacity mismatch, optimization and data mismatch, and potential propagation of teacher biases), so production pipelines must combine KD with pretraining, data strategies, and robustness/fairness checks to be reliable.

papers_seen.author: Carr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, general-purpose approach for translating large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. Across architectures, modalities, and deployment constraints, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of the teacher's performance; however, realizing those gains in practice requires matching the distillation formulation to data availability, model mismatch, and robustness requirements.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for creating smaller, faster models from larger ones while retaining much of their functionality. When combined with representation matching, architecture-aware surgery, selective sample strategies, and privacy-aware protocols, KD enables deployment of high-quality models across modalities and constrained environments. However, its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to handle limited or sensitive data; without such care, distillation can underperform or transfer undesirable behaviors. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the central, composable tool in compression toolkits, and outlines concrete methodological priorities that practitioners should follow to realize reliable, efficient distilled models.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Sims
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Paradigm for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted training paradigm that enables compact, deployable models by transferring aspects of teacher models to smaller students. When treated as a central tool rather than a single recipe, KD supports a range of targets (soft logits, intermediate features, relational signals), deployment modalities (on-device, federated, data-limited), and complementary compressions (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design). Its practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to adapt data and curricula; with these considerations KD can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints, though optimization subtleties and robustness remain important caveats.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Ashley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision and language tasks. KD works at multiple levels — soft logits, intermediate representations, relational structure, and ensemble behaviour — and is most effective when combined with data strategies, teacher–student co-design, and complementary compression such as pruning or quantization. While KD often preserves much of teacher performance and can regularize student training, its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align capacities, and how to handle limited or mismatched data; careful, task-aware protocols are therefore essential for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Estes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Toolbox: Principles, Limits, and Practical Prescriptions for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation should be understood and applied as a flexible set of techniques that go well beyond simple parameter compression. When treated as a toolbox—combining soft-target supervision, internal representation matching, layer-aware alignment, attention-guided mapping, and complementary compression methods—distillation can produce compact models that preserve accuracy, improve interpretability, and transfer robustness or privacy properties. Success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to prepare the student, and how to mitigate propagation of teacher defects; practitioners benefit from system-level designs that pair distillation objectives with pre-training, data augmentation, and architecture-aware compression.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Model Compression and Practical NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher's effectiveness. A growing body of work shows KD's versatility across modalities (vision, speech, text), deployment regimes (edge devices, distributed training), and model families (transformers, convolutional nets, generative models). Combining richer teacher signals (intermediate representations, attention maps, or learned teacher updates), stronger input-side practices (data augmentation), and complementary compression methods (architecture search, pruning) yields robust, efficient students suitable for real-world constraints. This paper argues that distillation should be treated not as a single recipe but as a flexible toolkit whose components are chosen to match task constraints, and it highlights promising techniques to improve transfer fidelity, training efficiency, and downstream performance.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure from teachers to students. A rich family of KD methods—soft-target/logit matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, multi-teacher and ensemble supervision, data-free and data-augmented distillation, and teacher-student co-design—has been developed to meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy) across vision and language tasks. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance when distillation objectives, data strategies, and architecture choices are well matched. Remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher biases or errors, scarcity or absence of real data, and preserving low-frequency behaviors in sequence models. Practical pipelines combine pretraining of compact architectures, multi-objective distillation (outputs + internals), data augmentation or synthesis, and teacher adaptation to produce robust, efficient student models.

papers_seen.author: Santana
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students for deployment in resource-constrained settings. The literature shows a spectrum of distillation objectives—from matching soft output distributions to transferring intermediate representations, relational statistics, and task-specific features—and emphasizes combining KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free distillation). Successful distillation pipelines attend to teacher–student capacity alignment, layer- and signal-selection, and data provenance to preserve accuracy, robustness, and domain suitability. Remaining challenges include distillation without original data, robustness under distribution shift or adversarial attack, and automated, architecture-agnostic distillation for heterogeneous deployment environments.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Practical Prescriptions for Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, efficient students suitable for deployment. While KD reliably reduces model size and inference cost, its effectiveness depends critically on choices around teacher design, the training signal (soft labels vs. representations), the data used for distillation, and additional constraints such as fairness and privacy. To realize reliable, high-quality compressed models in NLP and related domains, practitioners should treat KD as a system composed of complementary ingredients—data augmentation, multi-teacher or meta-learned teachers, representation-level objectives, and interventions for bias and privacy—rather than a single off-the-shelf loss.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural relations. A variety of KD objectives—matching teacher logits (soft targets), aligning features or attention maps, transferring relational or contrastive structure, and self- or multi-teacher schemes—have been adapted across vision, language, multimodal, and structured prediction tasks. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and which data to use or synthesize for distillation. Although KD often preserves much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, open challenges remain including optimization hardness, propagation of teacher errors, domain and device heterogeneity, data- or privacy-constrained settings, and preserving robustness under distributional shift. Effective deployment commonly combines KD with complementary techniques (pre-training students, pruning, quantization, or data augmentation) and task-aware design choices.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Cornerstone of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic for transferring soft targets into a unifying toolkit that enables model compression, deployment on constrained devices, privacy-aware release, and modality transfer. By combining architectural mapping, contrastive and adversarial objectives, and data-free or federated setups, KD can preserve much of a teacher model's performance while drastically reducing footprint and computation. This makes KD essential for translating state-of-the-art large models into real-world, resource-limited, and privacy-sensitive applications.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Compression and Transfer in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured beyond a single recipe for copying soft labels: it is a flexible set of techniques that address model compression, domain and task transfer, privacy-constrained scenarios, distributed training, and continual learning. Practical KD variants operate at different levels (logits, features, layers), use data augmentation or synthetic data when real data are unavailable, and adapt training schedules to the target application. When chosen to match the constraints of the deployment setting—data availability, compute budget, task type, and model architecture—KD consistently enables smaller or more specialized students to approach or sometimes exceed teacher performance while offering operational benefits such as faster inference, lower memory, and more reproducible training.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger, often ensemble or over-parameterized teacher models to smaller, faster student models. Across computer vision, graph, generative, and language tasks, distillation reduces storage and inference cost while often retaining most of the teacher's accuracy. Methods range from matching output distributions to aligning intermediate representations or using adversarial generators when training data are unavailable. Distillation has been applied successfully to compress transformers and other large pretrained language models, to speed up question answering and reading-comprehension systems, and to produce compact models suitable for deployment on edge devices. At the same time, distillation faces challenges including loss of certain types of teacher knowledge, sensitivity to which samples are distilled, potential transfer or amplification of undesirable biases, and concerns about robustness and privacy. Recent work addresses these issues by selective sample weighting, multi-teacher schemes, adversarial data-free approaches, and robustness-aware objectives, suggesting a rich design space for future improvement.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other learned structure. Methods span data-dependent distillation using teacher soft targets and intermediate hints, multi-teacher and ensemble compression, many-to-many layer mapping for large pre-trained language models, data-free or zero-shot distillation where training data are unavailable, and approaches that combine distillation with quantization or pruning for deployment. Empirical results demonstrate that distillation can recover much of a teacher's accuracy while enabling efficiency gains, but trade-offs remain around robustness, optimization difficulty, domain shifts, and the need for careful alignment of inputs or representations. Recent work addresses these challenges with generative replay, adversarial objectives, layer-matching distances, and teacher-annealing strategies, yet open problems include theory of optimization, scalable privacy-preserving protocols, and balancing fairness or robustness with compression.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques convert large, accurate neural models into smaller, faster models suitable for constrained inference environments. Approaches vary from transferring soft-label outputs to aligning intermediate representations, progressively replacing modules, augmenting or synthesizing data during teacher–student training, and compressing ensembles. Empirical results across speech, language, vision, and graph tasks show that well-designed distillation can preserve most of a teacher's performance while reducing parameter count and inference cost; task-adaptive compression and careful design of teacher–student interactions (including training teachers to be student-friendly) further improve student effectiveness. Practical choices—what to distill (logits, features, or structure), how to align mismatched architectures, and how to augment data or leverage ensembles—determine final trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Frost
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable means to compress large models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of teacher performance. When matched to task constraints—choosing what teacher signals to transfer, how to align layers or features, and whether or how to handle missing or private training data—KD enables deployment of competitive models in latency- and resource-constrained settings. However, KD is not a plug-and-play cure: careful design (task-aware layer selection, many-to-many mapping for large pre-trained transformers, selective sample weighting, and data-free procedures when needed) is required to avoid propagating teacher errors, worsening robustness, or underfitting compact students. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the central compression engine for modern deep learning and NLP pipelines, but that success depends on matching KD mechanisms to application constraints and combining KD with complementary engineering (efficient distillation pipelines and synthetic-data or adversarial generators when data are unavailable).

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or multi-modal deep models into smaller, more deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or other structured knowledge. Work across vision, speech, and NLP shows a range of mechanisms (soft-label matching, internal-representation matching, layer mapping, and feature/attention guidance) and adaptations for limited or private data. Empirical results indicate distilled students can approach teacher accuracy while greatly reducing size and inference cost, but effectiveness depends on what knowledge is distilled, how it is represented, and the training regime.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Task-Aware Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best viewed not as a single algorithm but as a multifaceted, task-aware toolbox that enables practical model compression across modalities. When used thoughtfully—selecting what signals to transfer (logits, features, relations), aligning teacher and student architectures, choosing or synthesizing distillation data, and combining KD with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search)—KD produces compact students that often preserve most of a teacher’s performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Realizing these gains requires explicit attention to teacher imperfections, capacity gaps, domain or data mismatch, and deployment constraints; addressing those concerns with multi-teacher schedules, data-agnostic generators, curriculum/annealing strategies, and interpretable or task-adaptive student designs yields the most reliable outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.author: Beck
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful set of techniques for transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller student models so that compact models can retain much of the performance of their teachers. Across modalities and tasks, KD has evolved from simple soft-target (logit) matching to include feature- and layer-level supervision, online and multi-teacher schemes, meta-learned teachers, data-free and privacy-aware variants, and combinations with quantization and low-precision inference. Empirical work shows KD can substantially reduce model size and inference cost with modest performance loss, but success depends on careful choice of what to transfer, how to align teacher and student representations, and how to handle limited or mismatched data. Remaining practical issues include teacher–student heterogeneity, propagation of teacher errors, robustness to domain shifts, and limits to compression for some generative and structured prediction tasks.

papers_seen.author: Frost
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable means to compress large models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of teacher performance. When matched to task constraints—choosing what teacher signals to transfer, how to align layers or features, and whether or how to handle missing or private training data—KD enables deployment of competitive models in latency- and resource-constrained settings. However, KD is not a plug-and-play cure: careful design (task-aware layer selection, many-to-many mapping for large pre-trained transformers, selective sample weighting, and data-free procedures when needed) is required to avoid propagating teacher errors, worsening robustness, or underfitting compact students. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the central compression engine for modern deep learning and NLP pipelines, but that success depends on matching KD mechanisms to application constraints and combining KD with complementary engineering (efficient distillation pipelines and synthetic-data or adversarial generators when data are unavailable).

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Effective Practices and Practical Recommendations for Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression are practical, versatile tools for deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Across computer vision, multimodal, and natural language processing tasks, distillation can preserve or approximate teacher performance while substantially reducing model size and latency. Successful distillation strategies go beyond matching final logits: they exploit intermediate representations, task-aware selection of teacher signals, many-to-many layer mappings, and feature-level or adversarial training to transfer richer knowledge. Combining these approaches yields compact models that retain robustness and task performance, and that can be further complemented by pruning or hardware-aware compression for deployment.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, pragmatic technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. KD operates at multiple levels—soft outputs, intermediate representations, and structured relational signals—and is effective across modalities when paired with complementary compression methods, careful data strategies, and student-aware architecture design. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its success depends on aligning teacher and student capacity, selecting appropriate distillation targets, preparing or synthesizing suitable training data, and validating robustness and fairness. A production-ready compression pipeline treats KD as a system of interacting components (signal selection, data, initialization, and optimization) and couples distillation with architecture-aware transforms, pruning, or quantization to meet real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core and a Bounded Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and flexible approach for compressing large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with task-aware objectives, intermediate representation alignment, appropriate data strategies (including synthetic-data approaches), and architecture-aware design, KD yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance and enable deployment in resource-constrained or heterogeneous environments. However, KD has predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity, propagation of teacher errors, and optimization fragility—that demand complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful protocol design to realize reliable compression in practice.

papers_seen.author: Waller
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across computer vision, speech, multimodal, and NLP tasks, distillation protocols—ranging from soft-target (logit) matching to intermediate feature and attention-based transfers—enable practical trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and memory. Success depends on careful choices of distillation targets, teacher-student compatibility, data availability, and training dynamics; when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, low-precision, architecture search, or federated protocols) it yields deployable models for resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller students to enable deployment under computation, memory, latency, or privacy constraints. The field has evolved from simple logit matching to a spectrum of strategies that include representation- and attention-level matching, multi-teacher and teacher-adaptation schedules, data- and augmentation-aware objectives, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning, architecture search, or quantization. Practical success depends on what is distilled (soft targets, features, relational structure), how the teacher and student are matched (layer mapping, capacity-aware losses), and how input data or surrogates are chosen or synthesized. Key open problems remain: choosing or constructing “student-friendly” teachers, avoiding transfer of teacher errors and biases, handling limited or private data, and aligning compression choices with hardware constraints. Below I synthesize mechanisms, empirical patterns, and practitioner guidance grounded in recent literature.

papers_seen.author: Joyce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Settings, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable deployment of high-performing deep models in latency- or resource-constrained settings by transferring knowledge from larger “teacher” models or ensembles to smaller “student” models. Work in this area spans methods that match final outputs, intermediate representations, or relational structure; approaches that adapt teacher signals through meta-learning or task-aware filters; and specializations for settings such as vision–language, graph learning, federated or distributed training, and data-free scenarios. Empirical results show KD can yield large efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance, but practical success depends on handling domain shift, architectural mismatch, heterogeneous data and devices, and the quality or calibration of teacher outputs. Important theoretical and statistical analyses have begun to clarify when and why distillation helps, but open problems remain around robust, privacy-preserving, and architecture-agnostic distillation for production systems.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques enable deploying large deep models by transferring their predictive behavior or internal structure to smaller, faster models. Research has progressed from soft-label teacher-student training toward richer objectives that match internal representations, feature spaces, and decision boundaries; from data-dependent distillation to data-free and privacy-preserving approaches; and from one-size-fits-all compression to task-adaptive, architecture-aware methods. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance across speech, vision, and language tasks when distillation objectives, training data (real or synthetic), and search for efficient architectures are carefully tailored. Remaining challenges include optimization barriers that prevent perfect teacher matching, balancing regularization and fidelity, and handling heterogeneous or absent data during distillation.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Dixon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods compress large deep models into smaller, faster, or more private models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. The literature shows a spectrum of KD signals (soft logits, intermediate features, layer mappings), enhancements via data interventions and architecture search, and combinations with pruning or low-precision inference. Practical success depends on task- and deployment-aware choices (which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, what augmentations or synthetic data to use) as well as attention to privacy and robustness. The field has produced effective recipes for compressing pretrained language models, vision transformers, and generative models, while ongoing work clarifies limits and complementary techniques for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-level toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. Effective KD requires selecting what to transfer (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational signals), matching teacher and student capacities, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques. When applied with task-aware objectives, projector or alignment modules, and careful treatment of data and teacher preparation, KD yields compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints, though capacity mismatch and data limitations remain important caveats.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Practical Pathways for Compressing Large NLP Models: Pre-train the Student, Distill Carefully, and Guard for Data & Robustness
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and versatile approach to compress large deep learning models for NLP and related tasks. When the student model is itself pre-trained, distillation yields especially strong and consistent gains; complementary methods — including data augmentation during distillation, progressive module replacement, ensemble teachers or teacher adaptation, and data-free or privacy-aware distillation — address common deployment constraints such as limited task data, inference cost, data access, and adversarial robustness. Combining these techniques and choosing distillation targets and schedules with theoretical and empirical guidance yields compact models that retain much of the original performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Mccarthy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Flexible Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the primary, flexible strategy for compressing and adapting deep models for real-world deployment. When framed as a toolbox—combining soft-target supervision, intermediate-representation matching, teacher ensembles, data-aware synthesis, and architecture-aware compression—KD routinely yields compact students that retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Successful application requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to address robustness and rare-event behavior; when these are handled explicitly, KD enables reliable, deployable models across modalities and tasks.

papers_seen.author: Ball
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, efficient students by transferring learned behavior or representations. Across modalities and tasks, KD variants transfer logits, intermediate features, attention patterns, or relational information and are often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Practical success depends on what signals are transferred, student capacity and initialization, data strategies during distillation, and addressing robustness, privacy, and distributional mismatch. While distilled students frequently approach teacher performance, open problems remain in aligning heterogeneous architectures, preventing transfer of teacher errors or biases, and designing data-efficient or privacy-preserving distillation protocols.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques provide practical ways to transfer performance from large, expensive models to smaller, faster ones. The literature spans soft-label distillation from ensembles, feature- and representation-based matching, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, task-adaptive compression for large pretrained language models, and methods to transfer non-standard properties such as adversarial robustness. Empirical results demonstrate that properly designed distillation procedures can retain much of teacher performance across vision and language tasks, that internal-representation matching often improves downstream generalization beyond logits-only approaches, and that KD variants can be adapted to constraints such as limited (or private) data, distributed training, and resource- or latency-aware deployment. Open challenges include understanding which aspects of teacher knowledge are most useful for which student architectures and tasks, designing distillation under strict privacy or data-availability constraints, and transferring robustness properties reliably.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from matching teacher logits to a flexible toolkit for producing compact, efficient models suitable for deployment and adaptation in deep learning and NLP. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can transfer predictive behavior, intermediate representations, and task-specific properties (e.g., robustness or privacy signals), and it is most effective when combined with complementary strategies such as pre-training of compact architectures, data-side interventions, and low-precision or structured pruning. Success depends on careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous teacher and student architectures, how to construct or augment distillation data, and how to adapt teacher behavior; practical pipelines treat KD as one component of a broader compression workflow rather than a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Adaptive Tool for Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the original performance. KD's successes across vision, speech, and NLP show that careful choice of what to transfer (logits, intermediate features, attention), how to align teacher and student, and whether to rely on original data or generated/synthetic data determines outcomes. To be effective in real deployments, KD must be combined with complementary methods (data-free generation, federated protocols, targeted augmentation, and robustness-aware objectives) and applied adaptively to task and resource constraints. When used thoughtfully, KD enables substantial efficiency gains without wholesale architectural redesign; when used naively it can propagate teacher errors or exacerbate distributional and low-frequency lexical problems.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Methods, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring behavioral and representational signals from teachers. KD includes diverse techniques — soft-target supervision, intermediate feature and attention matching, layer-mapping strategies, online and ensemble-to-single transfers, and selective sample or data-aware procedures — that are adapted to task, architecture, and deployment constraints. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and appropriate data strategies, KD can yield compact models that retain most teacher performance; however, success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, and data availability.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Large scale distributed neural network training through online distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Techniques such as ensembling and distillation promise model quality improvements when paired with almost any base model. However, due to increased test-time cost (for ensembles) and increased complexity of the training pipeline (for distillation), these techniques are challenging to use in industrial settings. In this paper we explore a variant of distillation which is relatively straightforward to use as it does not require a complicated multi-stage setup or many new hyperparameters. Our first claim is that online distillation enables us to use extra parallelism to fit very large datasets about twice as fast. Crucially, we can still speed up training even after we have already reached the point at which additional parallelism provides no benefit for synchronous or asynchronous stochastic gradient descent. Two neural networks trained on disjoint subsets of the data can share knowledge by encouraging each model to agree with the predictions the other model would have made. These predictions can come from a stale version of the other model so they can be safely computed using weights that only rarely get transmitted. Our second claim is that online distillation is a cost-effective way to make the exact predictions of a model dramatically more reproducible. We support our claims using experiments on the Criteo Display Ad Challenge dataset, ImageNet, and the largest to-date dataset used for neural language modeling, containing $6\times 10^{11}$ tokens and based on the Common Crawl repository of web data.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression methods form a diverse toolkit for producing smaller, faster, or more deployable models while retaining much of the performance of larger teachers. Research spans soft-label and self-distillation strategies, layer- and representation-level transfers, architecture-aware and task-adaptive compression, and deployment-aware approaches that combine pruning, quantization, and distillation. Empirical work shows that careful choice of distillation signal (logits, intermediate representations, or feature maps), alignment strategy between teacher and student layers, data augmentation, and optimization scheduling materially affects student performance. Practical systems exploit these design choices to compress large pre-trained language models, accelerate inference, enable heterogeneous-device training, or improve low-precision networks. Despite progress, open questions remain about principled objective design, sample efficiency under limited data, and theory connecting transferred representations to generalization.
